chapters.title: Living Together
chapters.summary: In this chapter: village life and shared places; planning van mahotsav; helping hands in the community; the community bridge and working together.

lessons.title: Village Life and Shared Places

activities.prompt: What makes a village feel like everyone’s special place?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Life in Chandan's Village
activities.body: Chandan lives in a beautiful village with a large playground near his house. He plays kabaddi with his friends after school. The village has shared places where people play, relax and meet others. Working together in these places brings people closer.
keyPoints: Chandan lives in a village.
The village has shared places.
People play, relax and meet.
activities.explanation: Shared places help people play, meet and work together.

activities.prompt: Chandan finds litter near the large playground. What should he and his friends do?
steps: They clean near the playground because it is a public place used for playing.
They work together because people can clean and decorate shared places.
So, Chandan and his friends should clean it together, because working together in shared places brings people closer.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Caring for Shared Places
activities.body: Public places are for playing, relaxing and meeting others. People can work together to clean and decorate them. Roads connect different areas and make it easy to move goods and services. Sharing these places and working together brings people closer.
keyPoints: Public places support village life.
People can care for shared places.
Working together brings people closer.
activities.explanation: Working together in shared places brings people closer.

activities.title: Find the Playground
activities.prompt: Where is the large playground?
options: near Chandan's house
inside the shop
under the banyan tree
at the health centre
activities.explanation: The large playground is near Chandan's house.

activities.prompt: Chandan plays kabaddi with his friends after school.
activities.explanation: Chandan enjoys kabaddi with his friends after school.

activities.title: Join the Village
activities.prompt: Roads connect people who live in different ______.
activities.hint: Different parts of the village.
activities.explanation: Roads connect the different areas where people live.

activities.title: Places and Their Uses
activities.prompt: Match each place with what people do there.
activities.explanation: Each place helps people talk, buy needs, receive treatment, play or meet.

activities.title: The Benefit of Teamwork
activities.prompt: What benefit comes from working together in shared places?
options: They stop helping each other.
They bring people closer.
They keep their distance.
They forget shared places.
activities.explanation: People who work together in shared places bring each other closer.

activities.prompt: A public place can be used only for relaxing.
activities.explanation: Public places are also used for playing and meeting others.

activities.prompt: The road is blocked. Chandan’s friends visit the shopkeeper. What will happen?
options: Food and clothes will not reach the shop easily.
The shopkeeper will sell more goods to nearby children.
The road will connect more areas for the shopkeeper.
People will find the health centre more easily.

why.The shopkeeper will sell more goods to n: This mistake thinks a blocked road helps the shopkeeper sell more.
why.The road will connect more areas for the: This mistake thinks roads create new links when they are blocked.
why.People will find the health centre more: This mistake mixes up moving goods with getting medical care.

activities.explanation: This is right because roads make it easy to move goods and services.

activities.prompt: After school, Chandan wants to play kabaddi and meet his friends. Which place fits best?
options: The large playground near Chandan’s house is best.
The health centre for ill people is the best.
The shop for food and clothes is the best.
The banyan tree for village elders is best.

why.The health centre for ill people is the: This mistake chooses treatment when the children want to play.
why.The shop for food and clothes is the bes: This mistake chooses shopping when the children want recreation.
why.The banyan tree for village elders is be: This mistake chooses talking when the children want kabaddi.

activities.explanation: This is right because the playground is used for playing and meeting friends.

activities.prompt: Chandan wants to test if working together cleans better. Which test is fair?
options: Use equal litter in equal spaces for one cleaner and a group.
Give one cleaner more time than the whole group.
Let the group clean a much dirtier space than the cleaner.
Ask one cleaner to clean while nobody watches the group.

why.Give one cleaner more time than the whol: This mistake gives one method more time, so the test is unfair.
why.Let the group clean a much dirtier space: This mistake changes the starting mess and the space size.
why.Ask one cleaner to clean while nobody wa: This mistake does not check what each group really did.

activities.explanation: This is right because it keeps litter and space the same for both tests.

activities.prompt: Branches block the road to another area. What should villagers do first?
options: Clear the path so goods and services can move.
Use the health centre to move all goods.
Ask elders to stop talking under the tree.
Fill the path with more branches for play.

This mistake thinks a health centre moves goods instead of treating people.
why.Ask elders to stop talking under the tre: This mistake thinks closing roads helps people and goods move.
why.Fill the path with more branches for pla: This mistake thinks blocking paths is a good way to care for roads.

activities.explanation: This is right because roads make it easy to move goods and services.

lessons.title: Planning Van Mahotsav

activities.prompt: How can we make our park brighter and greener before the festival?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Getting Ready for Van Mahotsav
activities.body: Van Mahotsav is a festival in India. It is held during the rainy season, from 1 July to 7 July. Chandan and his friends are excited. They plan to clean the park and plant trees. They will also invite family members. A colourful poster can bring neighbourhood people. Their work can make the earth greener and give walkers better air.
keyPoints: Van Mahotsav is held from 1 July to 7 July.
The children will clean the park and plant trees.
A poster can invite people to the celebration.
activities.explanation: The children have exciting plans for the festival and its park.

activities.prompt: Van Mahotsav is coming soon. Why might the children’s park work help Mallika’s grandmother?
steps: They will clean the park because they planned it for the festival.
They will plant trees because planting protects the environment.
Mallika’s grandmother walks there daily, so trees can give her better air.
Thus, their work will make the park greener and the air better.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which two jobs will the children do in the park?
options: Clean it and plant trees
Clean it and make posters
Plant trees and clean posters
Invite neighbours and clean trees
activities.explanation: The children plan to clean the park and plant trees. Well done!

activities.prompt: Chandan and his school friends feel excited about Van Mahotsav.
activities.explanation: Chandan and his school friends were excited about the festival. You spotted the right feeling!

activities.prompt: Van Mahotsav is held from ______ to 7 July.
activities.hint: Think of the first day of the celebration.
activities.explanation: Van Mahotsav starts on 1 July and ends on 7 July. Great!

activities.prompt: Match each action with its result.
activities.explanation: You matched the children's actions with their helpful results. Good thinking!

activities.prompt: Why can a colourful poster be useful for Van Mahotsav?
options: Invite neighbours to the celebration
Give walkers cleaner air
Make the earth greener
Help children plant trees
activities.explanation: A colourful poster can invite neighbourhood people to the celebration. Exactly!

activities.prompt: Which statement correctly joins the celebration and the environment?
options: A poster invites people; trees make earth greener.
A daily walk invites people; trees clean the park.
Family members plant posters; walks make earth greener.
The rainy season plants trees; posters clean the park.
activities.explanation: The poster invites people, while trees make the earth greener. You linked both ideas!

activities.prompt: The children will clean the park and plant trees. What will their work do?
options: The park will become greener and help protect the environment.
The park will have less green space and weaker air.
The park will stay the same because planting changes nothing.
The park will need fewer trees and less fresh air.

why.The park will have less green space and: This mistake assumes that tree planting removes green space and air.
why.The park will stay the same because plan: This mistake assumes that cleaning and planting cannot change a park.
why.The park will need fewer trees and less: This mistake thinks a clean park needs fewer trees and less air.

activities.explanation: Right, because planting protects the environment and makes Earth greener.

activities.prompt: A colourful poster can invite neighbours. One poster is dull. Which should they use, and why?
options: Choose the dull one because dull colours attract more people.
Choose the colourful one because it can invite neighbours.
Choose the dull one because posters cannot invite people.
Choose the colourful one because it will plant more trees.

why.Choose the dull one because dull colours: This mistake believes dull colours attract more neighbours.
why.Choose the dull one because posters cann: This mistake believes posters cannot invite neighbourhood people.
why.Choose the colourful one because it will: This mistake believes a poster can grow trees by itself.

activities.explanation: This is right because a colourful poster can invite neighbours.

activities.prompt: Van Mahotsav is held from 1 July to 7 July. When should the children finish planning?
options: Start all planning after 7 July.
Plan only on the last festival day.
Wait until the next rainy season.
Finish all planning before 1 July.

This mistake waits until after the festival has ended.
This mistake leaves planning until the festival is almost over.
This mistake waits a whole season even though the festival is soon.

activities.explanation: This is right because the festival begins on 1 July.

activities.prompt: A colourful poster can invite neighbours. Which test can check this fairly?
options: Show the poster to everyone and guess what they will do.
Ask only children who read the poster if they will join.
Give two similar groups one poster or none, then compare.
Use two colourful posters and compare their picture sizes.

why.Show the poster to everyone and guess wh: This mistake guesses instead of comparing two groups.
why.Ask only children who read the poster if: This mistake asks only readers, so it ignores other neighbours.
why.Use two colourful posters and compare th: This mistake compares poster pictures instead of testing invitations.

activities.explanation: This is right because only the poster changes between similar groups.

activities.prompt: The children want family members and neighbourhood people at Van Mahotsav. Which plan includes both?
options: Tell only family members and put up no poster.
Tell family members and put up a colourful poster.
Invite only neighbours and tell no family members.
Keep family members and neighbours away from the event.

why.Tell only family members and put up no p: This mistake leaves neighbourhood people without a clear invitation.
why.Invite only neighbours and tell no famil: This mistake leaves family members without an invitation.
why.Keep family members and neighbours away: This mistake treats both groups as people to keep away.

activities.explanation: This is right because it invites family members and neighbourhood people.

lessons.title: Helping Hands in the Community

activities.prompt: What did the children and their neighbors do to get their park ready?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Many Hands Make a Happy Park
activities.body: Parents and villagers were happy to join the children. They met under the big banyan tree to plan the festival. The park needed repairs, and the parents chose to help. Sameer could repair benches, Babita offered to repair the street light, and Noor brought saplings. Working together would make the park ready quickly. After the work, it looked beautiful with new saplings and clean paths.
keyPoints: Parents and villagers joined the children.
Everyone helped with the park repairs.
The finished park had new saplings and clean paths.
activities.explanation: You can see how each helper made the park ready.

activities.prompt: The park needs repairs before a festival. How can everyone in the community help?
steps: The park needs repairs before the festival.
Parents and villagers help because they are happy to join the children.
Sameer fixes benches, Babita fixes the light, and Noor plants saplings.
Their shared work makes the park ready quickly and beautiful.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Happy Helpers
activities.prompt: The villagers were happy to join the children.
activities.explanation: Yes! Parents and other villagers were happy to help.

activities.title: The Meeting Place
activities.prompt: Where did the villagers meet to plan the festival?
options: Under the big banyan tree
Inside the plant nursery
Beside the street light
Along the park boundary
activities.explanation: The villagers gathered under the big banyan tree.

activities.title: Who Helped With What?
activities.prompt: Match each helper with their helpful task.
activities.explanation: Each person brought a skill, tools, or plants to help.

activities.title: The Park Needs Work
activities.prompt: What did the park need before the festival?
options: New street lights
More saplings
Another festival
Park repairs
activities.explanation: The park needed repairs before the festival.

activities.title: Noor's Contribution
activities.prompt: Noor brought ______ from her plant nursery.
activities.hint: Think about what she brought for planting.
activities.explanation: Noor brought saplings to plant along the park boundary.

activities.title: From Planning to a Beautiful Park
activities.prompt: Put these moments in the correct order.
items: Villagers planned under the banyan tree
The park looked beautiful after the work
activities.explanation: Planning and helping came before the completed repairs.

activities.title: Why Teamwork Helped
activities.prompt: Why would working together make the park ready quickly?
options: Because one person did every job.
Because everyone worked and helped one another.
Because some helpers stayed away.
Because the park had no repairs.
activities.explanation: Working together and helping one another made the work faster.

activities.title: Before and After
activities.prompt: The park looked the same before and after the work.
activities.explanation: After the work, the park looked beautiful with new saplings and clean paths.

activities.prompt: The park needs repairs before the festival. What should the group do next?
options: Work together to make the park ready.
Wait until the festival has started.
Let one person do all the work.
Keep the park just as it is.

This mistake thinks waiting helps, but repairs are needed first.
This mistake ignores that everyone worked together and helped one another.
This mistake forgets that the park needed repairs before the festival.

activities.explanation: This is right because working together makes the park ready quickly.

lessons.title: The Community Bridge and Working Together

activities.prompt: How can a community build something stronger together?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Building a Bridge Together
activities.body: The Chinar river in Kanker often overflows during the rainy season. Moving goods and vehicles then becomes difficult. Reaching schools and hospitals also becomes a major challenge. The whole community built a strong bridge together. They used bamboo, stones and other material. Now, students reach their schools more easily. Villagers can cross the river easily too.
keyPoints: The river often overflows during the rainy season.
The whole community built the bridge together.
Students and villagers can travel more easily.
activities.explanation: Working together helped the community overcome river difficulties.

activities.prompt: The Chinar often overflows. How can the community make school travel easier?
steps: Because the river often overflows, moving goods and vehicles becomes difficult.
Reaching schools and hospitals is hard, so the community builds a bridge.
The community builds together using bamboo, stones, and other material.
Students now reach school more easily, and villagers cross easily.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Communities That Work Together
activities.body: Schools and neighbourhoods depend on people working as a team. An ant colony is like a community where every ant has a special job. Some ants collect food, care for babies and protect their home. Bees also work as a community, with each member having special roles.
keyPoints: Schools and neighbourhoods depend on teamwork.
Every ant in a colony has a special job.
Bees work together with special roles.
activities.explanation: Communities succeed when their members work together.

activities.title: When the River Overflows
activities.prompt: Which task becomes difficult when the Chinar river overflows?
options: Caring for ant babies
Collecting food for ants
Protecting a bee home
Moving goods and vehicles
activities.explanation: Moving goods and vehicles becomes difficult when the river overflows.

activities.title: Bridge Materials
activities.prompt: The community used bamboo, ______ and other material to build the bridge.
activities.hint: Choose one of the other bridge materials.
activities.explanation: The community used bamboo, stones and other material for the bridge.

activities.title: The Bridge Helps
activities.prompt: Match each part of the story with its result.
pairs: Students reach their schools more easily
activities.explanation: The community bridge makes school travel and river crossing easier.

activities.title: Another Community
activities.prompt: Which group also works as a community with special roles?
options: A bee community
The Chinar river
The bridge materials
The rainy season
activities.explanation: Bees work as a community, with each member having special roles.

activities.title: The Bridge Story in Order
activities.prompt: Put these events in order.
activities.explanation: The overflow caused difficulties. The community built a bridge, and travel became easier.

activities.title: Connecting the Communities
activities.prompt: Why is the ant colony similar to the human community in this lesson?
options: One member does every job in both communities.
Special jobs replace teamwork in both communities.
Both show people or ants working together.
Both communities succeed without working together.
activities.explanation: The community built the bridge together. An ant colony also works together, with every ant having a special job.

activities.prompt: The Chinar overflows, making schools and hospitals hard to reach. What result shows that the community bridge helped?
options: Students reach schools more easily, and villagers cross easily.
The river overflows less often during the rainy season.
Villagers use fewer materials when crossing the river.
The community stops working together to build things.

why.The river overflows less often during th: This wrongly assumes the bridge made the river overflow less.
why.Villagers use fewer materials when cross: This confuses building materials with materials used while travelling.
why.The community stops working together to: This mistakes working together for giving up teamwork.

activities.explanation: Students and villagers can now travel more easily across the river.

activities.prompt: How can we fairly check that the bridge makes river crossing easier?
options: Compare crossing before and after the bridge.
Ask only people who watched the bridge being built.
Check crossing only when the river overflows.
Use another bridge and ignore this one.

why.Ask only people who watched the bridge b: This uses builders' opinions instead of comparing crossings.
why.Check crossing only when the river overf: This does not compare crossing before and after the bridge.
This ignores the bridge that needs to be tested.

activities.explanation: Comparing before and after shows whether crossing became easier.

activities.prompt: Ant colonies need food, care, and protection. How should the jobs be shared?
options: Each ant should do the job that fits its role.
Every ant should collect food and do nothing else.
One ant should do every job for the colony.
Some ants should stop caring for the babies.

why.Every ant should collect food and do not: This ignores that ants also care for babies and protect their home.
why.One ant should do every job for the colo: This forgets that a colony depends on different special jobs.
why.Some ants should stop caring for the bab: This wrongly treats caring for babies as an unimportant job.

activities.explanation: says every ant has a special job.

activities.prompt: Bees work as a community, with special roles. What classroom idea matches this?
options: Everyone can contribute a special part to shared work.
Everyone should do exactly the same part.
One student should do every job alone.
Only one kind of work really matters.

why.Everyone should do exactly the same part: This mistakes special roles for doing exactly the same job.
This believes one member can replace the whole community.
This forgets that different roles each help the community.

activities.explanation: Bees show that community members can have special roles.

lessons.title: A Shared Meal and Festival Celebrations

activities.prompt: How does a shared meal bring a community together and help it thrive?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Celebrating Together
activities.body: Villagers bring vegetables and cereals, then everyone sits together to eat. The feast celebrates everyone's hard work. Afterwards, banana leaves go into a pit and become manure for the soil. Magh Bihu begins on Uruka, 14 January. In Assam, people build Bhela Ghar. In Sikkim, communities harvest crops together. After the festival, everyone is tired but happy, and children care for the park.
keyPoints: The shared feast celebrates hard work.
Buried banana leaves improve soil as manure.
Magh Bihu begins on Uruka, 14 January.
activities.explanation: These details show how shared work, food and care bring a community together.

activities.prompt: Why are banana leaves put in a pit after the shared feast?
steps: After the feast, villagers put the banana leaves in a pit.
They bury the leaves so the leaves can become manure.
Manure improves the soil, so the leaves can still be useful.
Therefore, putting the leaves in a pit helps improve the soil.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What Did They Bring?
activities.prompt: What did the villagers bring for the meal?
options: vegetables and cereals
tools and seeds
jewellery and toys
wood and stone
activities.explanation: The villagers brought vegetables and cereals for their shared meal.

activities.title: Help for the Soil
activities.prompt: Leaves buried in a pit become ______ that improves the soil.
activities.hint: Something that helps soil grow better.
activities.explanation: Buried leaves become manure, which improves the soil.

activities.title: Festival Details
activities.prompt: Match each word with its correct detail.
pairs: the first day of Magh Bihu
people build a bamboo-and-hay hut called Bhela Ghar
community members come together to harvest crops
activities.explanation: Each detail is linked to the correct festival word or place.

activities.title: The Festival's End
activities.prompt: What happens at the end of Magh Bihu?
options: a feast
a hunt
a rest
a market
activities.explanation: The Magh Bihu celebration ends with a feast for everyone.

activities.title: The Shared Meal's Aftermath
activities.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: After the feast, banana leaves go into a pit.
Buried leaves become manure for the soil.
activities.explanation: The feast comes first, followed by the banana leaves and their benefit to the soil.

activities.title: After the Festival
activities.prompt: Which pair matches what happened after the festival?
options: Tired but happy; leave the park alone.
Happy but rested; take care of the park.
Tired but happy; take care of the park.
Tired but angry; take care of the park.
activities.explanation: Everyone was tired but happy, and the children chose to care for the park.

activities.prompt: After the feast, banana leaves were put in a pit. What will happen to the soil?
options: The soil will improve because the leaves become manure.
The soil will improve because the leaves become food.
The soil will worsen because the leaves become manure.
The soil will stay the same because the leaves disappear.

why.The soil will improve because the leaves: This confuses manure with food for people.
why.The soil will worsen because the leaves: This reverses the good effect that manure has on soil.
why.The soil will stay the same because the: This misses that buried leaves change into useful manure.

activities.explanation: This is right because buried leaves become manure that improves soil.

activities.prompt: Villagers brought vegetables and cereals for a community feast. Why did everyone eat together?
options: To celebrate everyone’s hard work with a shared meal.
To show that the villagers brought no food.
To decide who worked the hardest during the year.
To begin harvesting crops together in the fields.

why.To show that the villagers brought no fo: This wrongly assumes that bringing food means bringing none.
why.To decide who worked the hardest during: This turns a celebration of teamwork into a competition.
why.To begin harvesting crops together in th: This confuses the shared feast with the harvest in Sikkim.

activities.explanation: This is right because the feast celebrated everyone’s hard work.

activities.prompt: In Sikkim, community members come together to harvest crops. Who would be the best helper?
options: A Khetala, because they specialise in agriculture.
A person who only builds bamboo-and-hay huts.
A person who only prepares meals for festivals.
A person who has never worked with crops.

why.A person who only builds bamboo-and-hay: This confuses festival building with agricultural work.
why.A person who only prepares meals for fes: This confuses preparing food with working during the harvest.
why.A person who has never worked with crops: This ignores the special farming knowledge that Khetala have.

activities.explanation: This is right because Khetala specialise in agriculture.

activities.prompt: After the festival, children decided to take care of the park. What does this show?
options: They believe caring for a shared place matters.
They believe only adults should care for shared places.
They believe the park is useful only for eating.
They believe the park should not be cared for again.

why.They believe only adults should care for: This wrongly suggests that children should not help.
why.They believe the park is useful only for: This wrongly treats the park as only a place for meals.
why.They believe the park should not be care: This directly ignores the children’s decision to care for it.

activities.explanation: This is right because their choice shows responsibility for the park.

lessons.title: Our School, Our Team

activities.prompt: What makes our school team special, and how does everyone help?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Working Together at School
activities.body: School is a place where many people work together. A teacher helps students learn new things. Teachers, students, caretakers and bus drivers each have a role. An artefact is something people make using materials from nature. A leaf-plate can be useful, while a garland can be decorative. A locality means the place around your school. You can help it through cleaning, helping others or organising an event.
keyPoints: Many people have roles at school.
Artefacts can be made using materials from nature.
Locality activities can include cleaning, helping others or organising an event.
activities.explanation: Many people work together to make school and its locality better.

activities.prompt: How can our class work as a team to make artefacts and help our locality?
steps: First, the teacher helps students learn, so they know how to make artefacts.
Next, four or five students work together, because small groups can do school activities.
Then, they use materials from nature to make useful or decorative artefacts.
Finally, they clean, help others or organise an event, so our school team helps our locality.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: A teacher helps students learn new things.
activities.explanation: A teacher helps students learn new things.

activities.prompt: Which clue belongs to the bus riddle?
options: People use swings and slides
People wait to catch a ride
People shop and meet others
People send letters and parcels
activities.explanation: Waiting to catch a ride is the clue in the bus riddle.

activities.prompt: A leaf-plate and a garland are examples of ______.
activities.hint: They are things people make.
activities.explanation: Both a leaf-plate and a garland are artefacts.

activities.prompt: Match each school word with its clue.
pairs: can use groups of four or five
activities.explanation: Each clue matches one idea from our school team.

activities.prompt: Put these ideas in order from the starting material to the result.
activities.explanation: People can use materials from nature to make artefacts. A leaf-plate and a garland are examples.

activities.prompt: The bus riddle mentions letters, stamps and parcels.
activities.explanation: Letters, stamps and parcels appear in the post-office riddle. The bus riddle describes people waiting for a ride.

activities.prompt: Which plan matches a small-group school activity of four or five students?
options: Four or five students work together.
One student works alone.
Students work in a large group.
Students work in a very large group.

This misses the small-group idea by using one student.
This is too large for the stated small-group activity.
This is too large for the stated small-group activity.

activities.explanation: This matches the stated small-group size.

activities.prompt: Students use leaves for a leaf-plate and garland. What do these show?
options: Useful and decorative artefacts from nature.

activities.context: After school, Chandan and his friends play kabaddi on the large playground near his house. Later, he sees the village elders sitting under a banyan tree and talking together. The shopkeeper provides food, clothes and other daily needs, while roads help people and goods reach different areas. If a shared place becomes untidy, people can work together to clean and decorate it.
activities.prompt: In the case, why would it help to work together to clean the playground after playing kabaddi?
options: It would improve the shared space and strengthen teamwork among the people who use it.
It would help the shopkeeper decide which food and clothes people need.
It would make the roads connect fewer areas of the village.
It would cause the health centre to stop treating people who are ill.

why.It would help the shopkeeper decide whic: The shopkeeper's work is selling food, clothes and daily needs.
why.It would make the roads connect fewer ar: Cleaning the playground does not change the roads.
why.It would cause the health centre to stop: The health centre is for treatment, not for cleaning or play.

activities.explanation: Cleaning and decorating improve a shared place.

activities.context: After school, Chandan and his friends play kabaddi on the large playground near his house. Later, he sees the village elders sitting under a banyan tree and talking together. The shopkeeper provides food, clothes and other daily needs, while roads help people and goods reach different areas. If a shared place becomes untidy, people can work together to clean and decorate it.
activities.prompt: Why is the banyan tree area useful even though the people there are not playing?
options: It gives people a place to relax and talk with one another.
It helps the shopkeeper sell food and clothes there.
It allows goods and services to move along the roads.
It provides treatment to people who are ill.

why.It helps the shopkeeper sell food and cl: Selling daily needs is the shopkeeper's work.
why.It allows goods and services to move alo: Moving goods and services is the purpose of roads.
why.It provides treatment to people who are: Providing treatment is the health centre's work.

activities.explanation: Public places can be used for relaxing and meeting others.

activities.prompt: How do roads and the health centre support village life?
activities.answer: Roads connect different areas and make it easier to move goods and services. The health centre provides treatment when people are ill. Together, these shared services help people reach what they need and get care when they are unwell.
points: Roads connect different areas.
Roads help move goods and services.
The health centre treats ill people.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Chandan and his friends were excited because Van Mahotsav was going to be held soon in India during the rainy season from 1 July to 7 July. They planned to clean the park and plant trees, and they wanted to invite their family members too. Mallika’s grandmother walked in the park every day. The children believed a clean park with trees would give walkers better air to breathe. They also planned a colourful poster to invite neighbourhood people.
activities.prompt: If the children cleaned the park but did not plant any trees, what would happen to their plans for the park and the people who walk there?
options: The park would not become greener, and walkers might not get the better air that trees can provide.
The park would become greener because cleaning the park is the same as planting trees.
The park would give walkers better air because a colourful poster replaces trees.
The park would become greener because the festival is held during the rainy season.

why.The park would become greener because cl: Cleaning and planting trees are different actions.
why.The park would give walkers better air b: A poster invites people; it does not replace trees.
why.The park would become greener because th: The rainy season does not itself make the park greener.

activities.explanation: This follows the connection between planting trees, greener surroundings, and better air.

activities.context: Chandan and his friends were excited because Van Mahotsav was going to be held soon in India during the rainy season from 1 July to 7 July. They planned to clean the park and plant trees, and they wanted to invite their family members too. Mallika’s grandmother walked in the park every day. The children believed a clean park with trees would give walkers better air to breathe. They also planned a colourful poster to invite neighbourhood people.
activities.prompt: Suppose Mallika’s grandmother could no longer walk in the park every day. What should the children still do before Van Mahotsav?
options: They should still clean the park and plant trees.
They should stop cleaning the park because nobody walks there now.
They should remove the poster because neighbourhood people will not come.
They should plant trees only after Van Mahotsav is over.

why.They should stop cleaning the park becau: One person not walking there would not cancel the children’s plans.
why.They should remove the poster because ne: The poster could still invite neighbourhood people.
why.They should plant trees only after Van M: Planting trees before the festival follows the children’s plan.

activities.explanation: The children had already planned these activities for the festival.

activities.prompt: How can cleaning the park and planting trees help people who walk there?
activities.answer: Cleaning the park and planting trees can make the earth greener and give walkers better air to breathe. The children’s plans therefore help the people who use the park. Planting trees also protects the environment, so their work supports both the festival and the surroundings around the park.
points: Cleaning helps keep the park clean.
Planting trees makes the earth greener.
Trees can give walkers better air.
Planting trees protects the environment.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Before the festival, the village park needed repairs. Sameer had wood and nails, so he could repair the benches. Babita offered to fix the street light near the park, while Noor brought saplings from her plant nursery to plant along the park boundary. Parents and other villagers gathered under the big banyan tree to plan the festival and decided to help. When everyone worked together, the park became ready quickly and looked beautiful with new saplings and clean paths.
activities.prompt: Why was the park able to become ready quickly for the festival?
options: People shared different jobs and helped one another.
One person was left to complete every repair alone.
The parents watched while the others did all the work.
The festival began before any repair work was done.

why.One person was left to complete every re: Sharing all the work with one person would slow it down.
why.The parents watched while the others did: The parents decided to help rather than only watch.
why.The festival began before any repair wor: Planning the festival did not complete the repairs.

activities.explanation: Working together made the park ready quickly.

activities.prompt: Explain why working together helped the community prepare the park for the festival.

Identifies Babita’s street-light repair.
Identifies Noor’s work with saplings.
Explains that shared work made the park ready quickly.

activities.context: Uruka was the first day of Magh Bihu on 14 January. In Assam, people built a bamboo-and-hay hut called Bhela Ghar. The villagers brought vegetables and cereals, and everyone sat together for the community feast, which celebrated everyone’s hard work. After the feast, the banana leaves were put in a pit, where they could become manure and improve the soil. The children then chose to look after the park. After the festival, everyone felt tired but happy.
activities.prompt: After the feast, what should the villagers do with the banana leaves?
options: They should place them in the pit, allowing them to turn into manure.
They should keep them inside the Bhela Ghar.
They should give them to the Khetala.
They should leave them in the park instead.

why.They should keep them inside the Bhela G: Bhela Ghar is a bamboo-and-hay hut, not a place for the leaves.
Khetala specialise in agriculture, but the case gives them no role in handling the leaves.
why.They should leave them in the park inste: The children are caring for the park, while the banana leaves belong in the pit.

activities.explanation: Putting the leaves in a pit allows them to become manure that improves the soil.

Sit together for another shared meal.
Join the community harvest in Sikkim.

Another shared meal is part of the festival, not the children’s park plan.
Crop harvesting in Sikkim is a community activity, not park care.
Building a Bhela Ghar is an Assamese custom on Uruka, not park care.

activities.explanation: This action follows the children’s decision to care for the park.

activities.prompt: Explain how the community feast and the banana leaves are connected.
activities.answer: The community feast celebrated everyone’s hard work, and the villagers shared the meal together. After the feast, the banana leaves were put in a pit. Leaves buried in a pit become manure, and this manure improves the soil, connecting the shared meal with care for the land.
points: The feast celebrated everyone’s hard work.
Everyone sat together to share the meal.
The banana leaves were put in a pit after the feast.
The resulting manure improves the soil.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

The bus waiting place

chapters.summary: In this chapter: our journey and the post office; how people communicate; fast travel and environmental balance; the hospital and eye care.

lessons.title: Our Journey and the Post Office

activities.prompt: How does a letter travel from a postbox to the post office?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Our School Journey
activities.body: When the school bell rang, the classes finished. The students excitedly talked about wonderful books shown by their teachers in the library. School buses and e-rickshaws waited at the gate. Navya and her grandfather walked to a bus stop. Everyone got aboard the bus one by one. Navya saw a red postbox. A postman took letters to the post office, where letters were sorted by region.
keyPoints: Classes finished when the school bell rang.
Teachers showed wonderful books in the library.
Navya saw a red postbox during her bus journey.
Post offices sort letters by region.
activities.explanation: This links Navya's school journey with the work of a post office.

activities.prompt: How do letters reach groups for their regions?
steps: Dada ji puts letters in a postbox, so their journey starts there.
A postman takes them to the post office, because sorting happens there.
It sorts letters by region, so each region gets a separate group.
So letters move from postbox to post office, then into regional groups.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: When the Bell Rang
activities.prompt: What happened when the school bell rang?
options: The classes finished.
The books arrived.
The bus doors opened.
The letters were sorted.
activities.explanation: The classes ended when the school bell rang.

activities.title: Exciting Book Talk
activities.prompt: The students talked excitedly about wonderful books.
activities.explanation: The students chatted excitedly about the wonderful books.

activities.title: The Teachers' Books
activities.prompt: The teachers showed the books to the students in the ______.
activities.hint: This is where the teachers showed the books.
activities.explanation: The teachers had shown the books in the library.

activities.title: Waiting at the Stop
activities.prompt: What were some people at the bus stop doing?
options: They were reading books.
They were showing books.
They were waiting there.
They were sorting letters.
activities.explanation: Some people were waiting at the bus stop.

activities.title: Match Places and Events
activities.prompt: Match each place with what happened there.
activities.explanation: Each place had its own special event during the journey.

activities.title: The Postman's Route
activities.prompt: The postman took letters from the post office to the postbox.
activities.explanation: The postman took letters from the postbox to the post office.

activities.title: Sorting the Letters
activities.prompt: What did the post office do with the letters?
options: Showed them to the students.
Dropped them into a postbox.
Carried them into the library.
Sorted them by their regions.
activities.explanation: The post office sorted letters according to their regions.

activities.title: The Letter Journey
activities.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: Dada ji dropped letters into a postbox.
A postman took letters to the post office.
The post office sorted letters by their regions.
activities.explanation: Letters were dropped off, collected and then sorted by region.

activities.prompt: Classes finish when the school bell rings. Why does the school journey begin then?
options: The classes finish, and transport is waiting at the gate.
The students enter the library and talk about more books.
The postman puts letters into a postbox near the gate.
The teacher keeps reading until the buses leave.

why.The students enter the library and talk: This mistakes a library activity for the start of the journey.
why.The postman puts letters into a postbox: This mixes the postman's job with the school trip.
why.The teacher keeps reading until the buse: This forgets that the bell ends the classes.

activities.explanation: The bell ends classes, and transport waits at the gate.

activities.prompt: Navya watches the road from a window seat. Which detail connects her ride to Dada ji's memory?
options: The red postbox, where Dada ji used to drop letters.
The school gate, where Dada ji used to finish classes.
The library, where Dada ji used to show books.
The bus window, where Dada ji used to sort letters.

why.The school gate, where Dada ji used to f: This gives Dada ji a school role that is not stated.
why.The library, where Dada ji used to show: This gives Dada ji a teacher's role that is not stated.
why.The bus window, where Dada ji used to so: This makes the window a place for sorting letters.

activities.explanation: Dada ji used to drop letters into that red postbox.

lessons.title: How People Communicate

activities.prompt: How did people share news before mobile phones and computers?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Ways We Share Information
activities.body: Long ago, people communicated with drumbeats and carvings on rocks. Later, messengers and pigeons carried letters between people. The postal service began much later. It sent letters, parcels and important documents. The telephone, radio and television made sharing information easier. Today, mobile phones and computers use the internet. This helps people connect with anyone, anywhere, in seconds.
keyPoints: Early methods included drumbeats and rock carvings.
Postal service sent letters, parcels and important documents.
Phones and computers use the internet for quick connections.
activities.explanation: Communication tools have changed, but each helped people share information.

activities.prompt: Dada ji has important news for his brother. What should he use when the news cannot wait?
steps: He needs quick news because a letter reply could take several weeks.
A mobile phone or computer uses the internet, so it can connect quickly.
The internet reaches anyone and anywhere in seconds, so it fits urgent news.
Therefore, he should use a mobile phone or computer for urgent news.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which method did people use first to communicate?
options: mobile phones and computers
letters and parcels
drumbeats and rock carvings
messengers and pigeons
activities.explanation: People used drumbeats and carvings on rocks before the other methods.

activities.prompt: The postal service began much later than messengers and pigeons.
activities.explanation: Messengers and pigeons came later, and the postal service began much later.

activities.prompt: Match each way of communicating with its use.
activities.explanation: Each method helped people share information in its own way.

activities.prompt: Put these communication methods in the correct time order.
items: Mobile phones and computers using the internet
activities.explanation: The methods developed from early signals to letters and internet communication.

activities.prompt: How long could a reply to Dada ji's letter sometimes take?
options: within seconds
much later
several weeks
very quickly
activities.explanation: A letter reply could sometimes take several weeks to arrive.

activities.prompt: Which choice matches information given in the lesson?
options: Dada ji received letters after a long wait.
Pigeons carried internet messages.
Rock carvings sent important documents.
Postal service began with early drumbeats.
activities.explanation: A letter reply could sometimes take several weeks to reach Dada ji.

activities.prompt: A child is far from a parent and needs to share important news quickly. Which choice can help in seconds?
options: Use a mobile phone through the internet.
Use a telephone, radio or television.
Send a letter with a postal parcel.
Make drumbeats or rock carvings.

This mixes different tools because seconds-long connections come from the internet.
This misunderstands time because postal letters can take weeks.
This mixes old methods with internet-speed connections.

activities.explanation: This is right because the internet can connect people in seconds.

activities.prompt: Dada ji sends the same news by email and by handwritten letter. Which reply should arrive first, and why?
options: The email, because email made communication faster.
The letter, because postal letters always move faster.
The email, because email needs several weeks.
The letter, because drumbeats travel farther.

why.The letter, because postal letters alway: This wrongly thinks postal letters move faster than email.
why.The email, because email needs several w: This swaps the speeds because email does not need weeks.
why.The letter, because drumbeats travel far: This wrongly treats drumbeats as faster than email.

activities.explanation: This is right because email made communication much faster.

activities.prompt: Dada ji wants to know whether email or handwritten letters reach his brother faster. Which test is fairest?
options: Send equal messages both ways and compare their times.
Send one email and many handwritten letters.
Choose the method that looks more modern.
Compare messages sent to different people.

why.Send one email and many handwritten lett: This is unfair because the two methods get different numbers of messages.
why.Choose the method that looks more modern: This chooses looks instead of checking how fast each method is.
why.Compare messages sent to different peopl: This changes the messages and people, so it does not test speed alone.

activities.explanation: This is fair because both methods get equal messages and their times are compared.

activities.prompt: Someone says people used postal services before drumbeats and carvings. Why is this claim wrong?
options: Drumbeats and carvings came before postal service.
Postal service came before every early message.
Pigeons carried letters before people made carvings.
Mobile phones began before postal services.

why.Postal service came before every early m: This reverses the order because postal service began much later.
why.Pigeons carried letters before people ma: This reverses the order because pigeons came after drumbeats and carvings.
why.Mobile phones began before postal servic: This reverses the order because mobile phones came much later.

activities.explanation: This is right because drumbeats and carvings came much earlier than postal service.

activities.prompt: Someone says all communication now happens in seconds. Which fact shows this claim is too broad?
options: Dada ji's letter reply could take several weeks.
Mobile phones send messages through the internet.
Radio and television made sharing information easier.
The internet connects people anywhere in seconds.

why.Mobile phones send messages through the: This supports faster communication but does not show that all communication is instant.
why.Radio and television made sharing inform: This supports easier sharing but does not show that all communication is instant.
why.The internet connects people anywhere in: This supports internet speed but does not include slower letter replies.

activities.explanation: This is right because it shows that some letter replies still take weeks.

activities.prompt: Email and video calls can be much faster, but Dada ji still enjoys handwritten letters. What does this show?
options: Fast and slow communication can both suit him.
He only wants slow handwritten letters.
He has stopped writing letters completely.
He thinks email is always better.

This wrongly assumes that he likes only slow letters.
why.He has stopped writing letters completel: This wrongly assumes that faster tools stopped him writing letters.
This wrongly assumes that he dislikes email because he enjoys letters.

activities.explanation: This is right because faster tools do not remove his enjoyment of handwritten letters.

lessons.title: Fast Travel and Environmental Balance

activities.prompt: How can we travel faster while keeping nature safe?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Fast Travel and Nature
activities.body: Fast travel helps people move quickly. Metro trains travel very quickly. Flyovers are high roads. They help vehicles cross busy roads and crossings. Some carry metro trains. Others carry buses and cars. Flyovers save travelling time, so modern facilities make life easier. But many animals, birds and trees that once lived there are now gone. Navya asks if developments can keep the environment safe and secure. Planting trees can help.
keyPoints: Flyovers help vehicles cross busy roads and save time.
Changes can cause animals, birds and trees to disappear.
Planting trees can help keep the environment secure.
activities.explanation: Fast travel helps us, but caring for nature matters too.

activities.prompt: Navya's bus takes a turn. She then sees a fast-moving metro train. How can development help while the environment stays secure?
steps: Some flyovers carry metro trains, which travel very quickly.
Flyovers help vehicles cross busy roads, so they save travelling time.
Many animals, birds and trees are gone, and changes are one reason.
So fast travel helps, and tree planting can help secure the environment.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Navya's Sighting
activities.prompt: What did Navya see after the bus took a turn?
options: A fast-moving metro train
A slow-moving metro train
A high road flyover
A tree near the road
activities.explanation: Navya saw the fast-moving metro train after the bus took a turn.

activities.title: High Roads
activities.prompt: Flyovers are high roads. They help vehicles move above ______ roads.
activities.hint: Think about roads with many vehicles.
activities.explanation: Flyovers help vehicles move above busy roads.

activities.title: Match the Facts
activities.prompt: Match each beginning with its ending.
activities.explanation: Flyovers help with busy roads and travelling time. Trees help secure the environment.

activities.title: Why Are Living Things Gone?
activities.prompt: What is one reason that many animals, birds and trees are now gone?
options: Changes to the area
More metro journeys
Longer bus journeys
Busy road crossings
activities.explanation: These changes are one reason for the disappearance of animals, birds and trees.

activities.title: A Change Over Time
activities.prompt: Put these events in order from earliest to latest.
items: Animals, birds and trees lived there
Many animals, birds and trees were gone
activities.explanation: The living things once lived there. Changes helped cause their disappearance.

activities.title: Care for the Environment
activities.prompt: What can help keep the environment safe and secure?
options: Planting trees
Building longer flyovers
Using more metro trains
Making more road crossings
activities.explanation: Planting trees can help keep the environment secure.

activities.prompt: A crossing is busy. What happens if a bus uses a flyover?
options: The bus can cross sooner because the flyover saves time.
The bus must wait below because the flyover saves time.
The bus can cross later because the flyover saves time.
The bus must turn back because the flyover saves time.

why.The bus must wait below because the flyo: This wrongly says the flyover keeps the bus below the crossing.
why.The bus can cross later because the flyo: Saving travelling time supports sooner travel, not later travel.
why.The bus must turn back because the flyov: Nothing in the facts says a flyover makes the bus turn back.

activities.explanation: The flyover helps the bus cross and saves travelling time.

activities.prompt: How can we test if a flyover helps vehicles cross busy roads?
options: Compare travel time on one busy road before and after a flyover.
Compare travel time on one busy road and one quiet road.
Compare tree counts on roads with and without flyovers.
Compare bus colours on roads with and without flyovers.

why.Compare travel time on one busy road and: Different busy and quiet roads do not test the flyover fairly.
why.Compare tree counts on roads with and wi: Tree counts do not show whether vehicles can cross busy roads.
why.Compare bus colours on roads with and wi: Bus colours do not show whether vehicles can cross busy roads.

activities.explanation: Using the same busy road makes the flyover the main change.

activities.prompt: A child says, “Flyovers make life easier, so trees do not matter.” What is missing?
options: The effects on animals, birds and trees are ignored.
The speed of metro trains on trips is ignored.
The shape of the new flyover is ignored.
The position of nearby bus stops is ignored.

why.The speed of metro trains on trips is ig: It only checks speed, which does not show environmental harm.
It only checks shape, which does not show environmental harm.
why.The position of nearby bus stops is igno: It only checks bus stops, which does not show environmental harm.

activities.explanation: This misses changes linked to the loss of animals, birds and trees.

activities.prompt: What should people ask before building a flyover near trees and animals?
options: Can the environment stay safe and secure?
Can metro trains travel more slowly?
Can the flyover use a bright colour?
Can the trees grow on the road?

why.Can metro trains travel more slowly?: Slower trains do not answer whether the environment can stay safe.
why.Can the flyover use a bright colour?: A colour choice does not answer the environmental safety question.
why.Can the trees grow on the road?: Trees growing on a road does not answer the environmental safety question.

activities.explanation: This is the safety question Navya wondered about after changes.

activities.prompt: After road changes, what can help secure the area?
options: Plant trees around the area that changed.
Remove trees around the area that changed.
Build more roads around the area that changed.
Make people cross the area that changed.

why.Remove trees around the area that change: Removing trees does not follow the tree-planting fact.
why.Build more roads around the area that ch: More roads do not show how to secure the environment.
Crossing more often does not show how to secure the environment.

activities.explanation: Planting trees can help keep the environment secure.

activities.prompt: Another flyover has no metro. Who may use it?
options: Buses and cars may use this flyover.
Only metro trains may use this flyover.
Animals and birds may use this flyover.
Trees and buses may use this flyover.

Metro trains use some flyovers, not necessarily every flyover.
Animals and birds do not use flyovers as vehicles do.
Trees do not use flyovers as vehicles do.

activities.explanation: Other flyovers are used by buses and cars.

lessons.title: The Hospital and Eye Care

activities.prompt: What might we learn during a visit to the hospital?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Hospital in the Community
activities.body: Hospitals are places where people go when they are unwell. The hospital near the bus stop had many visitors. A banner outside announced an eye check-up camp. Dada ji brought Navya’s grandmother for an eye operation. The doctors helped her see better and greatly improved her life. The hospital was an important part of their community.
keyPoints: People visit hospitals when they are unwell.
An eye check-up camp was announced outside the hospital.
Doctors helped Navya’s grandmother see better.
activities.explanation: This lesson connects hospitals, eye care and community life.

activities.prompt: How can the hospital help Navya’s grandmother and their community?
steps: Dada ji brought Navya’s grandmother because she needed an eye operation.
The doctors helped her see better, so her life improved greatly.
Many people visited the hospital, so it served its community.
It was important because it improved life and served its community.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Bus Stop
activities.prompt: Where was the bus stop that some passengers used?
options: Close to a hospital
Close to a hotel
Close to an office
Close to a station
activities.explanation: The lesson says the bus stop was close to a hospital.

activities.title: Why Dada ji Came
activities.prompt: Dada ji brought Navya’s grandmother for an eye ______.
activities.hint: This word names a medical treatment.
activities.explanation: Dada ji brought Navya’s grandmother for an eye operation.

activities.title: The Hospital’s Camp
activities.prompt: What was the hospital organising?
options: A sports coaching camp
An eye check-up camp
A reading workshop
A music lesson
activities.explanation: The hospital was organising an eye check-up camp.

activities.title: Match the Hospital Clues
activities.prompt: Match each clue to its answer.
pairs: Place for people who feel unwell
activities.explanation: Each pair joins a clue from the hospital story with its answer.

activities.title: Navya’s Grandmother’s Story
activities.prompt: Put the events in Navya’s grandmother’s story in order.
items: Dada ji brought her for an eye operation
activities.explanation: The operation came first. Then her sight improved, and her life improved too.

activities.title: The Camp Announcement
activities.prompt: What announced the hospital’s eye check-up camp?
options: An announcement on the bus
A sign inside a shop
A note from a passenger
A banner outside the hospital
activities.explanation: The banner outside the hospital announced the eye check-up camp.

activities.prompt: The hospital organises an eye check-up camp. Many people are visiting the hospital. Why might they be there?
options: They may want their eyes checked at the camp.
They may be waiting for the next bus.
They may be buying bus tickets near the stop.
They may be looking for somewhere to eat.

This choice ignores the camp and focuses on bus travel.
why.They may be buying bus tickets near the: This choice focuses on bus tickets, but the banner offers eye care.
why.They may be looking for somewhere to eat: This choice focuses on food, but the banner offers eye care.

activities.explanation: The camp checks eyes, so visitors may want an eye check-up.

activities.prompt: People visit this hospital when they are unwell. Some visit for eye operations. Why is the claim ‘only for eye operations’ too narrow?
options: People also go there when they are unwell.
Many people visited the hospital that day.
The bus stop was close to the hospital.
Navya’s grandmother saw better after her operation.

why.Many people visited the hospital that da: Many visitors show hospital use, but not its wider purpose.
A close bus stop shows location, not the kinds of care.
why.Navya’s grandmother saw better after her: One improved eye operation does not show every hospital purpose.

activities.explanation: Going when unwell shows the hospital serves more than eye operations.

activities.prompt: Many people visit this hospital, and it greatly improved Navya’s grandmother’s life. What evidence best tests its community importance?
options: Who visits the hospital and how it helps their lives.
How many buses stop near the hospital each day.
Where the eye check-up banner is placed outside.
When one grandmother came for an eye operation.

why.How many buses stop near the hospital ea: Bus numbers do not show how the hospital helps its community.
why.Where the eye check-up banner is placed: Banner position does not show how the hospital helps its community.
why.When one grandmother came for an eye ope: One visit alone cannot show the hospital’s community importance.

activities.explanation: Many people visit, and the hospital helped one life greatly.

activities.prompt: The hospital’s eye check-up camp ends. People still visit when unwell. What should remain true?
options: The hospital will remain important to its community.
The hospital will stop helping people who are unwell.
The hospital will close after the camp ends.
The bus stop will move farther from the hospital.

why.The hospital will stop helping people wh: Ending the camp does not mean the hospital stops helping unwell people.
why.The hospital will close after the camp e: Ending one camp does not mean the whole hospital must close.
why.The bus stop will move farther from the: Ending a camp does not change where the bus stop is placed.

activities.explanation: The hospital serves people when unwell and remains important to the community.

lessons.title: Banking, Savings and Money

activities.prompt: How did families send money to loved ones long ago?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How Money and Banks Help Us
activities.body: A bank is a special place where money stays safe. Banks help people save for future needs. An ATM means Automated Teller Machine. It helps people take out money whenever they need it. Long ago, people used barter to exchange goods and services. Money was invented to make exchanges simpler. Money Orders were used to send money through the post office. Now mobile phones can send money online within seconds.
keyPoints: Banks keep money safe and help people save.
ATMs and mobile phones help people send or take out money.
Money made barter exchanges simpler.
activities.explanation: These ideas show how money, banks, and ways of paying have changed.

activities.prompt: A family has extra money for future needs and wants to keep it safe. Where should the family save it, and why?
steps: The family should use a bank because it is a special place where money is kept safe.
Keeping the money there protects it while it waits for future needs.
A bank also helps the family save money for those future needs.
So a bank meets both the family's safety and saving needs.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What Does an ATM Do?
activities.prompt: Which action does an ATM help people do?
options: Take out money
Keep money safe
Send money online
Save money
activities.explanation: An ATM helps people take out money whenever they need it.

activities.prompt: A bank is a special place where money is kept safe.
activities.explanation: Yes. A bank is a special place where money is kept safe.

activities.title: Match Each Thing with Its Description
activities.prompt: Match each thing with the correct description.
activities.explanation: Each pair shows a service, place, method, or exchange from the lesson.

activities.title: An Old Way of Exchanging
activities.prompt: Long ago, people used ______ to exchange goods and services.
activities.hint: This was an exchange of goods and services.
activities.explanation: Barter was used before money made exchanges simpler.

activities.title: Dada Ji and ATMs
activities.prompt: Dada ji had an ATM when he was Navya’s age.
activities.explanation: Dada ji did not have an ATM then. He had to visit a bank and wait in long queues.

activities.title: Why Was Money Invented?
activities.prompt: Why was money invented?
options: To make food and gifts
To make exchanges simpler
To keep banks open
To send money by post
activities.explanation: Money was invented to make exchanges simpler. Barter exchanged goods and services instead.

activities.title: Sending Money for Gifts
activities.prompt: Mama sent money for Raksha Bandhan gifts. Which method can send money online now?
options: Using a Money Order
Exchanging wheat for milk
Waiting in a bank queue
Using a mobile phone
activities.explanation: Mobile phones can send money online within seconds. Mama sent money for the gifts.

activities.prompt: An ATM means Automated Teller Machine. It helps people take out money whenever they need it. A child needs cash for a shop. What can the child do?
options: The child can take out money at the ATM.
The child can only save money at the ATM.
The child must wait in a long queue.
The child must exchange wheat for money.

why.The child can only save money at the ATM: The child is confusing saving money with taking money out.
The child is mixing up an ATM with an old bank visit.
The child is confusing an ATM with barter.

activities.explanation: An ATM helps people take out money whenever they need it.

activities.prompt: Dada ji did not have an ATM when he was Navya's age. Mobile phones can now send money online within seconds. What can people do today that Dada ji could not do then?
options: People can send money online within seconds.
People can keep money safe without any bank.
People can exchange wheat directly for milk.
People can take out money from any ATM.

why.People can keep money safe without any b: This confuses sending money online with keeping money safe.
why.People can exchange wheat directly for m: This describes old barter instead of today's new mobile service.
Dada ji did not have an ATM then, so this is not the change.

activities.explanation: Mobile phones now send money online within seconds.

lessons.title: Looking Around the Neighbourhood

activities.prompt: How can we explore the places and directions around our neighbourhood?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Places and Directions
activities.body: Public places give services for health, safety, cleanliness and the environment. Hospitals, banks, post offices and police stations are public places. Public libraries and bus stations are also public places. Parks, shops, hospitals and bus stops can be useful landmarks. Landmarks help people recognise a place easily. North is up, south is down, and west is on the left of a map. The rising sun helped Navya know east.
keyPoints: Public places provide services for the community.
Landmarks help people recognise places easily.
Maps help us understand directions.
activities.explanation: Now you can find public places and read directions on a map.

activities.prompt: Navya is marking places in her neighbourhood. She chooses a hospital, park, and bus station. Why do these choices work on her map?
steps: Hospitals and bus stations are public places.
Public places provide services connected with health, safety, cleanliness, and the environment.
Parks and hospitals can be useful landmarks.
So her map shows both public services and places that are easy to recognise.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Public libraries and bus stations are public places.
activities.explanation: Yes! The lesson says libraries and bus stations are public places.

activities.prompt: The rising sun helped Navya identify the ______ direction.
activities.hint: Look towards the rising sun.
activities.explanation: Well done! The rising sun helped Navya identify east.

activities.prompt: Match each direction to its clue.
activities.explanation: These pairs use the direction clues from the lesson.

activities.prompt: What helps people recognise a place easily?
options: Landmarks
Directions
Services
Journeys
activities.explanation: Landmarks help people recognise a place easily.

activities.prompt: A place appears on the left side of Navya's map. Which direction is it?
options: east
west
north
south
activities.explanation: On Navya's map, west appears on the left side.

activities.prompt: Places in the south appear at the top of Navya's map.
activities.explanation: Good try! Places in the south appear at the bottom of her map.

activities.prompt: On a map, north points upwards. The park is above the hospital. Which direction is the park from the hospital?
options: The park is north of the hospital.
The park is south of the hospital.
The park is west of the hospital.
The park is east of the hospital.

This treats the bottom of the map as north.
This mistakes the left side for the top side.
This mistakes the right side for the top side.

activities.explanation: North points upwards, and the park is above the hospital.

activities.prompt: On Navya's map, west appears on the left. The shop is left of the library. Which direction is the shop from the library?
options: The shop is east of the library.
The shop is west of the library.
The shop is north of the library.
The shop is south of the library.

This reverses the left and right sides.
This uses upward instead of leftward to find west.
This uses downward instead of leftward to find west.

activities.explanation: West appears on the left, so the shop is west of the library.

activities.prompt: On Navya's map, north points up and west points left. The rising sun shows east. Where should she draw a hospital east of her?
options: She should draw it on the left.
She should draw it at the top.
She should draw it on the right.
She should draw it at the bottom.

This puts east where west belongs.
This puts east where north belongs.
This puts east where south belongs.

activities.explanation: West is left and north is up, so east must be right.

activities.prompt: Public places provide services connected with health, safety, cleanliness, and the environment. Which place is most likely to provide a health service?
options: The bank is most likely to help.
The hospital is most likely to help.
The post office is most likely to help.
The police station is most likely to help.

The bank is public, but no health service is linked to it here.
The post office is public, but no health service is linked to it here.
why.The police station is most likely to hel: The police station is public, but no health service is linked to it here.

activities.explanation: Hospitals are public places linked with health services.

lessons.title: Test practice
lessons.sceneAlt: A red post box stands on a pole in Bangalore.
lessons.sceneCaption: A bright red post box on a pole in Bangalore.

sceneCredit.text: Postbox on Pole by Rajesh dangi at English Wikipedia, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
