lessons.title: Farming, Honey and Natural Helpers

activities.prompt: How did people keep grains safe and show kindness to nature?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Nature Helps People
activities.body: Earthen pots and bamboo baskets stored grains. Neem leaves lined the pots, and cow dung covered the outside of baskets. This protected the grains from insects and pests. The Jenu Kurubas were a tribe from Karnataka. “Jenu” meant honey. They apologised through songs when collecting honey, showing respect for nature. Dada ji made a neem oil mixture for Reena and Amit. The mixture stopped mosquitoes from biting them.
keyPoints: Grains were stored in earthen pots and bamboo baskets
Neem leaves and cow dung helped protect the grains
Honey songs showed respect for nature
A neem oil mixture stopped mosquito bites
activities.explanation: These methods show care for stored grain and respect for nature.

activities.prompt: Reena stores grain in an earthen pot and bamboo basket. How should she prepare them?
steps: She should line the pot inside with neem leaves for protection.
She should spread cow dung outside the basket for protection.
Both actions are part of the stated grain-storage method.
This method helps keep insects and pests away.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What lined the inside of the earthen pots?
options: Neem leaves
Cow dung
Grains
Honey
activities.explanation: Neem leaves lined the pots. Good choice!

activities.prompt: Cow dung was spread inside the bamboo baskets.
activities.explanation: Good try! Cow dung was spread on the outside of the baskets.

activities.prompt: Match each item with how it was used.
pairs: held medicines and mosquito repellent cream
activities.explanation: Each pair shows a use described in the lesson.

activities.prompt: What did the word “Jenu” mean?
options: Honey
Neem oil
Cow dung
Grains
activities.explanation: Yes! “Jenu” meant honey for the Jenu Kurubas.

activities.prompt: The Jenu Kurubas sang songs to apologise when they collected honey.
activities.explanation: Correct! Their songs apologised when they collected honey.

activities.prompt: What did the Jenu Kurubas' songs show?
options: Use of neem leaves
Use of cow dung
Respect for nature
Use of mosquito repellent cream
activities.explanation: Their songs showed respect for nature. You spotted the key idea!

activities.prompt: Put these events in the correct order.
items: Make a mixture with neem oil.
Rub the mixture on Reena and Amit's hands and feet.
activities.explanation: Dada ji made the mixture before it was rubbed on their hands and feet.

activities.prompt: If Reena and Amit rubbed the mixture on their hands and feet, what would happen?
options: They would collect honey.
They would store grains.
Mosquitoes would stop biting them.
They would sing an apology song.
activities.explanation: Yes! Rubbing the neem oil mixture would stop mosquitoes from biting them.

activities.prompt: Reena stores grain in a pot without neem leaves. What may happen?
options: Fewer insects may reach the grains.
The grains may become much harder.
The grains may taste much sweeter.
More insects may reach the grains.

This wrongly assumes that the pot alone protects every grain.
This mistake thinks lining with leaves makes grains harder.
This mistake thinks lining with leaves changes the grains' taste.

activities.explanation: Without the lining, the grains may lose the stated protection.

activities.prompt: Which test best checks if neem leaves stop insects?
options: Fill one pot with grain and another with water.
Compare lined grain with grain in a cow-dung basket.
Leave one pot open and line another with leaves.
Use two similar pots of grain; line only one with neem leaves.

why.Fill one pot with grain and another with: Water changes what is stored, so it does not test neem leaves.
why.Compare lined grain with grain in a cow-: This compares neem leaves with cow dung, not with no leaves.
why.Leave one pot open and line another with: Leaving one open changes another condition besides the leaves.

activities.explanation: Only the neem-leaf lining changes, so the test checks its effect.

lessons.title: Celebrations, Sacred Groves and Local Rituals

activities.prompt: How do villagers celebrate while caring for the trees and animals around them?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Village Celebration
activities.body: The village celebration came alive in the evening. Colourful lights made the whole village shine. Everyone gathered in a big field. People wore traditional clothes and jewels. Prayers were offered to the God and mother nature. The dhol and nagada filled the air, and lively beats made everyone tap their feet. Reena and Amit joined a traditional dance. Later, children thought about helping and thanking nature.
keyPoints: The village shone with colourful lights.
People celebrated with music, dance and prayers.
Children began thinking about helping and thanking nature.
activities.explanation: These details show the village celebration and the children's thoughts about nature.

activities.prompt: A community wants to make a small forest patch a Sacred Grove. What should it do?
steps: Small forest patches are Sacred Groves because local communities protect them.
The trees and wildlife stay preserved because the community looks after that patch.
Local rituals connect animals and plants with celebrations because they are part of nature.
So, the community should protect the patch and preserve its trees and wildlife.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Sacred Groves and Local Rituals
activities.body: Sacred Groves are small patches of forests protected by local communities. The trees and wildlife inside them are preserved. Local people celebrate rituals connected with animals and plants. Children in the lesson began thinking about what they could do for nature and how they could thank it.
keyPoints: Sacred Groves are small forest patches.
Local communities protect them.
Local rituals are connected with animals and plants.
activities.explanation: Sacred Groves help communities protect forests, wildlife and living things.

activities.prompt: What made the whole village shine in the evening?
options: Traditional jewels made it shine
Colourful lights made it shine
Dhol beats made it shine
Forest animals made it shine
activities.explanation: The lesson says that colourful lights made the whole village shine.

activities.prompt: The sounds of ______ and nagada filled the air.
activities.hint: It is named with nagada.
activities.explanation: The dhol and nagada made the sounds that filled the air.

activities.prompt: Match each part of the celebration to what the lesson says.
pairs: the village shone with colourful lights
activities.explanation: Each detail comes from the lively village celebration.

activities.prompt: Everyone gathered in a big field for the festivities.
activities.explanation: Yes, the people gathered in a big field for the festivities.

activities.prompt: What did the children begin thinking about after the celebrations?
options: how they could leave groves unprotected
how they could stop local rituals
how they could help and thank nature
how they could remove village lights
activities.explanation: The children thought about what they could do for nature and how they could thank it.

activities.prompt: Colourful lights shine across the village in the evening. What will likely happen next?
options: Everyone will gather in the big field.
The field will empty when people leave.
The lights will vanish before people arrive.
The festival will move indoors for the night.

This mistake thinks the lights make people leave.
why.The lights will vanish before people arr: This mistake thinks evening lights cannot shine before the gathering.
why.The festival will move indoors for the n: This mistake imagines the gathering happens indoors.

activities.explanation: This is right because everyone gathers in the big field.

activities.prompt: The dhol and nagada fill the air with lively beats. What will people likely do?
options: They will tap their feet in celebration.
They will leave the field while music plays.
They will stay still when the beats start.
They will take off their traditional clothes.

why.They will leave the field while music pl: This mistake thinks the music makes people leave.
why.They will stay still when the beats star: This mistake thinks lively beats do not make people move.
why.They will take off their traditional clo: This mistake thinks the music makes people remove clothes.

activities.explanation: This is right because lively beats make everyone tap their feet.

activities.prompt: People wear traditional clothes and jewels for the festivities. What will they also do?
options: They will pray to God and to mother nature.
They will avoid all prayer during the village festivities.
They will remove their traditional clothes and festive jewels.
They will leave mother nature outside the village festivities.

why.They will avoid all prayer during the vi: This mistake thinks festive clothes and prayer cannot happen together.
why.They will remove their traditional cloth: This mistake thinks traditional clothes and jewels are removed.
why.They will leave mother nature outside th: This mistake thinks mother nature is excluded from the celebration.

activities.explanation: This is right because prayers are offered to God and mother nature.

activities.prompt: Someone says, "A Sacred Grove is just a field for festivities." What is wrong?
options: A Sacred Grove is a protected forest patch, not a field.
A Sacred Grove is a field covered with colourful lights.
A Sacred Grove is where people wear traditional clothes.
A Sacred Grove is where dhol and nagada always play.

why.A Sacred Grove is a field covered with c: This mistake uses colourful lights as the sign of a Sacred Grove.
why.A Sacred Grove is where people wear trad: This mistake uses traditional clothes as the sign of a Sacred Grove.
why.A Sacred Grove is where dhol and nagada: This mistake uses the drums as the sign of a Sacred Grove.

activities.explanation: This is right because a Sacred Grove is a forest patch protected by local communities.

activities.prompt: A local ritual includes animals and plants. What should the children think about next?
options: Think about caring for nature and ways to thank nature.
Think only about the lights and forget about nature.
Stop thinking about nature because the ritual has ended.
Think about cutting every tree inside a Sacred Grove.

why.Think only about the lights and forget a: This mistake thinks the celebration matters more than caring for nature.
why.Stop thinking about nature because the r: This mistake thinks thoughts about nature should stop after rituals.
why.Think about cutting every tree inside a: This mistake thinks caring for nature means cutting trees in Sacred Groves.

activities.explanation: This is right because the children think about caring for and thanking nature.

lessons.title: Caring for Nature and Natural Resources

activities.prompt: How can we show kindness to nature and the animals around us?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Nature Needs Our Care
activities.body: Natural resources are things people collect from nature. Fruits, cotton and neem are examples. We can care for nature by reducing paper waste and saying no to plastic. We can spread awareness, or share what we know, about saving plants. Keeping food and water for birds helps us care for them. We can plant trees and organise a clean-up drive. Overusing wood can make forests deplete, meaning they have fewer trees.
keyPoints: Reduce paper waste and say no to plastic.
Care for birds, plants and forests.
Natural resources are things collected from nature.
activities.explanation: These caring actions help us look after nature.

activities.prompt: The school wants to help nature. It also wants to help birds. Which actions should it take, and why?
steps: It should reduce paper waste, because this helps care for nature.
It should say no to plastic, because this is another way to care for nature.
It should keep food and water for birds, because this helps care for them.
Together, these actions help the school care for nature and birds.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Planning a Herbal Garden
activities.body: A herbal garden can be designed using pictures of your favourite herbs. Pictures of different favourite herbs can go in different parts of the garden. Even herbs you like less can be included in the garden. This shows how one garden plan can include many different herbs.
keyPoints: Use pictures of favourite herbs.
Place different herbs in different parts.
Include herbs you like less too.
activities.explanation: These ideas show how to plan a herbal garden with pictures.

activities.prompt: What can you do to use less paper?
options: Say yes to plastic
Reduce paper waste
Overuse forest wood
Keep food from birds
activities.explanation: Reducing paper waste helps us care for nature.

activities.prompt: Saying yes to plastic is another way to care for nature.
activities.explanation: Saying no to plastic is a way to care for nature.

activities.prompt: Which pair should we keep for birds?
options: Food and plastic
Food and paper
Food and water
Wood and fruit
activities.explanation: Keeping food and water for birds helps us care for them.

activities.prompt: We can spread ______ about saving plants.
activities.hint: Share what you know about caring for plants.
activities.explanation: Spreading awareness tells other people about saving plants.

activities.prompt: Match each action with its result.
activities.explanation: The lesson connects each action with nature, birds, plants or forests.

activities.prompt: A herbal garden must leave out herbs that a child likes less.
activities.explanation: Even herbs that a child likes less can be included.

activities.prompt: There is paper waste. The class also says no to plastic. What may happen to nature?
options: Nature may be cared for by these choices.
Plants may lose plant awareness from these choices.
Birds may get less food and water from them.
Forests may begin to deplete from these choices.

why.Plants may lose plant awareness from the: These actions do not spread awareness about saving plants.
why.Birds may get less food and water from t: These actions do not reduce food and water kept for birds.
why.Forests may begin to deplete from these: Forest depletion comes from overusing wood, not from these choices.

activities.explanation: Reducing paper waste and refusing plastic both help care for nature.

activities.prompt: Two children like different herbs. How can a garden use pictures of both?
options: Put pictures of both herbs in different parts.
Include only the most-liked herb in the garden.
Put all herb pictures in the same part.
Leave out pictures of every less-liked herb.

why.Include only the most-liked herb in the: A garden can include even herbs a child likes less.
Different favourite herbs can go in different parts, not all together.
why.Leave out pictures of every less-liked h: Less-liked herbs can still be included in the garden.

activities.explanation: Pictures of different favourite herbs can go in different garden parts.

activities.prompt: A nature display needs things people collect. Which set fits best?
options: Fruit, cotton, and neem.
Fruit, paper, and neem.
Fruit, plastic, and neem.
Fruit, paper, and plastic.

Paper is not among the things people collect from nature.
Plastic is not among the things people collect from nature.
Paper and plastic are not among the things people collect from nature.

activities.explanation: Fruits, cotton, and neem are all collected from nature.

activities.prompt: The class wants less paper waste. It also wants bird care and plant awareness. Which plan fits?
options: Reduce paper waste, feed birds, and spread awareness.
Reduce paper waste, collect neem, and design pictures.
Plant trees, collect cotton, and design pictures.
Clean up, feed birds, and collect fruit.

why.Reduce paper waste, collect neem, and de: It lacks bird care and awareness about saving plants.
why.Plant trees, collect cotton, and design: It lacks paper waste reduction, bird care, and plant awareness.
Collecting fruit does not spread awareness about saving plants.

activities.explanation: This reduces waste, feeds birds, and spreads plant awareness.

activities.context: At a harvest festival, Reena and Amit travelled to their village near a forest. It was going to become fully powered by solar energy, so they could not wait to see it shining for the celebrations. They saw trees covered with orange-red flowers. The Palash tree was also called the ‘flame of forest’ because its blooms could make forest look reddish-orange. The houses used natural materials. Reena’s grandmother’s wall painting showed her mixing rice flour and water to make dye.
activities.prompt: What change would allow the village to shine with the full solar power Reena and Amit expect?
options: Provide the village with solar energy for all its power.
Use the Palash flowers to provide the village’s power.
Use the rice-flour dye to provide the village’s power.
Replace the natural-material houses with different ones.

why.Use the Palash flowers to provide the vi: The Palash flowers can change the forest’s appearance, but they are not described as providing power.
why.Use the rice-flour dye to provide the vi: Rice flour and water were used to make dye, not to supply the village’s power.
why.Replace the natural-material houses with: Changing the houses would not provide the solar power the children expect.

activities.explanation: This directly matches the village becoming fully powered by solar energy.

activities.context: At a harvest festival, Reena and Amit travelled to their village near a forest. It was going to become fully powered by solar energy, so they could not wait to see it shining for the celebrations. They saw trees covered with orange-red flowers. The Palash tree was also called the ‘flame of forest’ because its blooms could make forest look reddish-orange. The houses used natural materials. Reena’s grandmother’s wall painting showed her mixing rice flour and water to make dye.
activities.prompt: If the Palash trees had no flowers, how would the forest’s appearance change?
options: The reddish-orange colour would not come from the blossoms.
Solar power would make the forest look reddish-orange.
The houses’ natural materials would make the forest look reddish-orange.
The rice-flour dye would make the forest look reddish-orange.

why.Solar power would make the forest look r: Solar energy is for powering the village, not colouring the forest.
why.The houses’ natural materials would make: Natural materials are used to build the houses, not to colour the forest.
why.The rice-flour dye would make the forest: The passage does not say that the grandmother’s dye colours the forest.

activities.explanation: The Palash blossoms are what can make the forest look reddish-orange.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between the Palash tree’s blooming and Reena’s grandmother’s dye-making.
activities.answer: The Palash tree’s bright orange-red flowers can make the forest look reddish-orange. Reena’s grandmother’s method was different: she combined rice flour and water to make dye, and she showed that method in a wall painting.
points: Palash has bright orange-red flowers
The blooms can make the forest look reddish-orange
The grandmother mixed rice flour and water
The wall painting showed the dye-making method
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Reena and Amit watched their grandmother paint on a cloth. Her paint used natural extracts from flowers and leaves, together with powdered coloured stones. They had also seen Gond art on walls, showing trees, animals, birds and humans. The children collected plant parts and boiled them in about one or two litres of water to make a dye. After straining, they had natural dye and planned to paint a light-coloured handkerchief.
activities.prompt: Why do Reena and Amit strain the boiled liquid before using it?
options: Remove the plant pieces while keeping the colouring liquid
Remove the dye while keeping the boiled plant pieces
Turn the plant pieces into powdered coloured stones
Leave the plant pieces in the liquid before painting

why.Remove the dye while keeping the boiled: The plant material is removed, not the dye.
why.Turn the plant pieces into powdered colo: Boiling and straining produce dye; the stones are a separate part of the paint.
why.Leave the plant pieces in the liquid bef: The dye is left behind after the plant materials are removed.

activities.explanation: Straining removes the plant material from the liquid containing the dye.

activities.context: Reena and Amit watched their grandmother paint on a cloth. Her paint used natural extracts from flowers and leaves, together with powdered coloured stones. They had also seen Gond art on walls, showing trees, animals, birds and humans. The children collected plant parts and boiled them in about one or two litres of water to make a dye. After straining, they had natural dye and planned to paint a light-coloured handkerchief.
activities.prompt: If Amit chooses beetroot, hibiscus and marigold as the collected plant parts for the boiling and straining process, what should he expect?
options: All three can provide colouring for the dye
Only beetroot can provide colour in the final liquid
Only hibiscus and marigold can provide colour in the final liquid
None can provide colour because only flowers and leaves can be boiled

why.Only beetroot can provide colour in the: Beetroot is not the only one of the three with colouring properties.
why.Only hibiscus and marigold can provide c: Hibiscus and marigold are not the only ones with colouring properties.
why.None can provide colour because only flo: All three can provide colour, and dye can also be made from other plant parts.

activities.explanation: Beetroot, hibiscus and marigold all have colouring properties.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between the natural dye and the paint used by the grandmother.
activities.answer: The paint on the cloth contained natural extracts from flowers and leaves and powdered coloured stones. Natural dye was made by boiling collected plant parts in water and straining out the plant material. The dye was the colouring liquid left after the plant pieces were removed.
points: Paint contained extracts from flowers and leaves
Paint also contained powdered coloured stones
Dye was made by boiling plant parts
The plant material was strained out
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Reena and Amit helped store grain in earthen pots and bamboo baskets. Neem leaves lined the pots, and cow dung covered the outside of the baskets, protecting the grain from insects and pests. Dada ji made a neem-oil mixture for them to rub on their hands and feet so mosquitoes would not bite them. Their first-aid box held medicines and mosquito repellent cream. When the Jenu Kurubas collected honey, they sang apologetic songs that showed respect for nature.
activities.prompt: If cow dung were not spread on the outside of a bamboo basket, what would most likely happen to the stored grain?
options: The grain would have less protection from insects and pests.
The grain would have more protection because the earthen pots were lined.
The grain would have exactly the same protection from the other method.
The grain would be protected from insects but not from pests.

why.The grain would have more protection bec: The lining helped, but losing one method would not increase protection.
why.The grain would have exactly the same pr: One missing method would not guarantee exactly the same protection.
why.The grain would be protected from insect: Insects and pests were both threats, so they cannot be separated this way.

activities.explanation: Removing cow dung removes one way of protecting the grain.

activities.context: Reena and Amit helped store grain in earthen pots and bamboo baskets. Neem leaves lined the pots, and cow dung covered the outside of the baskets, protecting the grain from insects and pests. Dada ji made a neem-oil mixture for them to rub on their hands and feet so mosquitoes would not bite them. Their first-aid box held medicines and mosquito repellent cream. When the Jenu Kurubas collected honey, they sang apologetic songs that showed respect for nature.
activities.prompt: Reena sees the Jenu Kurubas collecting honey and begin singing. What is the best explanation for their songs?
options: The songs apologise for taking honey and show respect for nature.
The songs are a practical method for protecting the beehive from insects.
The songs guide the collectors in deciding how grain should be stored.
The songs ask Dada ji to prepare the neem-oil mixture.

why.The songs are a practical method for pro: Singing was not described as a way to protect a beehive.
why.The songs guide the collectors in decidi: The songs expressed respect rather than storage instructions.
why.The songs ask Dada ji to prepare the nee: The songs were not instructions for making the mixture.

activities.explanation: Their songs were apologies for collecting honey.

activities.prompt: Explain how the two grain-storage methods protected the stored grains.
activities.answer: Neem leaves lined the inside of the earthen pots, while cow dung was spread on the outside of the bamboo baskets. Together, these methods protected the stored grains from insects and pests by creating protective coverings around them.
points: Neem leaves lined the earthen pots.
Cow dung covered the outside of the bamboo baskets.
The methods protected grains from insects and pests.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: In the evening, the village shone with colourful lights, and everyone gathered in a field for the festivities. The dhol and nagada filled the air, and the lively beats made everyone tap their feet. Reena and Amit joined the traditional dance. The children began thinking about how they could help and thank nature. Sacred Groves were small patches of forests protected by local communities. Their trees and wildlife were preserved, and local people celebrated rituals connected with animals and plants.
activities.prompt: If local communities stopped protecting a Sacred Grove, what would most likely happen?
options: The grove's trees and wildlife would be less protected.
The field celebration would lose its dhol and nagada music.
Local rituals would no longer be connected with animals and plants.
The village would have more forest patches under local protection.

why.The field celebration would lose its dho: This affects the evening celebration rather than protection of the grove.
why.Local rituals would no longer be connect: Choosing what a ritual is connected with is separate from protecting the grove.
why.The village would have more forest patch: More protected patches would exist only if protection increased, not stopped.

activities.explanation: Local communities' protection helps preserve the trees and wildlife.

activities.context: In the evening, the village shone with colourful lights, and everyone gathered in a field for the festivities. The dhol and nagada filled the air, and the lively beats made everyone tap their feet. Reena and Amit joined the traditional dance. The children began thinking about how they could help and thank nature. Sacred Groves were small patches of forests protected by local communities. Their trees and wildlife were preserved, and local people celebrated rituals connected with animals and plants.
activities.prompt: Why is celebrating a ritual connected with animals and plants suitable for a Sacred Grove?
options: Animals and plants are living things that the grove helps preserve.
The grove and the evening field are both protected by local communities.
The grove is mainly used for the traditional dance during the festivities.
The ritual concerns the dhol and nagada used in the celebration.

why.The grove and the evening field are both: Only the Sacred Grove is described as protected by local communities.
why.The grove is mainly used for the traditi: The grove is described as a forest patch, not as a place for dancing.
why.The ritual concerns the dhol and nagada: The instruments belong to the festivities, while the ritual is about living things.

activities.explanation: The grove preserves trees and wildlife, including animals and plants.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between Sacred Groves and the village festivities?
activities.answer: The village festivities were an evening celebration with colourful lights, traditional clothes and jewels, music, dancing, and prayers to the God and mother nature. Sacred Groves were small patches of forests protected by local communities, where trees and wildlife were preserved.
points: The festivities were an evening village celebration.
People wore traditional clothes and jewels, played music, and danced.
Sacred Groves were small patches of forests.
Local communities protected groves, preserving trees and wildlife.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Neem and cotton are collected from nature, and fruits are also collected from nature. A class is planning a herbal garden and wants to plant trees. One child suggests placing pictures of favourite herbs in different parts of the garden. Another child says that herbs the class likes less can also be included. The class is also discussing ways to care for nature, such as reducing paper waste, saying no to plastic and organising a clean-up drive.
activities.prompt: If the class follows the second child's idea, what will the garden design include?
options: It will not be limited to the herbs the class prefers.
It will contain only the herbs the class prefers.
It will have no pictures of any herb.
It will place the same picture in every part.

why.It will contain only the herbs the class: This wrongly excludes herbs that can be included.
This wrongly leaves out all herb pictures.
why.It will place the same picture in every: This wrongly uses one picture instead of different ones.

activities.explanation: Less-liked herbs can also be included.

activities.context: Neem and cotton are collected from nature, and fruits are also collected from nature. A class is planning a herbal garden and wants to plant trees. One child suggests placing pictures of favourite herbs in different parts of the garden. Another child says that herbs the class likes less can also be included. The class is also discussing ways to care for nature, such as reducing paper waste, saying no to plastic and organising a clean-up drive.
activities.prompt: The class needs some wood for its nature activity. What choice would help prevent forests from depleting?
options: Avoid overusing wood taken from nature.
Take as much wood as possible from nature.
Keep taking extra wood even if forests begin to deplete.
Ignore forest depletion when choosing wood.

why.Take as much wood as possible from natur: Taking as much as possible can deplete forests.
why.Keep taking extra wood even if forests b: Extra taking continues the harm to forests.
why.Ignore forest depletion when choosing wo: Ignoring depletion does not prevent it.

activities.explanation: Avoiding overuse protects forests from depletion.

activities.prompt: Explain why reducing paper waste and saying no to plastic are ways of caring for nature.
activities.answer: Reducing paper waste helps us care for nature. Saying no to plastic is another way to care for nature. Both actions are ways of looking after nature, so wasting less paper and avoiding plastic can be part of caring for it.
points: Reducing paper waste cares for nature.
Saying no to plastic cares for nature.
Both actions show ways to look after nature.

chapters.title: Food for Health
chapters.summary: In this chapter: festival of many tastes; six tastes and millet foods; why food helps us; junk food and a balanced plate.

lessons.title: Festival of Many Tastes

activities.prompt: What secret makes the festival’s mystery food so unforgettable?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Festival Full of Food
activities.body: Students and their parents brought foods to the festival. The stalls showed fresh fruits, vegetables, sprouts and other foods. Mukesh and his friends lined up at a stall. A guessing game filled it with laughter and curiosity. The mystery food was a little sweet, salty and bitter. Ugadi Pachadi, a traditional food of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana, blends tastes in the right measure. Each taste makes it special.
keyPoints: Students and parents brought different foods.
A guessing game filled the stall with laughter.
Ugadi Pachadi blends different tastes in the right measure.
activities.explanation: This introduces the food, the guessing game and Ugadi Pachadi.

activities.prompt: In Festival of Many Tastes, why can one food have many tastes together?
steps: The tastes are blended together, so one food can have several tastes.
Ugadi Pachadi has pungent, bitter and astringent tastes.
Each taste makes the food special, so every taste matters.
The right measure balances the blend and makes it special.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What did students and their parents bring to the festival?
options: Different foods
Colourful books
Music and games
Sports equipment
activities.explanation: Students and their parents brought a variety of food to the festival.

activities.prompt: The stalls displayed fresh fruits, vegetables and sprouts.
activities.explanation: Yes. These were among the many foods displayed at the stalls.

activities.prompt: Match each thing to what happened or was true.
pairs: lined up at a colourful stall
filled the stall with laughter and curiosity
were eager to taste different food items
blends tastes in the right measure
activities.explanation: Each pair shows an action or special quality from the lesson.

activities.prompt: Ugadi Pachadi is a traditional food of Andhra Pradesh, ______ and Telengana.
activities.hint: This place is listed with Andhra Pradesh and Telengana.
activities.explanation: Ugadi Pachadi is traditional in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana.

activities.prompt: Which set matches the mystery food's tastes?
options: Sweet, salty, bitter
Only sweet and salty
Only salty and bitter
Only sweet and bitter
activities.explanation: The mystery food had a hint of sweetness. It was also a little salty and bitter.

activities.prompt: Put these festival moments in order from first to last.
items: Food was brought to the festival
Mukesh and his friends lined up
The guessing game filled the stall with laughter
activities.explanation: Food came first, then the stalls, the queue and the guessing game.

activities.prompt: Mukesh tasted the mystery food. It was sweet, salty and bitter. What can he tell?
options: The food has several tastes.
The food has only one taste.
The food has no salty taste.
The food has no bitter taste.

This ignores the sweet, salty and bitter clues.
This ignores that the food was a little salty.
This ignores that the food was a bit bitter.

activities.explanation: Sweet, salty and bitter show that it has several tastes.

activities.prompt: Ugadi Pachadi is special because of its tastes. To find why, which test is fairest?
options: Compare the full blend with the same blend missing one taste.
Compare one sweet food with one bitter food only.
Compare full food bowls with empty food bowls.
Compare one single taste with a blend of many tastes.

why.Compare one sweet food with one bitter f: This compares two different foods instead of removing one taste.
why.Compare full food bowls with empty food: This changes the amount of food instead of one taste.
why.Compare one single taste with a blend of: This compares mixing levels without isolating one taste.

activities.explanation: Changing one taste shows what that taste adds.

activities.prompt: Mukesh and his friends lined up at a colourful stall. What are they most likely to do next?
options: Taste the food and stay very curious.
Taste only the sweetest food there.
Wait until the stall has no food.
Guess at the food without tasting it.

This mistakes eagerness to taste for liking only sweet food.
Lining up does not mean waiting until no food remains.
The guessing game needs tasting, not guessing without it.

activities.explanation: The game brought laughter and curiosity, and children were eager to taste.

activities.prompt: The tastes of Ugadi Pachadi are blended in the right measure. What may happen if the measure is wrong?
options: The balanced special taste may be lost.
The food may taste even more special.
The game may fill with more laughter.
The stalls may show many more foods.

This assumes any blend is better, but the right measure matters.
A taste change does not tell us that more children will come.
A taste change does not explain why the stalls show more foods.

activities.explanation: The right measure is needed for the blended tastes to work together.

activities.prompt: Ugadi Pachadi is traditional in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana. What can a child expect the taste to be like?
options: A blend of several special tastes.
A single sweet taste only.
A taste with no salty part.
A food with no bitter part.

This ignores the food's other blended tastes.
The food can include a salty taste as well.
The food can include a bitter taste as well.

activities.explanation: Ugadi Pachadi blends several tastes in the right measure.

lessons.title: Six Tastes and Millet Foods

activities.prompt: What surprising tastes and stories might we discover at a millet stall?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Tastes and Millet Foods
activities.body: Shad rasa means the six tastes in Ayurveda. They are sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent. Eating balanced food containing shad rasa is good for health. Surbhi and her friends visited a stall of millet foods. Millets are rich sources of nutrients. The children ordered jowar upma and ate healthy foods made from millet.
keyPoints: Six tastes are sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent.
Balanced food containing shad rasa is good for health.
Millet foods provide nutrients, and children enjoyed jowar upma.
activities.explanation: These cards show the lesson's main ideas.

activities.prompt: Surbhi visits a millet-food stall and wonders how Grandma's foods and the six tastes support healthy eating.
steps: Surbhi can call the six tastes shad rasa, because that is their name in Ayurveda.
A balanced meal with shad rasa is good for health, because it contains all six tastes.
The stall foods and Grandma's rotis are healthy choices, because millets are rich in nutrients.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which item is one of the six tastes?
options: sweet
millet
jowar
jau
activities.explanation: Sweet is one of the six tastes listed in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Match each part of the story with the correct detail.
activities.explanation: The pairs match foods and places with the correct details.

activities.prompt: Why is food containing shad rasa good for health?
options: It is balanced food.
It has all six tastes.
It is served at a stall.
It is eaten in winter.
activities.explanation: The lesson says balanced food containing shad rasa is good for health.

activities.prompt: Her grandmother ate ______ and bajra roti in winter.
activities.hint: Choose the grain eaten with bajra roti in winter.
activities.explanation: Her grandmother used to eat jowar and bajra roti in winter.

activities.prompt: Which roti did her grandmother eat during summers?
options: jau roti
jowar roti
bajra roti
jowar upma
activities.explanation: Her grandmother ate jau roti during summers.

activities.prompt: Put Surbhi's millet-food events in the order they happened.
items: Eat healthy foods made from millet
activities.explanation: The children visited first, ordered next, and ate afterwards.

activities.prompt: A balanced meal has sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent. What is likely?
options: The meal is good for health.
The meal is missing one taste.
The meal has only sweet food.
The meal is bad for health.

This mistake thinks having six tastes means one taste is missing.
This mistake thinks a meal with six tastes can contain only sweet food.
This mistake turns the health benefit into the opposite claim.

activities.explanation: This is right because balanced food with shad rasa is good for health.

activities.prompt: Surbhi plans a meal with all six tastes. Grandma plans jowar roti. What makes both choices healthy?
options: Shad rasa and millet nutrients support health.
Only the six tastes provide food nutrients.
Only jowar roti has food nutrients.
Healthy food must avoid the six tastes.

why.Only the six tastes provide food nutrien: This mistake thinks tastes provide all food nutrients.
This mistake believes only one kind of roti has nutrients.
This mistake thinks healthy food must avoid the six tastes.

activities.explanation: This is right because shad rasa and nutrient-rich millets both support health.

activities.prompt: At the stall, the children order jowar upma. Their faces look happy. What does this show?
options: They enjoy ordering this millet food.
They must be forced to order it.
The dish must contain all six tastes.
The dish must have no nutrients.

This mistake assumes happiness means the children were forced.
This mistake treats happy ordering as proof of all six tastes.
This mistake treats happy ordering as proof of missing nutrients.

activities.explanation: This is right because the children were happy to order jowar upma.

activities.prompt: A child says, "The children were happy, so jowar upma has no nutrients." Which reply shows the mistake?
options: Happiness shows enjoyment, not nutrient content.
A happy taste must have fewer nutrients.
Nutrient-rich millet foods cannot make children happy.
Happiness proves that all six tastes are present.

This mistake links a happy feeling to fewer nutrients.
why.Nutrient-rich millet foods cannot make c: This mistake separates nutrients from the children's happy feelings.
why.Happiness proves that all six tastes are: This mistake treats enjoyment as proof of every taste.

activities.explanation: This is right because happiness shows enjoyment, while millets are rich in nutrients.

activities.prompt: A balanced meal has five shad rasa tastes. Sour is the one missing taste. Sour is added. What now matches the lesson?
options: It contains shad rasa and is good for health.
It adds a new taste outside shad rasa.
It loses its balanced mix of tastes.
It becomes a meal with only sweet.

This mistake thinks sour is outside the six tastes.
This mistake thinks adding a taste ruins the balanced meal.
This mistake thinks one added taste removes the other five.

activities.explanation: This is right because the balanced meal now contains all six tastes.

lessons.title: Why Food Helps Us

activities.prompt: How does the food we eat help our bodies stay healthy and strong?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Food Helps Our Body
activities.body: Our body needs different kinds of food to stay healthy, energetic and strong. Food also helps our body grow in a balanced way. No single food has all the nutrients our body needs. That is why it is important for us to eat a variety of foods. Energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods each help our body in different ways.
keyPoints: Different foods help our body in different ways
No single food contains all needed nutrients
Eating a variety of foods is important
activities.explanation: A balanced variety of foods helps our body grow and stay well.

activities.prompt: A child eats only rice for every meal. Is one food enough for a healthy body?
steps: Rice is rich in energy, so it can help give energy.
The body needs different foods because it must stay healthy, energetic, and strong.
No single food has all needed nutrients, so rice alone is not enough.
He should eat varied foods, including pulses that help the body grow.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Three Jobs of Food
activities.body: Some foods give us energy. Rice, potato, wheat, butter, ghee and oil do this. Other foods help us grow and build strong muscles. Pulses, legumes, soybeans, chickpeas and peanuts are body-building foods. Carrot, orange, lemon, papaya and spinach are protective foods. Protective foods help us fight against diseases.
keyPoints: Some foods provide energy
Body-building foods help us grow
Protective foods help us fight diseases
activities.explanation: Different foods have different jobs in our body.

activities.prompt: What does our body need to stay healthy, energetic and strong?
options: Different kinds of food
Only one kind of food
No kinds of food
Food only at night
activities.explanation: Our body needs different kinds of food to stay healthy, energetic and strong.

activities.prompt: It is important for us to eat a variety of foods.
activities.explanation: A variety of foods gives our body the different nutrients it needs.

activities.prompt: Which group includes only protective foods?
options: Carrot, rice and wheat
Rice, pulses and oil
Carrot, lemon and spinach
Potato, ghee and peanuts
activities.explanation: Carrot, lemon and spinach are protective foods.

activities.prompt: Which choice includes an energy food, a growth food and a protective food?
options: Rice, chickpeas, spinach
Rice, rice, spinach
Rice, chickpeas, rice
Chickpeas, chickpeas, spinach
activities.explanation: Rice is rich in energy, chickpeas help growth, and spinach is protective.

activities.prompt: A child eats only rice each day. Which advice follows from this lesson?
options: Eat more rice each day
Eat a variety of foods
Stop eating energy foods
Eat only protective foods
activities.explanation: No single food has all the nutrients our body needs, so variety is important.

activities.prompt: A child eats only rice. Which added food helps his body grow?
options: Add pulses, soybeans, chickpeas, and peanuts.
Add butter, ghee, and cooking oil.
Add carrots, oranges, lemons, and spinach.
Add more rice, potatoes, and wheat.

This mistake thinks energy foods also meet growth needs.
why.Add carrots, oranges, lemons, and spinac: This mistake treats protective foods as growth foods.
More energy foods still leave growth needs unmet.

activities.explanation: Right: These foods help us grow and build the body.

activities.prompt: One child eats only rice. Another eats rice, pulses, carrot, and oil. Who eats a wider variety of foods?
options: The child eating rice and potato at every meal.
The child eating only rice for every meal.
The child eating more rice at every meal.
The child eating rice, pulses, carrot, and oil.

why.The child eating rice and potato at ever: Rice and potato give energy but make a smaller variety.
why.The child eating only rice for every mea: Only rice cannot meet every food need.
why.The child eating more rice at every meal: More rice adds no new kinds of food.

activities.explanation: This child eats several kinds of foods, so the diet is varied.

activities.prompt: A child's meal has rice, potato, wheat, butter, oil, carrot, and orange. Which need may still be unmet?
options: Growing strong and building muscles.
Getting enough food energy.
Fighting against diseases.
Having many different foods.

Rice, potato, wheat, butter, and oil provide energy.
Carrot and orange are protective foods that fight diseases.
The meal already includes several different kinds of foods.

activities.explanation: The meal lacks body-building foods that support growth and muscles.

activities.prompt: A child says, "Rice has energy, so I need no other food." Which reply shows the best thinking?
options: Rice gives energy, but no food has every needed nutrient.
More rice is useful because energy is the body's only need.
Other foods are useless because rice already gives energy.
Rice is enough because all foods give the same nutrients.

why.More rice is useful because energy is th: This mistake thinks energy is the body's only need.
why.Other foods are useless because rice alr: This mistake thinks other foods add nothing to a varied diet.
why.Rice is enough because all foods give th: This mistake thinks all foods have the same nutrients.

activities.explanation: Right: Variety is needed because no single food has all nutrients.

lessons.title: Junk Food and a Balanced Plate

activities.prompt: How can we make our plates healthier without giving up all our favorite foods?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What Makes a Balanced Plate?
activities.body: Junk food has lots of oil, salt and sugar. Eating large amounts regularly is not healthy. Soft drinks, chips, burgers and pizza are junk foods. Over-processed packaged foods are junk foods. Fresh home-cooked food is better than packaged food. A food diary shows missing food groups. A balanced plate has right quantities from all three groups. Protective foods make up the most. It includes body-building and some energy foods.
keyPoints: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar
Fresh home-cooked food is better than packaged food
Protective foods make up most of a balanced plate
activities.explanation: These ideas help you choose healthy foods and build a balanced plate.

activities.prompt: A child eats chips every day. How can the child choose a better balanced plate?
steps: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar.
So eating it often in large amounts is not healthy.
A balanced plate needs right quantities from all three food groups.
Therefore, choose mostly protective foods, with body-building and some energy foods.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Find the Junk Food
activities.prompt: Which one is an example of junk food?
options: Fresh home-cooked food
Bread pakoda
Food diary
Balanced plate
activities.explanation: Bread pakoda is an example of junk food. The other choices are not examples.

activities.title: What Is Inside Junk Food?
activities.prompt: Junk food contains high amounts of oil, salt and sugar.
activities.explanation: Junk food contains high amounts of oil, salt and sugar.

activities.title: What Can a Food Diary Show?
activities.prompt: A food diary can show which food groups are ______ from your meals.
activities.hint: These are groups that your meals do not have.
activities.explanation: A food diary can show which food groups are missing from your meals.

activities.title: Match Each Clue
activities.prompt: Match each item with its correct clue.
pairs: Make up most of a balanced plate
Has right quantities from all three groups
activities.explanation: Soft drinks are junk food. A food diary reveals missing groups and helps build balanced meals.

activities.title: Choose a Balanced Plate
activities.prompt: Which description matches a balanced plate?
options: Only protective foods, with no body-building or energy foods.
Equal amounts from all three groups, with no largest group.
Mostly protective foods, with body-building and some energy foods.
Mostly junk food, with body-building and some energy foods.
activities.explanation: Protective foods make up the most. The plate also includes body-building and some energy foods.

activities.title: Steps for Using a Food Diary
activities.prompt: Put these food diary steps in order.
items: Write down what you eat each day.
Do this for every day of a week.
See which food groups are missing.
activities.explanation: Record your meals each day for a week. Then use the diary to find missing food groups.

activities.prompt: A plate has much energy food and little protective food. It has no body-building food. What should change?
options: Add more protective and body-building foods.
Add only more energy foods.
Remove every food from the plate.
Add only a little more food.

More energy foods cannot replace missing protective and body-building foods.
Removing every food leaves no food groups for a balanced plate.
A small extra amount does not correct missing groups or wrong quantities.

activities.explanation: A balanced plate needs all three groups, with protective foods making most.

activities.prompt: After a week, a child's diary shows mostly chips and soft drinks. What does this suggest about the meals?
options: They may not give a balanced plate.
They must contain every food group.
They must be better than home-cooked food.
They need no food diary next week.

The diary does not show that every group is present.
why.They must be better than home-cooked foo: Fresh home-cooked food is better than over-processed food.
This wrongly assumes that one diary cannot help check meals.

activities.explanation: Junk foods do not guarantee right quantities from all three groups.

activities.prompt: A food diary shows no body-building foods all week. What should the child do?
options: Add body-building foods to the meals.
Add more soft drinks to the meals.
Remove all protective foods from the plate.
Add more energy-providing foods only.

Soft drinks are junk food and do not replace a missing food group.
why.Remove all protective foods from the pla: Removing protective foods conflicts with making protective foods the most.
Energy foods should be included, but only in some amounts.

activities.explanation: The diary shows a missing group, so body-building foods should be added.

lessons.title: Thali, Water and Cooking

activities.prompt: How does a thali bring tastes together, and why does water matter?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Thali, Water and Cooking
activities.body: A thali includes different foods with many tastes and health benefits. Every region in India has a special thali. Water is an important part of our diet. It helps digestion and keeps our skin and body healthy. Water also removes waste from our body. Fruit chaat and vegetable salads need no cooking. A chef is a professional cook. Solar cookers use sunlight to cook food. They make no smoke or ash.
keyPoints: Thalis include many tastes and health benefits.
Water helps digestion and keeps the body healthy.
Solar cookers use sunlight without making smoke or ash.
activities.explanation: These are the main ideas in this lesson.

activities.prompt: A family wants a varied thali lunch with water and no smoke. How can they prepare it?
steps: Fruit chaat needs no cooking, so it can be served without heat.
A thali includes different foods, giving many tastes and health benefits.
A solar cooker uses sunlight, so it makes no smoke or ash.
With water for digestion and waste removal, this is a varied meal.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What Is in a Thali?
activities.prompt: What does a thali include?
options: One kind of food
Different foods
Only sweet dishes
Cooked rice only
activities.explanation: A thali includes different foods with many tastes and health benefits.

activities.title: Water and Digestion
activities.prompt: Water helps the body ______ food.
activities.hint: Think about what water does during digestion.
activities.explanation: Water helps the body digest food.

activities.title: Match the Facts
activities.prompt: Match each food or habit with its correct fact.
pairs: is an important part of our diet
can help maintain water in our body
activities.explanation: Each pair shows a food, habit or person from the lesson.

activities.title: Water and Health
activities.prompt: What does water help to keep healthy?
options: Our skin and body
Our eyes and ears
Our books and bags
Our toys and games
activities.explanation: Water helps to keep our skin and body healthy.

activities.title: Ways Water Removes Waste
activities.prompt: Put the ways water removes waste in the order taught in this lesson.
activities.explanation: The lesson lists urine first, then sweat, then faeces.

activities.title: Cooking with Sunlight
activities.prompt: What does a solar cooker use to cook food?
options: Sunlight
Ash
Smoke
Salt
activities.explanation: A solar cooker uses sunlight to cook food.

activities.prompt: Every region in India has a special thali. A child visits a new region. What may they find?
options: A special thali with many foods and health benefits.
The same single dish in every Indian region.
A meal with foods that all taste exactly alike.
A meal with no foods, only drinking water.

why.The same single dish in every Indian reg: This misses that each region has its own special thali.
why.A meal with foods that all taste exactly: This mistakes a thali for water instead of many foods.
why.A meal with no foods, only drinking wate: This confuses water's role with the foods in a thali.

activities.explanation: This fits because each region has a special thali with different foods.

activities.prompt: Water helps our body digest food. A child drinks water with lunch. What may happen?
options: The body may digest the food more easily.
The food may gain many different tastes.
All body waste may leave through the water.
The child's skin and body may stay healthy.

This confuses digestion with the many tastes in a thali.
why.All body waste may leave through the wat: This wrongly thinks water removes all waste at once.
why.The child's skin and body may stay healt: This confuses digestion with keeping skin and body healthy.

activities.explanation: Water helps the body digest food, so this is right.

activities.prompt: Water-rich fruits help maintain water in the body. A child wants a snack. Which should they choose?
options: A water-rich fruit, because it helps maintain body water.
A dry snack, because less water is easier to maintain.
A meal with many tastes, because tastes maintain body water.
A cooked meal, because all cooked meals have much water.

why.A dry snack, because less water is easie: This confuses maintaining water with eating less water.
why.A meal with many tastes, because tastes: This confuses different tastes with water-rich foods.
why.A cooked meal, because all cooked meals: This wrongly assumes every cooked meal has much water.

activities.explanation: Water-rich fruit helps maintain water in the body.

activities.prompt: Some foods need no cooking. A child wants a meal without heat. What should they choose?
options: Fruit chaat or a vegetable salad.
A cooked dish made by a professional chef.
A dish cooked in a solar cooker.
A dish cooked over a smoky fire.

why.A cooked dish made by a professional che: This confuses being a chef with preparing food that needs no cooking.
This confuses using sunlight with needing no cooking.
This confuses cooking over fire with needing no cooking.

activities.explanation: Both foods need no cooking, so they fit the meal.

activities.prompt: Solar cookers use sunlight. One cooker is said to leave ash after lunch. What should we conclude?
options: The claim is wrong, because solar cookers make no smoke or ash.
The claim is right, because every cooker must make ash.
The claim is wrong, because sunlight cannot cook food.
The claim is right, because sunlight turns into cooking ash.

why.The claim is right, because every cooker: This wrongly assumes every cooker must make ash.
why.The claim is wrong, because sunlight can: This denies that sunlight can cook food.
why.The claim is right, because sunlight tur: This confuses sunlight used for cooking with ash.

activities.explanation: A solar cooker cooks food without making smoke or ash.

lessons.sceneCaption: An Indian thali brings six different tastes together on one metal plate.

lessons.title: Food Activities and Labels

activities.prompt: What can we discover about our food by exploring pictures and labels?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Food Collages and Label Checks
activities.body: Make a food collage by cutting food pictures from old magazines and newspapers. You use scissors and glue to place pictures on paper. The collage has energy-giving, body-building and protective food sections. At home, you can pick up a packaged food item to check its label. Note the expiry date and two main ingredients. A food festival may include home-made food from children.
keyPoints: Collage materials include old magazines, newspapers, scissors, glue and paper.
Food collage sections are energy-giving, body-building and protective.
Label checks note expiry dates and two main ingredients.
activities.explanation: This card introduces food collages, label checks and the food festival.

activities.prompt: You have old magazines and paper. How can you make a food collage and check a label?
steps: Use old magazines, newspapers, scissors, glue and paper because these are needed.
Cut out food pictures because this is how children make the collage.
Use three sections because they cover energy-giving, body-building and protective foods.
Write expiry date and two main ingredients because labels show these details.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Labels and the Food Festival
activities.body: At home, pick up a packaged food item and check its label. Note the expiry date and two main ingredients. The sample label says all natural, no sugar added, and pure and delicious. Children may bring home-made food to a food festival. The festival can be held at school. Parents may be encouraged to join it.
keyPoints: Label checks note an expiry date and two main ingredients.
The sample label says all natural, no sugar added, and pure and delicious.
Home-made food may come to a school food festival.
activities.explanation: You can check food labels at home and enjoy a school food festival.

activities.prompt: The collage has energy-giving, body-building and protective food sections.
activities.explanation: Yes, these are the three sections named in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Check the label for the expiry date and ______ main ingredients.
activities.hint: Your book gives the number of main ingredients.
activities.explanation: A label check includes the expiry date and two main ingredients.

activities.prompt: Match each item to its job in the collage activity.
activities.explanation: These materials help you find, cut out and join food pictures on paper.

activities.prompt: Which claim is written on the sample label?
options: All natural and no sugar added
All artificial and no sugar added
All natural and sugar added
Pure, delicious, sugar added
activities.explanation: The sample label says all natural, no sugar added, and pure and delicious.

activities.prompt: The food festival can be held at school.
activities.explanation: Yes, your book says that the food festival can be held at school.

activities.prompt: Match each group to its role in the food festival.
activities.explanation: Children may bring food, school may hold the festival and parents may join.

activities.prompt: The collage has energy-giving and body-building sections. What section is missing?
options: Protective food section
Expiry date section
Sample label section
Food festival section

why.Expiry date section: An expiry date belongs on a label, not in a collage section.
why.Sample label section: A sample label is used for a label check, not a collage section.
why.Food festival section: A food festival is an event, not a collage section.

activities.explanation: The collage includes a section for protective foods.
