activities.context: Students and parents brought a variety of food to the festival. Stalls displayed fresh fruits, vegetables, sprouts and other foods. Mukesh and his friends lined up at a colourful stall, where a guessing game filled it with laughter and curiosity. The mystery food had a hint of sweetness, was a little salty and a bit bitter. Children were eager to taste different items. Ugadi Pachadi, a traditional food of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana, has pungent, bitter and astringent tastes.
activities.prompt: After the guessing game at the colourful stall, what would the stallkeepers most likely do next?
options: Encourage them to try the foods on display.
Keep every food item hidden until the festival ended.
Ask them to try only the mystery food once more.
End the guessing game and send the children away.

why.Keep every food item hidden until the fe: Hiding the food would prevent the children from tasting the different items.
why.Ask them to try only the mystery food on: Asking them to repeat only the mystery-food tasting would ignore their eagerness to try other items.
why.End the guessing game and send the child: Sending the children away would interrupt the curiosity and fun of the guessing game.

activities.explanation: The children were eager to taste different food items, so inviting them to try the foods would be a sensible next step.

activities.context: Students and parents brought a variety of food to the festival. Stalls displayed fresh fruits, vegetables, sprouts and other foods. Mukesh and his friends lined up at a colourful stall, where a guessing game filled it with laughter and curiosity. The mystery food had a hint of sweetness, was a little salty and a bit bitter. Children were eager to taste different items. Ugadi Pachadi, a traditional food of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana, has pungent, bitter and astringent tastes.
activities.prompt: If the tastes in Ugadi Pachadi were blended in the wrong measure, what would happen?
options: Its special combination of tastes would not be the same.
It would have only one taste instead of several.
It would have no taste at all.
It would taste exactly as it does now.

why.It would have only one taste instead of: Using the wrong measure would change the combination, but it would not necessarily remove every other taste.
Nothing in the lesson suggests that incorrect blending would remove all taste.
The special combination would change because the tastes would no longer be blended in the right measure.

activities.explanation: The right measure is needed to blend the different tastes as intended.

activities.prompt: How do the different tastes and the right measure make Ugadi Pachadi special?
activities.answer: Ugadi Pachadi is special because it has several tastes, not just one. Its remaining tastes are pungent, bitter and astringent. Each taste makes it special, and blending all the tastes in the right measure creates its special combination.
points: Mentions that Ugadi Pachadi has several tastes.
Names pungent, bitter and astringent as remaining tastes.
Explains that each taste makes the food special.
Explains the importance of blending in the right measure.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Surbhi and her friends visited a stall of millet foods. Surbhi remembered that her grandmother used to eat jowar and bajra roti in winter, but she ate jau roti during summers. The friends were happy to order jowar upma. Surbhi explained that millets are rich sources of nutrients and that the food they ate was healthy because it was made from millet. She also knew that a balanced meal containing shad rasa was good for health.
activities.prompt: If Surbhi's grandmother wanted a roti that matched her usual summer habit, what should she choose?
options: Choose the roti made from jau, because she usually ate it during summers.
Choose the roti made from jowar, because winter was her usual roti season.
Choose the roti made from bajra, because she ate it with every season.
Choose the roti made from jowar, because she ate it instead of jau roti in summer.

why.Choose the roti made from jowar, because: Jowar roti was her winter habit, not her summer habit.
why.Choose the roti made from bajra, because: Bajra roti was also a winter choice; she did not eat it in summer.
why.Choose the roti made from jowar, because: This option mixes jowar with the summer habit and names the wrong roti.

activities.explanation: Jau roti matches her stated summer habit.

activities.context: Surbhi and her friends visited a stall of millet foods. Surbhi remembered that her grandmother used to eat jowar and bajra roti in winter, but she ate jau roti during summers. The friends were happy to order jowar upma. Surbhi explained that millets are rich sources of nutrients and that the food they ate was healthy because it was made from millet. She also knew that a balanced meal containing shad rasa was good for health.
activities.prompt: Why could Surbhi describe the jowar upma her friends ordered as a healthy choice?
options: The upma used millet, and the nutrient-rich nature of millet explains the healthy choice.
The friends were happy after ordering it, so their happiness proves that it was healthy.
The upma came from a stall, so buying food at a stall shows that it is healthy.
It was called jowar upma, so the name by itself proves that it was healthy.

why.The friends were happy after ordering it: Happiness does not prove that a food is healthy.
why.The upma came from a stall, so buying fo: The stall is where they bought it; that fact does not show its nutrient content.
why.It was called jowar upma, so the name by: A food's name alone cannot show that it is healthy.

activities.explanation: The passage identifies the upma as millet food and millet as nutrient-rich.

activities.prompt: Why should Surbhi's friends choose balanced food containing shad rasa?
activities.answer: Why should Surbhi's friends choose balanced food containing shad rasa? The six tastes—sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent—are called shad rasa in Ayurveda. Eating balanced food containing shad rasa is good for health.
points: Names the six tastes.
Explains that the six tastes are called shad rasa.
States that balanced food containing shad rasa is good for health.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student feels tired and is not growing well. The student often eats rice with oil for every meal and refuses pulses, soybeans, chickpeas, peanuts, carrot, orange, lemon, papaya and spinach. The family thinks rice and oil alone are enough because they both provide energy. However, no single food contains all the nutrients our bodies need. The student should eat a variety of foods, including body-building foods and protective foods, to stay healthy, energetic and strong.
activities.prompt: What should the student change about the meals?
options: Eat a varied diet rather than depending only on rice and oil.
Keep eating only rice and oil at every meal.
Eat only pulses, soybeans, chickpeas and peanuts.
Eat only carrot, orange, lemon, papaya and spinach.

why.Keep eating only rice and oil at every m: Rice and oil provide energy, but they cannot supply every needed nutrient.
why.Eat only pulses, soybeans, chickpeas and: These foods help growth, but they do not cover all our food needs.
why.Eat only carrot, orange, lemon, papaya a: These foods help fight diseases, but they do not cover all our food needs.

activities.explanation: A variety of foods supplies the different nutrients our body needs.

activities.context: A student feels tired and is not growing well. The student often eats rice with oil for every meal and refuses pulses, soybeans, chickpeas, peanuts, carrot, orange, lemon, papaya and spinach. The family thinks rice and oil alone are enough because they both provide energy. However, no single food contains all the nutrients our bodies need. The student should eat a variety of foods, including body-building foods and protective foods, to stay healthy, energetic and strong.
activities.prompt: Why are rice and oil alone not enough for the student?
options: Because rice and oil do not provide energy to the body.
Because relying on one kind of food cannot supply all the nutrients we need.
Because only body-building foods are needed for balanced growth.
Because protective foods can replace all other kinds of food.

why.Because rice and oil do not provide ener: Rice and oil do provide energy to our body.
why.Because only body-building foods are nee: Body-building foods are needed, but they are not the only useful foods.
why.Because protective foods can replace all: Protective foods fight diseases, but they cannot replace every other kind of food.

activities.explanation: No single food contains all the nutrients our bodies need.

activities.context: A student feels tired and is not growing well. The student often eats rice with oil for every meal and refuses pulses, soybeans, chickpeas, peanuts, carrot, orange, lemon, papaya and spinach. The family thinks rice and oil alone are enough because they both provide energy. However, no single food contains all the nutrients our bodies need. The student should eat a variety of foods, including body-building foods and protective foods, to stay healthy, energetic and strong.
activities.prompt: If the student adds protective foods but still leaves out body-building foods, what is likely?
options: The student may still lack food that helps build strong muscles.
The student will certainly have every nutrient needed for growth.
The student will become strong even without body-building foods.
The student will get more energy from protective foods alone.

why.The student will certainly have every nu: No single food supplies all the nutrients our bodies need.
why.The student will become strong even with: Strong muscles depend on body-building foods.
why.The student will get more energy from pr: Protective foods help fight diseases rather than provide energy.

activities.explanation: Protective foods fight diseases, but body-building foods are still needed for muscles and growth.

activities.prompt: Explain why we should eat a variety of foods.
activities.answer: Our body needs different kinds of food to stay healthy, energetic and strong. Energy-giving foods cannot supply every nutrient we need. Body-building foods help us grow and build muscles, while protective foods help us fight diseases. Eating a variety of foods therefore supports balanced growth and keeps us healthy.
points: Different foods are needed to stay healthy and strong.
No single food supplies all needed nutrients.
Body-building foods support growth and muscles.
Protective foods help fight diseases.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Every day, a student eats soft drinks and chips with lunch. The student also often chooses packaged pizza instead of fresh home-cooked food. To check the meals, the student writes down everything eaten each day for a week in a food diary. The diary shows that protective foods are missing from many meals and that junk food is taking the largest place on the plate.
activities.prompt: After checking the food diary, what should the student do about the missing food groups?
options: Add protective foods and make sure meals also include body-building foods and some energy-giving foods.
Add only more junk food because it was already taking up the most space.
Stop recording meals because the missing foods have already been identified.
Remove every food except the group that appeared most often in the diary.

why.Add only more junk food because it was a: More junk food would not correct the missing food groups.
why.Stop recording meals because the missing: The diary should continue to help the student check balanced meals.
why.Remove every food except the group that: Eating only one food group would not make a balanced plate.

activities.explanation: The diary shows that protective foods are missing, so they should be added.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between a food diary and a balanced plate.
activities.answer: A food diary records what someone eats each day for a week and can show missing food groups. A balanced plate includes the right quantities from all three groups. Protective foods take up most of it, while body-building foods and some energy-giving foods are also included.
points: A food diary records meals each day for a week.
A food diary can reveal missing food groups.
A balanced plate has the right quantities from all three groups.
Protective foods make up most of a balanced plate.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A chef is preparing a meal for families from different regions of India. Each region’s special thali contains foods with different tastes and health benefits. The chef also makes fruit chaat and a vegetable salad, which need no cooking. For a cooked dish, the chef uses a solar cooker. Water is served with the meal, and water-rich fruits help maintain water in the body.
activities.prompt: If the families drink too little water with their meal, what may happen next?
options: Their bodies may find digestion harder and waste removal less effective.
Their skin and bodies would become healthier.
They would digest their food more easily.
Their bodies would remove waste more quickly.

why.Their skin and bodies would become healt: Not drinking enough may reduce these benefits.
why.They would digest their food more easily: More water would help digestion, not make it easier.
why.Their bodies would remove waste more qui: Sufficient water helps remove waste more effectively.

activities.explanation: Water supports digestion and waste removal.

activities.context: A chef is preparing a meal for families from different regions of India. Each region’s special thali contains foods with different tastes and health benefits. The chef also makes fruit chaat and a vegetable salad, which need no cooking. For a cooked dish, the chef uses a solar cooker. Water is served with the meal, and water-rich fruits help maintain water in the body.
activities.prompt: What advantage does the solar cooker give the chef?
options: It cooks with sunlight and avoids making smoke or ash.
It cooks with sunlight but requires smoke and ash.
It cooks without sunlight but creates no smoke or ash.
It supplies drinking water while the food cooks.

why.It cooks with sunlight but requires smok: It does not make smoke or ash.
why.It cooks without sunlight but creates no: Sunlight is needed for a solar cooker to cook food.
why.It supplies drinking water while the foo: It cooks food rather than supplying water.

activities.explanation: A solar cooker uses sunlight for cooking.

activities.prompt: Why is water an important part of our diet?
activities.answer: Water is important because it helps the body digest food and keeps the skin and body healthy. It also removes waste through urine, sweat and faeces. Drinking sufficient water should therefore be a healthy habit.
points: Water helps digest food.
Water keeps the skin and body healthy.
Water removes waste from the body.
Drinking sufficient water is a healthy habit.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Explain why the food pictures are placed in different sections of the collage.
activities.answer: The pictures are placed in separate sections because the foods have different purposes. Energy-giving foods belong in the energy section, body-building foods belong in the body-building section, and protective foods belong in the protective section.
points: Explains that the pictures are sorted.
Identifies the energy-giving section.
Identifies the body-building and protective sections.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Food for Health

activities.prompt: Ugadi Pachadi is a traditional food of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana.
activities.explanation: It is traditional in all three places. Each taste makes it special.

activities.prompt: Millets are rich sources of ______.
activities.hint: These help our bodies stay healthy.
activities.explanation: Millets are rich sources of nutrients.

activities.prompt: Match each food with its food group.
activities.explanation: Energy foods give energy, body-building foods support growth, and protective foods fight diseases.

activities.prompt: Put these food diary steps in order.
items: Write down what you eat each day.
Keep doing this for a week.
Check which food groups are missing.
activities.explanation: A food diary can show which food groups are missing from meals.

activities.prompt: Mukesh's mystery food was not only sweet. What other tastes did it have?
options: salty and bitter
sour and salty
pungent and bitter
astringent and sour
activities.explanation: It had a little salty taste and a bit of bitter taste.

activities.prompt: Junk food usually has low amounts of oil, salt and sugar.
activities.explanation: Junk food contains high amounts of oil, salt and sugar.

activities.prompt: Which sentence about the food festival and collage is correct?
options: Students may bring home-made food to a food festival.
The collage needs only old magazines and paper.
The food festival must be held at home.
The collage has only energy-giving food sections.
activities.explanation: Students may bring home-made food, and the festival can be held at school. The collage has three food sections.

activities.prompt: A balanced plate has right quantities from all ______ food groups.
activities.hint: It has energy-giving, body-building and protective foods.
activities.explanation: It also includes protective foods, body-building foods and some energy-providing foods.

activities.prompt: Match each item with its description.
pairs: Includes foods with many tastes and health benefits
activities.explanation: Water supports digestion, and a solar cooker uses sunlight. Fruit chaat needs no cooking.

chapters.title: Happy and Healthy Living
chapters.summary: In this chapter: happy about food; the journey of the grains; mindful eating; valuing food.

lessons.title: Happy About Food

activities.prompt: What makes you feel happy when you eat something you love?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Food and Happiness
activities.body: Everyone feels happy sometimes, but people feel happy at different times. We also feel happy for different reasons. Eating our favourite foods is one happy occasion. We enjoy eating many kinds of food. Some foods are made from grains, pulses or vegetables. Rice and wheat grains can be part of our diet. It is interesting to know how each food item reaches us.
keyPoints: People feel happy at different times.
Eating favourite foods is one happy occasion.
Grains, pulses and vegetables can be used in food items.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you notice food and happiness around you.

activities.prompt: Two children feel happy at different times, and one is happy after a favourite food. Why?
steps: Happy times differ, so everyone can feel happy at a different time.
People have different reasons for happiness, so one child's reason may differ from another's.
Eating a favourite food is one happy occasion, so it can explain one child's happiness.
Therefore, the children can feel happy at different times and for different reasons.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which statement is true?
options: People feel happy at different times.
Everyone feels happy at the same time.
People feel happy for the same reason.
All happy times happen while eating.
activities.explanation: The lesson says people feel happy at different times and for different reasons.

activities.prompt: Rice is a kind of ______.
activities.hint: Rice and wheat are named together.
activities.explanation: Rice is named as a grain that can form part of our diet.

activities.prompt: Match each example to its group.
activities.explanation: Rice and wheat are grains. Pulses and vegetables can also be used in food items.

activities.prompt: Which group includes rice and wheat?
options: Grains
Pulses
Vegetables
Food items
activities.explanation: Rice and wheat are both named as grains in the lesson.

activities.prompt: The lesson says it is interesting to know what about each food item?
options: How it reaches us
Why it makes people happy
Why people feel happy
When people feel happy
activities.explanation: The lesson says it is interesting to know how each food item reaches us.

activities.prompt: Which statement fits the lesson?
options: People enjoy many kinds of food.
Everyone feels happy at the same time.
Food items are made only from grains.
Grains are not used in food items.
activities.explanation: People enjoy many kinds of food. The other statements contradict the lesson.

activities.prompt: Eating our favourite foods can be a happy occasion. A child is about to eat one. What should you expect?
options: The child may feel happy while eating it.
The child will feel happy at every happy occasion.
The child will never feel happy while eating.
The child must feel happy before tasting it.

why.The child will feel happy at every happy: It assumes one favourite food brings happiness every time.
why.The child will never feel happy while ea: It confuses one happy occasion with never feeling happy.
why.The child must feel happy before tasting: It puts happiness before the happy eating occasion.

activities.explanation: A favourite food is one happy occasion, so happiness is possible.

activities.prompt: Happiness has different reasons. One child feels happy after favourite food. What can we say about another child?
options: The other child may feel happy at a different time.
The other child must feel happy at a different time.
The other child must eat that same favourite food.
The other child cannot feel happy with another reason.

why.The other child must feel happy at a dif: It turns a possibility into a rule for every child.
why.The other child must eat that same favou: It wrongly assumes one food is needed for every reason.
why.The other child cannot feel happy with a: It assumes different reasons prevent any happiness.

activities.explanation: Different happy times are possible, but they are not certain.

activities.prompt: People enjoy eating many kinds of food. Why might several kinds suit a family?
options: Different kinds can match different happy reasons.
Every kind can make every family member happy.
Different kinds must give every person one reason.
One kind can be the only food that everyone enjoys.

why.Every kind can make every family member: It assumes every kind and every person will feel happy.
why.Different kinds must give every person o: It treats different reasons as one shared reason.
why.One kind can be the only food that every: It assumes people enjoy only one kind of food.

activities.explanation: People enjoy many kinds and feel happy for different reasons.

activities.prompt: Some food items are made from grains, pulses, and vegetables. How can we check them fairly?
options: Check one item from each group in the same way.
Check three grain items and skip the other groups.
Check one pulse item and guess about other groups.
Check food items without checking any food group.

why.Check three grain items and skip the oth: It gives extra attention to grains and skips other groups.
why.Check one pulse item and guess about oth: It checks pulses but guesses about grains and vegetables.
why.Check food items without checking any fo: It leaves all three groups unchecked.

activities.explanation: It checks every group once and uses the same method.

activities.prompt: It is interesting to know how each food item reaches us. What is the best way to learn?
options: Follow one food item and note each step.
Only count how many food items arrive.
Only ask if the food is a favourite.
Guess the route without checking it.

It counts food but does not learn the route.
It checks happiness instead of the food's route.
It guesses a route without gathering any clues.

activities.explanation: Following and checking the item can reveal how it reaches us.

lessons.title: The Journey of the Grains

activities.prompt: What helps a tiny seed become the food on our plate?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Many Helpers Help
activities.body: A grain’s journey from a farm to our plate is long and remarkable. It begins with sowing a seed. Farmers, sellers and other people help it happen. Animals help too. Water, soil and sunlight are important. We remember every helper with love and gratitude. This helps us value each grain and enjoy its taste.
keyPoints: The journey from sowing a seed to food is remarkable.
People, animals, water, soil and sunlight help.
Gratitude helps us value each grain and enjoy its taste.
activities.explanation: Remembering the helpers makes us value every grain.

activities.prompt: A child asks how a seed becomes food on the family plate.
steps: A seed is sown on a farm, starting the grain's long journey.
Water, soil, and sunlight help because they play an important part.
Farmers, sellers, and animals help because they make the journey possible.
The grain reaches our plate, so we remember every helper with gratitude.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Important Helpers
activities.prompt: Which three things play an important part in a grain’s journey?
options: Water, soil and sunlight
Farmers and animals
Sellers and festivals
People and gratitude
activities.explanation: Water, soil and sunlight all play an important part.

activities.title: Animal Helpers
activities.prompt: Animals also help make a grain’s journey possible.
activities.explanation: Animals help too. The lesson says they help make the journey possible.

activities.title: A Helpful Light
activities.prompt: Water, soil and ______ play an important part in a grain’s journey.
activities.hint: The lesson names this with water and soil.
activities.explanation: Sunlight is named with water and soil as important.

activities.title: Journey Connections
activities.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning from the lesson.
pairs: Also help make the journey possible
activities.explanation: People, animals and nature all help the journey. Gratitude helps us enjoy its result.

activities.title: Festivals of Gratitude
activities.prompt: What do some Indian festivals show to Mother Nature for food?
options: Deep gratitude
Great sadness
Bright anger
Calm fear
activities.explanation: Some festivals show gratitude to Mother Nature for the food we eat.

activities.title: The Effects of Gratitude
activities.prompt: Which pair of effects comes from remembering helpers with gratitude?
options: Valuing each grain and enjoying its taste
Forgetting each grain and enjoying its taste
Valuing each grain and avoiding its taste
Forgetting each grain and avoiding its taste
activities.explanation: Gratitude makes us feel each grain’s importance. It also helps us enjoy the taste.

activities.prompt: A child says, "Only the farmer helps." Why is this claim incomplete?
options: Water, soil, sunlight, people, and animals all help grain.
Only the farmer can make the whole journey possible.
Sellers and animals have no part in making grain possible.
Food reaches our plate without help from anyone.

why.Only the farmer can make the whole journ: This mistake ignores nature's part in grain growth.
why.Sellers and animals have no part in maki: This mistake ignores sellers, animals, and other helpers.
why.Food reaches our plate without help from: This mistake thinks food needs no helpers at all.

activities.explanation: This is right because nature, people, and animals all help.

activities.prompt: A child says, "Grain appears by itself." Why is this claim flawed?
options: The journey needs farmers, sellers, animals, and nature.
The seed can become food without water or sunlight.
The farmer alone makes grain ready for our plate.
The long journey ends before grain reaches our plate.

why.The seed can become food without water o: This mistake thinks water and sunlight are unnecessary.
why.The farmer alone makes grain ready for o: This mistake thinks only farmers help the grain.
why.The long journey ends before grain reach: This mistake ends the journey before it reaches our plate.

activities.explanation: This is right because many helpers and nature make the journey possible.

activities.prompt: If animals stop helping, what happens to the grain's journey?
options: The journey becomes harder because animals help make it possible.
The grain grows faster without animal help.
The journey stays exactly the same in every way.
The grain needs no farmers or sellers.

why.The grain grows faster without animal he: This mistake thinks losing animal help speeds up growth.
why.The journey stays exactly the same in ev: This mistake thinks one helper has no effect.
This mistake thinks farmers and sellers do not help.

activities.explanation: This is right because animals help make the journey possible.

lessons.title: Mindful Eating

activities.prompt: What do our senses notice when we eat one bite slowly?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Notice Every Bite
activities.body: Mindful eating means paying attention to what and how you eat. Put food in your mouth slowly. Your tongue and mouth feel its surface, and your teeth help you chew gently. Your tongue, nose and other senses help you notice flavour and taste. As you chew, you remember the taste. Before swallowing, remember the texture, or how food feels. This helps you make healthier choices and appreciate your food.
keyPoints: Put each food item in your mouth slowly.
Chew well and enjoy every bite fully.
Notice flavour, taste and texture.
activities.explanation: Slow, careful eating helps you enjoy and appreciate your food.

activities.prompt: A child eats a peanut too fast. How can eating slowly help?
steps: Slow eating lets the tongue and mouth feel the food’s surface.
The teeth can chew gently, helping the child notice each bite.
The tongue and mouth can notice the taste as chewing continues.
Remembering the taste and texture helps the child enjoy the bite.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: First, Sit and Listen
activities.prompt: What did the teacher ask the students to do first?
options: Stand in a circle and open their eyes.
Sit in a row and close their mouths.
Sit in a circle and close their eyes.
Stand in a row and clap their hands.
activities.explanation: The teacher asked students to sit in a circle. They also closed their eyes.

activities.title: The Peanut Activity
activities.prompt: The teacher placed one peanut on each student's palm.
activities.explanation: Yes, the teacher placed one peanut on each student's palm. This is exactly what happened.

activities.title: Remember Before Swallowing
activities.prompt: Before swallowing, we remember the food's ______.
activities.hint: Texture is how the food feels.
activities.explanation: Texture means how the food feels. You remember it before swallowing.

activities.title: Match the Eating Actions
activities.prompt: Match each body part or action to what it does.
activities.explanation: Your body parts and senses work together while eating. Each one has a special job.

activities.title: Choose Mindful Eating
activities.prompt: Which action best shows mindful eating?
options: Stop tasting every bite.
Swallow food without chewing.
Watch the clock while eating.
Eat slowly and focus on each bite.
activities.explanation: Eating slowly and focusing helps you enjoy your food better. These are important parts of mindful eating.

activities.title: Order the Eating Steps
activities.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: Put each food item in your mouth slowly
Feel the food's surface with your tongue and mouth
Chew the food gently with your teeth
activities.explanation: Slow tasting comes before gentle chewing. Remembering the texture comes before swallowing.

activities.title: A Better Way to Eat
activities.prompt: A student eats quickly without noticing each bite. Which choice shows mindful eating?
options: Eat while doing another task.
Eat slowly and focus on each bite.
Swallow each bite without chewing.
Choose food without noticing its taste.
activities.explanation: Mindful eating asks you to notice what and how you eat. Slow, focused bites help you enjoy your food.

activities.title: Mindful or Not?
activities.prompt: Mindful eating means eating without noticing what or how you eat.
activities.explanation: False. Mindful eating means paying attention to what and how we eat. Enjoying every bite fully is important too.

activities.prompt: Which test would best show how eating speed changes mindful eating?
options: Give matching bites and change only the eating speed.
Give different foods and change only the eating speed.
Give matching bites and change the food and speed.
Give different foods while every child eats the same way.

why.Give different foods and change only the: Changing the food as well hides the effect of speed.
why.Give matching bites and change the food: Changing food and speed does not test a clear cause.
why.Give different foods while every child e: Eating everyone the same way does not compare eating speeds.

activities.explanation: Only eating speed changes, so the test is fair.

activities.prompt: A child says, “Chew fast to enjoy every bite.” What is wrong?
options: Quick chewing gives less time to notice each bite.
Quick chewing makes the food taste less strongly.
Quick chewing makes the teeth chew more gently.
Quick chewing stops the tongue from feeling texture.

why.Quick chewing makes the food taste less: This wrongly says quick chewing changes how strongly food tastes.
why.Quick chewing makes the teeth chew more: This wrongly says quick chewing controls how gently teeth chew.
why.Quick chewing stops the tongue from feel: This wrongly says quick chewing blocks the tongue’s sense of touch.

activities.explanation: Slow chewing gives time to notice taste and texture.

lessons.title: Valuing Food

activities.prompt: How could a food diary help us value every meal?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Why Food Is Precious
activities.body: Every grain is precious because people have worked hard to bring food to our plates. Wasting food does not respect that hard work. We can value food by keeping a record for one week. After every meal, we make an entry. We write ‘Yes’ and a happy smiley if we ate everything. We write ‘No’ and a sad face if we left some food.
keyPoints: Every grain is precious.
Food records help us value food.
Yes and No entries show what we ate.
activities.explanation: A food record helps us notice how much food we eat.

activities.prompt: A child eats some food but leaves part of it. How should it be recorded, and why?
steps: Every grain is precious, so the food left still matters.
We check the plate, because the entry must show what was left.
Write “No” and draw a sad face, because that marks leftover food.
This record helps value food, because it shows the waste clearly.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What does a ‘Yes’ entry tell us?
options: We ate everything
We left some food
We skipped a meal
We made a record
activities.explanation: A ‘Yes’ entry means that you ate everything. It is marked with a happy smiley.

activities.prompt: A happy smiley marks a ‘Yes’ entry.
activities.explanation: The happy smiley shows that you ate everything.

activities.prompt: We can keep a record of our food for one ______.
activities.hint: Write the part of time after ‘one’.
activities.explanation: We can keep a food record for one week.

activities.prompt: Match each record sign or word to its meaning.
activities.explanation: Each word and face helps show whether you ate everything or left some food.

activities.prompt: Put these meal record steps in order.
activities.explanation: Make an entry after each meal. Breakfast comes before lunch and dinner.

activities.prompt: Which plan follows the food record rules?
options: One week, every meal, Yes or No with a face
One week, one meal, Yes or No with a face
One week, every meal, only Yes entries with faces
One week, every meal, Yes or No without faces
activities.explanation: Keep the record for one week and make an entry after every meal. Mark each entry Yes or No with a face.

activities.prompt: A child leaves some food but writes “Yes”. What should the teacher think?
options: The entry is correct because the child ate some.
The entry is wrong because some food was left.
The entry is wrong because the child ate too much.
The entry is correct because the child ate at lunch.

why.The entry is correct because the child a: Eating some food does not make a “Yes” entry correct.
why.The entry is wrong because the child ate: The rule does not judge how much the child ate.
why.The entry is correct because the child a: The entry must match what happened at every meal.

activities.explanation: A “Yes” means everything was eaten, but food was left.

activities.prompt: A child eats everything at every meal for one week. What pattern should appear?
options: Every entry says Yes with a happy smiley.
Every entry says No with a sad face.
Only breakfast says Yes with a happy smiley.
Only lunch says No with a sad face.

A sad face means food was left, but none was left.
why.Only breakfast says Yes with a happy smi: Breakfast alone does not represent all three meals.
Lunch alone does not represent all three meals.

activities.explanation: Each meal gets a Yes entry and a happy smiley.

activities.prompt: Why does leaving food fail to show that food is valued?
options: Everyone who brought the food has worked hard.
Every grain is precious, so food does not matter.
Food matters only after some is thrown away.
A happy face makes leftover food seem more valuable.

why.Every grain is precious, so food does no: This mistakes precious food for food that does not matter.
why.Food matters only after some is thrown a: This reverses the lesson that every grain is precious.
why.A happy face makes leftover food seem mo: A face changes the record, but not the wasted food.

activities.explanation: Leaving food does not respect the hard work behind it.

activities.prompt: A child says, “Leaving food is fine because I am full.” What is wrong with this claim?
options: Leaving food does not respect the hard work behind it.
Feeling full makes the hard work behind food disappear.
Full children should always clear every plate.
Food should be valued only when nobody feels full.

why.Feeling full makes the hard work behind: Feeling full does not erase the work that brought the food.
why.Full children should always clear every: The lesson does not say feeling full makes waste correct.
why.Food should be valued only when nobody f: Food is precious, even when the child feels full.

activities.explanation: Leaving food does not respect the hard work behind it.

lessons.title: Enjoy Sports and Sleep Well

activities.prompt: How can sports, yoga, and sleep help us feel our best?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Exercise, Yoga and Sleep
activities.body: Playing, running, jumping, cycling and skipping are physical activities. They help you stay strong and energetic. Yoga can improve your posture and help you stay happy and active. Khel Yoga includes interesting exercises and games. Your body also needs enough sleep every day. Good sleep takes away tiredness and helps you feel fresh.
keyPoints: Exercise helps us stay strong and energetic.
Yoga improves posture and helps us stay happy and active.
Enough sleep takes away tiredness and helps us feel fresh.
activities.explanation: Exercise, yoga and sleep all help your body.

activities.prompt: A child exercises regularly but sleeps too little. How can the child stay strong, energetic and fresh?
steps: Playing and running help us stay strong and energetic because these are physical activities.
A child who sleeps too little may feel tired and find work or play hard to focus on.
A good sleep takes away tiredness and makes us feel fresh.
So regular exercise and enough sleep are both important for staying healthy.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which set contains only physical activities?
options: playing, running and cycling
posture, happiness and sleep
strength, energy and food
activities.explanation: Playing, running and cycling are physical activities.

activities.prompt: A good sleep helps you feel ______.
activities.hint: You feel lively after a good sleep.
activities.explanation: Good sleep takes away tiredness and makes you feel fresh.

activities.prompt: Which group describes how you may feel without enough sleep?
options: tired, sleepy and irritable
fresh, happy and active
strong, energetic and healthy
activities.explanation: Without enough sleep, you may feel tired, sleepy and irritable.

activities.prompt: Put the yoga activities in order.
activities.explanation: Practise easy yoga poses for a week and then record your observations.

activities.prompt: What does a good sleep do?
options: It takes away tiredness and helps you feel fresh.
It improves your posture and helps you stay happy.
It provides many interesting exercises and games.
activities.explanation: Good sleep takes away tiredness and makes you feel fresh.

activities.prompt: Not getting enough sleep can make it hard to ______ on work or play.
activities.hint: Your mind finds it difficult to pay attention.
activities.explanation: Not getting enough sleep makes it difficult to focus on work or play.

activities.prompt: Physical activities make us strong and energetic. A body needs sufficient sleep every day. What may happen if a child runs daily but sleeps very little?
options: The child may feel tired and find play hard.
The child may stay energetic and feel fresh all day.
The child may feel sleepy but never feel tired.
The child may have more energy for running and jumping.

why.The child may stay energetic and feel fr: This wrongly assumes exercise alone can replace sleep.
why.The child may feel sleepy but never feel: Not sleeping enough can cause tiredness as well as sleepiness.
why.The child may have more energy for runni: This wrongly assumes exercise removes the effects of too little sleep.

activities.explanation: This matches the facts about tiredness and difficulty focusing on play.

activities.prompt: Yoga can improve our posture. We can practise easy poses for a week. Which plan is fairest?
options: Practise easy poses once and record posture.
Practise easy poses for a week and record posture.
Practise running and jumping for a week, then record posture.
Practise easy poses for a week without recording observations.

why.Practise easy poses once and record post: One day is shorter than the suggested week of practice.
why.Practise running and jumping for a week,: Running and jumping do not test yoga's effect on posture.
why.Practise easy poses for a week without r: Without an observation, the plan cannot check the posture change.

activities.explanation: It uses the suggested practice and checks posture over a week.

activities.prompt: A child played running today. The child says, 'So I can skip sleep.' Which reason shows the flaw?
options: Exercise helps us stay strong, but sleep is also needed.
Exercise alone removes tiredness, so sleep is not needed.
Sleep is needed only when a child plays sports.
Good sleep is less important than healthy food.

why.Exercise alone removes tiredness, so sle: This wrongly says exercise removes the need for sleep.
why.Sleep is needed only when a child plays: This wrongly says sleep matters only after sports.
why.Good sleep is less important than health: This wrongly makes sleep less important than healthy food.

activities.explanation: Exercise is important, but enough sleep is just as important.

activities.prompt: Not getting enough sleep makes it hard to focus on work or play. Which comparison is fairest?
options: Compare play focus after enough sleep and after too little sleep.
Compare play focus after running and after jumping.
Compare play focus after yoga and after no yoga.
Compare play focus after good sleep and after good food.

why.Compare play focus after running and aft: This compares activities instead of testing sleep.
why.Compare play focus after yoga and after: This compares yoga instead of testing sleep.
why.Compare play focus after good sleep and: This changes food and sleep together, so sleep is not tested alone.

activities.explanation: It changes sleep while keeping the focus task the same.

lessons.title: Feeling Safe and Healthy Living

activities.prompt: How can we tell what feels safe, and who can we tell?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Staying Safe and Feeling Well
activities.body: You may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable. Safe touch helps you feel happy and comfortable. Unsafe touch may make you feel uneasy, scared or confused. It can come from someone you know or a stranger. Speak up whenever you feel unsafe. Say ‘No’ and tell a trusted adult, such as your teacher. You do not have to feel guilty. Eat right, rest, relax, and care for your body and mind.
keyPoints: Safe touch helps you feel happy and comfortable.
Speak up whenever you feel unsafe.
Healthy living includes eating right, activity, rest and relaxation.
activities.explanation: Good choices help you speak up and care for your body and mind.

activities.prompt: What should you do if a family hug feels uncomfortable?
steps: The hug may be unsafe touch because you feel uncomfortable.
You should say ‘No’, because you should speak up when unsafe.
Tell your teacher, because a teacher can be a trusted adult.
Do not feel guilty, because speaking up when unsafe is important.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Speak Up
activities.prompt: What should you do whenever you feel unsafe?
options: Speak up.
Keep it secret.
Wait silently.
Laugh it off.
activities.explanation: Speaking up helps a trusted adult know that you feel unsafe.

activities.title: A Family Hug
activities.prompt: A hug from a family member can be a safe touch.
activities.explanation: A family hug can be safe touch and make you feel comfortable.

activities.title: Say Your Choice
activities.prompt: When you feel unsafe, you can say ‘______’ and tell a trusted adult.
activities.hint: Use the short word for refusing.
activities.explanation: Saying ‘No’ and telling a trusted adult are ways to speak up.

activities.title: Make the Match
activities.prompt: Match each idea to its correct partner.
activities.explanation: Safe touch supports comfort. Unsafe touch can feel uneasy. A teacher can be trusted.

activities.title: Unsafe Touch
activities.prompt: Who may give unsafe touch?
options: Someone you know
A stranger
Both people
Only strangers
activities.explanation: Unsafe touch can come from someone you know or from a stranger.

activities.title: Feeling Guilty
activities.prompt: You should feel guilty when unsafe touch happens.
activities.explanation: You do not have to feel uncomfortable or guilty about unsafe touch.

activities.title: Healthy Choices
activities.prompt: Which choice supports healthy living?
options: Eat right, rest and relax.
Eat at any time in any way.
Rest without eating or moving.
Care only for your body.
activities.explanation: Eating right, physical activity, rest and relaxation all support healthy living.

activities.prompt: A family member hugs you, and you feel happy and comfortable. Which thought fits best?
options: A family hug can be safe when it feels comfortable.
Every family hug is safe, even an uncomfortable one.
No family hug can ever feel comfortable.
Only hugs from strangers can feel comfortable.

why.Every family hug is safe, even an uncomf: This wrongly assumes every family hug is safe.
This wrongly assumes family hugs cannot feel comfortable.
why.Only hugs from strangers can feel comfor: The family hug already feels comfortable, so this is wrong.

activities.explanation: A family hug can be safe, and comfortable feelings fit safe touch.

activities.prompt: Someone you do not know touches you. You feel uneasy. What should you do?
options: Say ‘No’ and tell your teacher.
Keep quiet because the person is a stranger.
Smile because all stranger touches are safe.
Wait because unsafe touches soon feel comfortable.

why.Keep quiet because the person is a stran: This wrongly assumes a stranger cannot make you feel unsafe.
why.Smile because all stranger touches are s: This wrongly assumes every stranger touch is safe.
why.Wait because unsafe touches soon feel co: This wrongly assumes unsafe touch must soon feel comfortable.

activities.explanation: Unsafe touch can come from a stranger, and you should speak up.

activities.prompt: Explain why people feel happy at different times and for different reasons.
activities.answer: People feel happy sometimes, but not all at the same time. They also feel happy for different reasons. Eating a favourite food is one happy occasion, so one food may make one person happy while another person is happy about a different food.
points: Everyone feels happy sometimes.
People feel happy at different times.
People have different reasons for happiness.
Eating a favourite food can be a happy occasion.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A farmer sows a seed, and water, soil and sunlight help a grain grow. Farmers, sellers and other people make the grain's long journey from the farm to our plate possible, while animals also help. The journey from sowing the seed to food on our plate is remarkable. People remember every contributor with love and gratitude, which makes them feel the importance of each grain and helps them enjoy its taste.
activities.prompt: If the grain did not receive enough water, what would most likely happen?
options: It would not grow well.
It would grow as long as it received sunlight.
Farmers would not need to sow a seed.
Sellers would bring it to the plate before it grew.

why.It would grow as long as it received sun: Sunlight alone cannot replace the need for water.
A seed still needs to be sown before a grain can grow.
why.Sellers would bring it to the plate befo: A grain must grow before it becomes food.

activities.explanation: Water plays an important part in helping grain grow.

activities.context: A farmer sows a seed, and water, soil and sunlight help a grain grow. Farmers, sellers and other people make the grain's long journey from the farm to our plate possible, while animals also help. The journey from sowing the seed to food on our plate is remarkable. People remember every contributor with love and gratitude, which makes them feel the importance of each grain and helps them enjoy its taste.
activities.prompt: How should people show gratitude after enjoying the food?
options: Thank everyone who helped bring the grain to the plate.
Thank only farmers because they begin the journey.
Thank only the food and ignore all contributors.
Wait until another festival before showing gratitude.

why.Thank only farmers because they begin th: Farmers are important, but they are not the only contributors.
why.Thank only the food and ignore all contr: Showing gratitude includes remembering all contributors.
why.Wait until another festival before showi: Gratitude can be shown whenever people enjoy the food.

activities.explanation: Many people, animals and natural resources contribute to the journey.

activities.context: The teacher asked the students to sit in a circle and close their eyes. She placed one peanut on each student’s palm. As they ate, they put the food into their mouths slowly. Their tongues and mouths felt the peanut’s surface, while their teeth chewed it gently. They focused on its flavour, taste and texture, remembering the taste as they continued to chew. Before swallowing, they remembered its texture.
activities.prompt: After feeling the peanut’s surface, a student swallows it quickly. What is the student most likely to lose?
options: Time to remember the food’s texture before swallowing
The ability to feel the peanut’s flavour and taste
The help their teeth give while chewing
The chance to appreciate the food and enjoy each bite

why.The ability to feel the peanut’s flavour: Quick eating does not remove all taste.
why.The help their teeth give while chewing: The teeth can still help with chewing.
why.The chance to appreciate the food and en: Rushing reduces attention to the bite.

activities.explanation: Texture should be remembered before swallowing.

activities.context: The teacher asked the students to sit in a circle and close their eyes. She placed one peanut on each student’s palm. As they ate, they put the food into their mouths slowly. Their tongues and mouths felt the peanut’s surface, while their teeth chewed it gently. They focused on its flavour, taste and texture, remembering the taste as they continued to chew. Before swallowing, they remembered its texture.
activities.prompt: What should the student do to get the most from the next bite?
options: Slow down, chew well and focus on the bite.
Swallow immediately to avoid remembering texture.
Chew quickly so the flavour disappears.
Keep eating without noticing each bite.

why.Swallow immediately to avoid remembering: The texture should be remembered before swallowing.
Quick chewing does not support mindful eating.
Mindful eating requires attention to each bite.

activities.explanation: Slow, mindful eating supports enjoyment.

activities.prompt: How does mindful eating help us enjoy our food?
activities.answer: Mindful eating means paying attention to what and how we eat. By eating slowly and focusing on each bite, we can feel flavour, taste and texture. This helps us enjoy our food better, make healthier choices and appreciate what we are eating.
points: Pays attention to what and how we eat
Eats slowly and focuses on each bite
Notices flavour, taste and texture
Supports enjoyment and appreciation
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student wants to show that food is valued. The student makes a food record for one week, writing an entry after breakfast, lunch and dinner. If everything is eaten, the student writes “Yes” and draws a happy smiley. If some food is left, the student writes “No” and draws a sad face. The student uses the record to think about the hard work behind the food.
activities.prompt: If the student eats everything at dinner, which entry and mark should be made?
options: A “Yes” entry with a happy smiley
A “No” entry with a sad face
A “Yes” entry with a sad face
A “No” entry with a happy smiley

why.A “No” entry with a sad face: A “No” entry and sad face are used when some food is left.
why.A “Yes” entry with a sad face: A “Yes” entry should have a happy smiley, not a sad face.
why.A “No” entry with a happy smiley: A “No” entry is for food that was left, so it should not have a happy smiley.

activities.explanation: Correct: everything was eaten, so the entry is “Yes” with a happy smiley.

activities.context: A student wants to show that food is valued. The student makes a food record for one week, writing an entry after breakfast, lunch and dinner. If everything is eaten, the student writes “Yes” and draws a happy smiley. If some food is left, the student writes “No” and draws a sad face. The student uses the record to think about the hard work behind the food.
activities.prompt: If the student misses one dinner entry, what will the record no longer be able to show?
options: Whether the food at that dinner was eaten or left
That the food record was kept for one week
That every meal was fully eaten
That the student made an entry after every meal

why.That the food record was kept for one we: The record can still show that it was kept for one week.
why.That every meal was fully eaten: Other entries cannot prove that every meal was fully eaten.
why.That the student made an entry after eve: Missing one entry means the record cannot show an entry after every meal.

activities.explanation: Correct: without that entry, the record cannot show whether food was eaten or left at that dinner.

activities.prompt: Explain why wasting food does not respect the hard work behind it.
activities.answer: Wasting food does not respect the hard work behind it. Everyone who helped bring food to our plate has worked hard. Every grain is precious, so when food is left behind, we are not showing respect for the food or for the work that brought it to us.
points: Food that is left behind is wasted
The hard work behind food matters
Everyone who helped bring food has worked hard
Every grain is precious
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student enjoys Khel Yoga exercises and games, but often does not get enough sleep. The student feels tired and sleepy, has trouble focusing on work or play, and becomes irritable. The student also runs and jumps on some days. Yoga helps with posture and staying happy and active, but getting enough sleep is as important as eating healthy and exercising.
activities.prompt: If the student continues getting too little sleep, what is most likely to happen?
options: Schoolwork and play may become harder to handle.
Schoolwork and play will become easier to focus on.
The student will always feel fresh and energetic.
The student will need less sleep each day.

why.Schoolwork and play will become easier t: Enough sleep supports focus, so this is the opposite effect.
why.The student will always feel fresh and e: Lack of sleep may cause tiredness rather than constant freshness.
why.The student will need less sleep each da: The body still requires sufficient sleep every day.

activities.explanation: Not enough sleep can make focus difficult.

activities.context: A student enjoys Khel Yoga exercises and games, but often does not get enough sleep. The student feels tired and sleepy, has trouble focusing on work or play, and becomes irritable. The student also runs and jumps on some days. Yoga helps with posture and staying happy and active, but getting enough sleep is as important as eating healthy and exercising.
activities.prompt: The student wants to improve posture while staying happy and active. What should they practise?
options: Choose yoga to support posture, happiness and activity.
Choose only running, with no yoga at all.
Choose extra sleep in place of any physical activity.
Choose no activity while waiting for better health.

why.Choose only running, with no yoga at all: Running supports strength and energy but is not given as a posture exercise.
why.Choose extra sleep in place of any physi: Sleep and physical activity both matter, so one should not replace the other.
why.Choose no activity while waiting for bet: Doing nothing would not support strength, energy or activity.

activities.explanation: Yoga supports better posture and helps people stay happy and active.

activities.prompt: Explain why regular physical activity and sufficient sleep are both important for health.
activities.answer: Regular exercise helps us stay strong and energetic. Sufficient sleep takes away tiredness and makes us feel fresh. Not getting enough sleep can make it difficult to focus on work or play and can make us feel tired, sleepy and irritable. Therefore, exercising regularly and sleeping enough are both important for staying healthy.
points: Exercise supports strength and energy.
Sleep removes tiredness and restores freshness.
Lack of sleep can affect focus and feelings.
Both habits are important for health.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Sometimes a person may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable. A student feels uneasy and confused when a stranger touches her arm. She knows that unsafe touch can come from someone we know or from a stranger. When she feels unsafe, she says ‘No’ and tells her teacher, a trusted adult. She does not have to feel uncomfortable or guilty. Taking care of her body and mind helps her stay happy, healthy and joyful.
activities.prompt: She feels unsafe again and worries about being blamed. What should she do?
options: Speak up and ask her teacher for help without blaming herself.
Wait quietly and hope that the unsafe feeling passes.
Apologize for feeling unsafe so that nobody becomes uncomfortable.
Tell only the person who made her feel unsafe and keep it secret from adults.

why.Wait quietly and hope that the unsafe fe: Staying quiet may leave her feeling unsafe and unsupported.
why.Apologize for feeling unsafe so that nob: She does not have to feel guilty about her feelings.
why.Tell only the person who made her feel u: A trusted adult should be told when she feels unsafe.

activities.explanation: Speaking up and telling a trusted adult is the right action.

activities.context: Sometimes a person may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable. A student feels uneasy and confused when a stranger touches her arm. She knows that unsafe touch can come from someone we know or from a stranger. When she feels unsafe, she says ‘No’ and tells her teacher, a trusted adult. She does not have to feel uncomfortable or guilty. Taking care of her body and mind helps her stay happy, healthy and joyful.
activities.prompt: If a family member gives her a welcome hug and she feels happy and comfortable, what does this show?
options: The welcome family hug is a safe touch.
The hug must be unsafe because she felt uneasy earlier.
The hug is unsafe because the person giving it is a family member.
The hug is unsafe because it is physical touch.

why.The hug must be unsafe because she felt: Her earlier unease was about the stranger’s touch.
why.The hug is unsafe because the person giv: A hug from a family member can be safe.
why.The hug is unsafe because it is physical: Physical touch is not automatically unsafe.

activities.explanation: A welcome hug from a family member can be a safe touch.

activities.context: Sometimes a person may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable. A student feels uneasy and confused when a stranger touches her arm. She knows that unsafe touch can come from someone we know or from a stranger. When she feels unsafe, she says ‘No’ and tells her teacher, a trusted adult. She does not have to feel uncomfortable or guilty. Taking care of her body and mind helps her stay happy, healthy and joyful.
activities.prompt: After telling her teacher, how can she support healthy living?
options: Eat right, be physically active, and take time for rest and relaxation.
Eat whenever she wants, however she wants, and skip physical activity.
Only do physical activities and leave out rest and relaxation.
Only focus on food and leave out physical activity and relaxation.

why.Eat whenever she wants, however she want: Eating must be done at the right time and in the right way.
why.Only do physical activities and leave ou: Rest and relaxation are as important as physical activities.
why.Only focus on food and leave out physica: Healthy living balances all these parts instead of focusing on one.

activities.explanation: Healthy living includes food, activity, rest, and relaxation.

activities.prompt: Explain why it is important to know the difference between safe and unsafe touch.
activities.answer: A safe touch helps a person feel happy and comfortable, while an unsafe touch may cause uneasiness, fear, confusion, or discomfort. Unsafe touch may happen with someone familiar or with a stranger. If a touch feels wrong, the person should say ‘No’ and tell a trusted adult without feeling guilty.
points: Safe touch makes us feel happy and comfortable.
Unsafe touch may cause uneasy, scared, confused, or uncomfortable feelings.
Unsafe touch can come from someone known or a stranger.
The person can say ‘No’ and tell a trusted adult without guilt.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

chapters.summary: In this chapter: everyday things and first spins; making and testing spinners; charkha, shapes and spinning colours; floating and sinking.

lessons.title: Everyday Things and First Spins

activities.prompt: What makes our everyday things spin?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Things Around Us
activities.body: We use many things around us every day. A pencil helps us write, while a bag carries books. Meera and Dhruv love exploring how things work. Meera spun a coin and noticed that it shook as it slowed down. Coins and bangles can spin, but erasers do not spin properly. Meera also wanted to know how a top spins.
keyPoints: Some everyday things help us work.
A bag carries books, and a pencil helps us write.
Coins and bangles can spin.
Meera asks questions about how things work.
activities.explanation: This lesson connects everyday things with questions about spinning.

activities.prompt: Meera spins a coin and it slows down. What should she explore?
steps: Meera watches the coin closely because she loves exploring how things work.
The coin begins to shake as it slows down, so she notices the movement.
She asks why the shaking happens because the change makes her curious.
Her first investigation asks why the coin shakes as it slows down.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: A Useful Tool
activities.prompt: Which thing do you use for writing?
options: A bangle
A coin
A pencil
A bag
activities.explanation: The lesson says a pencil is used for writing.

activities.title: Things and Their Uses
activities.prompt: Match each thing to what it does.
activities.explanation: The pairs show each thing's use or spinning action.

activities.title: A Spinning Eraser
activities.prompt: Erasers spin properly.
activities.explanation: Erasers do not spin properly, so this statement is false.

activities.title: A Weekly Discovery
activities.prompt: Meera and Dhruv find something new to explore every ______.
activities.hint: It is a special part of the week when they discover something new.
activities.explanation: Meera and Dhruv discover something new to explore every weekend.

activities.title: The Shaking Coin
activities.prompt: Why did the coin begin to shake?
options: It slowed down.
It became warmer.
It changed colour.
It grew smaller.
activities.explanation: The coin began to shake as it slowed down.

activities.title: Meera's Coin
activities.prompt: Put Meera's coin events in the correct order.
activities.explanation: Meera first spun the coin, then wondered why it shook.

activities.title: A Curious Question
activities.prompt: Meera wanted to know how a top spins.
activities.explanation: The lesson says Meera wanted to know how a top spins.

activities.title: The Next Question
activities.prompt: What did Meera want to know about a top?
options: how it carries books
how it is used for writing
how it slows down
how it spins
activities.explanation: The lesson says Meera wanted to know how a top spins.

activities.prompt: A coin slows after Meera spins it. What happens next?
options: The coin begins to shake.
The coin starts spinning faster.
The coin becomes completely still.
The coin begins to roll away.

This mistake thinks shaking means the coin speeds up.
This mistake ignores the shaking that happens during slowing.
This mistake mistakes spinning for rolling away.

activities.explanation: This is right because the coin shakes as it slows down.

activities.prompt: Meera needs to write and carry books. Which pair helps her?
options: A pencil and a bag.
A coin and a bangle.
An eraser and a coin.
A bangle and a bag.

This mistake chooses spinning objects instead of work helpers.
This mistake does not choose the pencil used for writing.
This mistake chooses a bangle without a stated work job.

activities.explanation: This is right because a pencil writes and a bag carries books.

lessons.title: Making and Testing Spinners

activities.prompt: What could make a homemade spinner spin smoothly and stay upright?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Make and Test Spinners
activities.body: Make spinners from cardboard, toothpicks and small objects. An empty ballpoint pen tube can be used. Make a spinner with a toothpick at its centre and another with it away from its centre. The first spinner looks the same from all sides and remains upright while it spins. The second behaves differently. Spin the spinners and record observations. Changes in toothpick length or cardboard alignment can help spinners spin better.
keyPoints: Cardboard, toothpicks, small objects and an empty ballpoint pen tube can be used.
The first spinner has a centre toothpick and remains upright.
Observations help you check how each spinner behaves.
Changing toothpick length or cardboard alignment can help a spinner spin better.
activities.explanation: These steps help you build, test and improve your spinners.

activities.prompt: A child’s spinner does not work properly. How can the child help it spin better?
steps: The child checks the spinner because some spinners might not work properly.
The child changes the toothpick length below the cardboard because this can help.
The child changes the cardboard alignment because this can also help.
The child spins it, records observations, and checks whether it spins better.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: The spinners should be spun, and their observations should be recorded.
activities.explanation: Yes. Spinning and recording observations helps you check how your spinners behave.

activities.prompt: The first spinner has a ______ at its centre.
activities.hint: Name the part placed at the centre.
activities.explanation: The first spinner has a toothpick at its centre. The other spinner has it away from its centre.

activities.prompt: Match each item to its description.
pairs: Looks the same from all sides
Does not behave in the same way
activities.explanation: The first spinner looks the same from all sides and stays upright. The second spinner behaves differently.

activities.prompt: Where are the toothpicks in the first and second spinners?
options: Away from it and at the centre
At the centre and at the centre
Away from it and away from it
At the centre and away from it
activities.explanation: The first spinner has a toothpick at its centre. The second spinner has its toothpick away from the centre.

activities.prompt: Put the spinner-testing steps in order.
activities.explanation: First make the spinners. Then spin them and record what you observe.

activities.prompt: The second spinner remains upright while it spins.
activities.explanation: The first spinner remains upright while it spins. The second spinner does not behave in the same way.

activities.prompt: A spinner does not work properly. What can help it spin better?
options: Use an empty ballpoint pen tube instead
Spin each spinner and record observations
Place one toothpick at the centre
Change toothpick length or cardboard alignment
activities.explanation: Changing the toothpick length or cardboard alignment can help a spinner spin better. Great choice!

activities.prompt: One spinner has its toothpick at the centre. What is the child likely to observe?
options: It stays upright while it spins.
It looks different from all sides.
It behaves like the off-centre spinner.
It might not work properly.

The first spinner looks the same from all sides, not different.
The off-centre spinner is the one that behaves differently.
Some spinners might fail, but the centre spinner stays upright.

activities.explanation: This matches the first spinner, which stays upright while spinning.

activities.prompt: A spinner is not working properly. Which changes can help it spin better?
options: Change the toothpick length and change the cardboard alignment.
Change the toothpick length and change the first spinner’s shape.
Change the cardboard alignment and change the second spinner’s centre.
Change the first spinner’s centre and change the second spinner’s shape.

why.Change the toothpick length and change t: It confuses changing a part with changing a spinner’s shape.
why.Change the cardboard alignment and chang: It confuses changing alignment with changing a spinner’s centre.
why.Change the first spinner’s centre and ch: It mixes up the spinners and ignores the two useful changes.

activities.explanation: These are the two changes that can help a spinner.

lessons.title: Charkha, Shapes and Spinning Colours

activities.prompt: What secrets might a spinning shape reveal to curious eyes?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How Things Spin
activities.body: A charkha twists cotton fibre into thread. Its large wheel spins when you turn it by hand. Mahatma Gandhi used charkhas to make handmade clothes. A square card can appear circular while it spins. Spinners can be made from card pieces of different shapes. You can colour them and observe their colours. A lattu is a popular Indian top, commonly made of wood.
keyPoints: A charkha twists cotton fibre into thread.
A square card can appear circular while spinning.
Spinners can be made and coloured.
A lattu is a popular Indian wooden top.
activities.explanation: Charkhas, cards and tops all show us how things can spin.

activities.prompt: A child makes a colourful square card spinner and wants to know what can be seen while it spins.
steps: The child makes a spinner from a square card, because spinners can use card pieces of different shapes.
The child colours the spinner, because spinners can be coloured in different ways.
The child spins the coloured spinner and watches, because colours on a spinning spinner can be observed.
The child sees the square card appear circular, because a square card appears circular while it is spinning.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

It twists cotton fibre.
It colours card pieces.
It spins ceiling fans.

options: A few hours
Several days
Thousands of years
A short while

options: Thread
Wood
Card pieces
Clay

options: Wood
Clay
Thread
Card pieces

activities.prompt: Which chain shows how Gandhi could make handmade clothes with a charkha?
options: Press the clay; shape the top
Spin the top; shape the wood
Turn the wheel; twist the fibre
Colour the card; spin the fan

activities.prompt: A child says, "Only square card pieces can make spinners." Why is this claim wrong?
options: Spinners can use card pieces of different shapes.
Spinners can only use cotton fibre as card pieces.
Spinners must all use the same wooden shape.
Spinners can hide every kind of card shape.

why.Spinners can only use cotton fibre as ca: This wrongly thinks spinners are made from cotton fibre.
why.Spinners must all use the same wooden sh: This confuses a wooden lattu with a card spinner.
why.Spinners can hide every kind of card sha: This wrongly thinks spinners cannot show card shapes.

activities.prompt: Four coloured spinners are ready. How should the children observe their colours fairly?
options: Spin each spinner and watch its colours.
Hold each spinner still and watch its colours.
Paint each spinner again before watching it.
Use a charkha to spin each colour.

why.Hold each spinner still and watch its co: This thinks colours should be watched on a still spinner.
why.Paint each spinner again before watching: This changes the colours before the fair test.
This uses a thread-making tool instead of the spinners.

activities.prompt: Spinning tops have been used in India for thousands of years. A child says clay is still the usual material for lattu. What should the child learn?

Wood made earlier tops, but common lattu is made of clay.
Clay made earlier tops, but common lattu is made of card.
Clay made earlier tops, but common lattu is made of fibre.

why.Wood made earlier tops, but common lattu: This reverses the earlier and modern materials.
why.Clay made earlier tops, but common lattu: This mistakes card for the usual lattu material.
This mistakes cotton fibre for the usual lattu material.

activities.explanation: Clay was used earlier, but common lattu is made of wood.

lessons.title: Floating and Sinking

activities.prompt: What makes an object float or sink in water?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Float or Sink?
activities.body: Leaves float, while heavy iron nails sink. Weight alone does not decide whether an object floats or sinks. Children can test many objects. They should guess before dropping each object into water. Then they check whether it floats or sinks. The letter F means float, and S means sink.
keyPoints: Leaves float; heavy iron nails sink.
Weight alone does not decide the result.
Guess, drop, then check.
F means float; S means sink.
activities.explanation: Thinking before you test helps you notice what actually happens.

activities.title: Float or sink?

tasks.then: It is now denser than water, so it sinks.

activities.takeaway: Things lighter than water for their size float; denser things sink.
activities.explanation: Things lighter than water for their size float; denser things sink.

activities.prompt: A child chooses a leaf and a heavy iron nail. How can the child test which one floats and which one sinks?
steps: Choose a leaf and a heavy iron nail, because both can be tested.
Guess before dropping them, because the child should guess first.
Drop each object into a bucket of water, because this is the water test.
Mark the leaf F and the nail S, because F shows floating and S shows sinking.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where did the rain water gather?
options: in a puddle
in a bucket
