lessons.title: In the Land of Agriculture, with Gurpreet

activities.prompt: What will Gurpreet show us about Amritsar’s land, food, and Golden Temple?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Farming and Food in Amritsar
activities.body: In Amritsar's plains, you can see large fields where many people work in farming. The soil is rich and fertile. People enjoy makki di roti and sarson da saag. Makki di roti uses corn flour, while sarson da saag uses mustard leaves. The Golden Temple is also called Sri Harmandir Sahib. It has a gold-plated structure. A serene water tank surrounds it. Volunteers cook, serve meals and wash dishes.
keyPoints: Large fields in Amritsar have rich, fertile soil.
Many people work in farming and enjoy local dishes.
Langar sewa volunteers cook, serve meals and wash dishes.
activities.explanation: This lesson connects farming, local food and service at the Golden Temple.

activities.prompt: Gurpreet sees farm work in Amritsar’s plains, then eats makki di roti and sarson da saag. Why are land and food connected there?
steps: Large fields and rich, fertile soil make the plains suitable for farming.
Many people in the region work in farming, so agriculture is a common part of life.
Makki di roti uses corn flour, while sarson da saag uses mustard leaves.
These foods connect farming with what people eat, so agriculture shapes daily life there.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Golden Temple and Langar Sewa
activities.body: The Golden Temple is also called Sri Harmandir Sahib. It is one of India's most famous Gurudwaras. It has a gold-plated structure. A serene water tank surrounds the temple. The temple offers langar sewa, a community kitchen service. Volunteers cook meals, serve them and wash dishes. It is part of one of the world's largest community service operations.
keyPoints: Sri Harmandir Sahib is another name for the Golden Temple.
A serene water tank surrounds the gold-plated structure.
Langar sewa is a community kitchen service run with volunteers.
activities.explanation: The Golden Temple is famous for its structure, setting and community service.

activities.title: Good Farming Land
activities.prompt: What makes the plains of Amritsar good for farming?
options: Rich, fertile soil
Deep, rocky soil
Cold, dry soil
Salty, sandy soil
activities.explanation: The plains have large fields and rich, fertile soil.

activities.title: Corn Flour
activities.prompt: Makki di roti is made with corn flour.
activities.explanation: Yes, makki di roti is made with corn flour.

activities.title: The Flour in Makki di Roti
activities.prompt: Makki di roti is made with ______ flour.
activities.hint: Think of the grain used for makki di roti.
activities.explanation: Makki di roti is made with corn flour.

activities.title: Match Each Name
activities.prompt: Match each name with its correct detail.
activities.explanation: Each dish, place and service has a correct matching detail.

activities.title: Helping at Langar Sewa
activities.prompt: Who helps with langar sewa at the Golden Temple?
options: Volunteers
Farmers
Tourists
Shopkeepers
activities.explanation: Volunteers cook, serve meals and wash dishes.

activities.title: Langar Sewa Tasks
activities.prompt: Put the langar sewa tasks in the order they happen.
activities.explanation: Meals are cooked before serving, and washing happens afterwards.

activities.prompt: In Amritsar’s plains, there are large fields and rich, fertile soil. What does this show about agriculture?
options: Many people in this region work in farming.
Many people in this region serve community meals.
Many people in this region wash temple dishes.
Many people in this region grow mustard leaves.

why.Many people in this region serve communi: This mistake connects farming with the temple’s community meals.
why.Many people in this region wash temple d: This mistake connects farming with volunteers washing dishes.
why.Many people in this region grow mustard: This mistake treats mustard leaves in a dish as farm work.

activities.explanation: The large fields, fertile soil, and farm work fit together.

activities.prompt: Makki di roti uses corn flour. Sarson da saag uses mustard leaves. If a cook swaps the ingredients, what happens?
options: Both dishes lose their correct main ingredients.
Both dishes keep their correct ingredients because names stay.
Only sarson da saag loses its correct main ingredient.
Only makki di roti loses its correct main ingredient.

why.Both dishes keep their correct ingredien: This mistake thinks dish names can keep the wrong ingredients.
why.Only sarson da saag loses its correct ma: This mistake overlooks the corn flour being swapped out.
why.Only makki di roti loses its correct mai: This mistake overlooks the mustard leaves being swapped out.

activities.explanation: Swapping the ingredients puts the wrong main ingredient in each dish.

activities.prompt: The Golden Temple has a gold-plated structure. A serene water tank surrounds it. What should a visitor notice?
options: The gold-plated building stands inside calm surrounding water.
The gold-plated building stands inside a field of corn.
The gold-plated building stands inside a busy meal service.
The gold-plated building stands inside a field of mustard leaves.

why.The gold-plated building stands inside a: This mistake mixes the water tank with a corn field.
This mistake mixes the water tank with the community kitchen.
This mistake mixes the water tank with mustard-leaf fields.

activities.explanation: The gold-plated structure really stands inside the serene surrounding tank.

activities.prompt: The Golden Temple offers langar sewa. Volunteers cook, serve meals, and wash dishes. What happens if the dish-washing job is missed?
options: The used dishes stay dirty after the meal.
The served meals become dirty before cooking.
The water tank becomes dirty instead of the dishes.
The gold-plated structure becomes dull instead of the dishes.

why.The served meals become dirty before coo: This mistake moves the washing problem to the meals before cooking.
why.The water tank becomes dirty instead of: This mistake moves the washing problem to the surrounding water tank.
why.The gold-plated structure becomes dull i: This mistake moves the washing problem to the gold-plated structure.

activities.explanation: Without washing, the used dishes remain dirty after the meal.

activities.prompt: The Golden Temple has one of the world’s largest community service operations. Volunteers cook, serve meals, and wash dishes. Why do volunteers need different jobs?
options: Cooking, serving, and washing are all needed.
Only cooking is needed, since meals must be made.
Only serving is needed, since meals are already made.
Only washing is needed, since dishes need care.

why.Only cooking is needed, since meals must: This mistake thinks cooking is enough and overlooks serving and washing.
why.Only serving is needed, since meals are: This mistake thinks serving is enough and overlooks cooking and washing.
why.Only washing is needed, since dishes nee: This mistake thinks washing is enough and overlooks cooking and serving.

activities.explanation: The large service needs people to cook, serve, and wash.

lessons.title: In the Land of Endless Sand, with Ritika

activities.prompt: What helps people, plants, and animals survive in a desert?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Discovering Desert Life
activities.body: Deserts are dry places with very little rainfall. Cactus, khejri and babool grow there and need very little water. Cactus stores water in its stems. Camels live there. Traditional houses have mud walls, thatched roofs and water tanks called tankas. Rajasthani women wear colourful clothes while dancing. Rajasthani men wear turbans and play instruments. Jaisalmer Fort is a desert fort.
keyPoints: Deserts have very little rainfall.
Desert plants survive with very little water.
Rajasthani people wear colourful clothes and play instruments.
activities.explanation: These clues help you learn about desert life.

activities.prompt: A gardener gives a cactus very little water. Why might the cactus stay alive?
steps: Deserts have very little rainfall, so the place is dry.
Cactus can survive there because desert plants survive with very little water.
It stores water in its stem, keeping some water for dry times.
So the cactus can live with the little water given.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which description tells you about a desert?
options: A dry place with very little rainfall
A wet place with heavy rainfall
A place with many mud houses
A place with coloured bangles
activities.explanation: A desert is a dry place with very little rainfall.

activities.prompt: Many desert houses have water tanks called ______.
activities.hint: These containers hold water in many desert houses.
activities.explanation: The water tanks in many desert houses are called tankas.

activities.prompt: Which animal is known as the ship of the desert?
options: Lizard
Camel
Python
Eagle
activities.explanation: The camel is known as the ship of the desert.

activities.prompt: Match each clue to its correct detail.
pairs: An example of a desert fort
activities.explanation: Rajasthani people wear colourful clothes and play instruments. Jaisalmer Fort is a desert fort.

activities.prompt: Which items are part of a traditional desert house?
options: Bangles, ghaghras and bandhini dupattas
Mud walls and thatched roofs
Colourful turbans, khartal and sarangi
Water tankas and Jaisalmer Fort
activities.explanation: Traditional desert houses have mud walls and thatched roofs.

activities.prompt: Match each clue to its correct detail from the lesson.
pairs: An example of a desert fort
activities.explanation: The clues connect desert animals, homes, forts and Rajasthani life.

activities.prompt: A cactus has water stored in its stem. The gardener gives it very little water. What will help it survive?
options: It can use the water stored in its stem.
It can drink the heavy rain every day.
It can store sand instead of water.
It can turn its stem into a tanka.

This assumes deserts have heavy rain every day.
This confuses stored water with stored sand.
This confuses a plant stem with a house tank.

activities.explanation: The stem already holds water that the cactus can use.

activities.prompt: Many desert houses have water tanks called tankas. Why are tankas helpful where rainfall is very little?
options: They save water for dry times.
They bring heavy rain indoors.
They make mud walls into sand.
They change the house into a fort.

This wrongly assumes tankas can bring heavy rain.
This wrongly assumes tanka water changes mud walls.
This confuses a water tank with a desert fort.

activities.explanation: Tankas keep water available when rainfall is very little.

activities.prompt: Camels, lizards, wild cats, pythons and eagles live in deserts. The camel is known as the ship of the desert. What does this name suggest?
options: The camel helps people travel across deserts.
The camel lives inside a water tank.
The camel wears colourful Rajasthani clothes.
The camel builds houses with mud walls.

This confuses the camel's home with a house's tank.
why.The camel wears colourful Rajasthani clo: This confuses the animal with Rajasthani dancers.
This confuses the animal with traditional desert houses.

activities.explanation: Calling it a ship suggests it carries people across deserts.

activities.prompt: Jaisalmer Fort is an example of a desert fort. A child says, “It is the only desert fort.” What mistake did the child make?
options: One example does not mean there are no others.
A desert fort must be a mud house.
Every desert fort must have a tanka.
A fort cannot stand in a desert.

The child has mixed up forts with traditional desert houses.
The child has wrongly applied a house fact to every fort.
The child has wrongly thought a desert fort cannot stand there.

activities.explanation: One example does not prove that no other desert fort exists.

lessons.title: On the Seashore, with Chandni

activities.prompt: What wonders might Chandni discover along Puri’s seashore?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Chandni Visits the Seashore
activities.body: Puri is a coastal city in Odisha. Its sandy beaches are famous for colourful sand art. Different sea shells can be found there. A shankh is a conch shell that is blown during pooja. During a boat ride, Chandni sees fishermen, turtles and other wonderful creatures. Fishing supports many people in coastal regions.
keyPoints: Puri is a coastal city in Odisha with sandy beaches.
Artists make sand art, and different sea shells can be found there.
A shankh is a conch shell blown during pooja.
Chandni sees sea creatures during a boat ride.
activities.explanation: Puri has sandy beaches, colourful art, sea shells and wonderful sea creatures.

activities.prompt: Chandni watches fishermen near the seashore. Why might the sea matter to coastal families?
steps: Chandni saw fishermen because they ride in boats on the sea.
Their work is fishing, so it helps provide a living.
Many coastal people depend on fishing for their living.
So the sea supports families as well as giving Chandni new sights to see.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Know Puri
activities.prompt: Which statement about Puri is correct?
options: It is a coastal city in Odisha.
It is a conch shell in Odisha.
It is a fishing boat in Odisha.
It is a sand art form in Odisha.
activities.explanation: Puri is a coastal city in Odisha. It is also famous for its sandy beaches.

activities.title: Sea Shells on the Beach
activities.prompt: Puri’s beaches have only one kind of sea shell.
activities.explanation: Different kinds of sea shells can be found on Puri’s beaches.

activities.title: Fishing and Livelihoods
activities.prompt: Why is fishing important in coastal regions?
options: It makes the beaches colourful.
It creates beautiful sand art.
Many people depend on it for their living.
It pulls huge temple chariots.
activities.explanation: Many people in coastal regions depend on fishing for their living.

activities.title: A Special Conch Shell
activities.prompt: During pooja, a conch shell called a ______ is blown.
activities.hint: This shell is a type of conch shell.
activities.explanation: A shankh is a conch shell that is blown during pooja.

activities.title: Match the Facts
activities.prompt: Match each word with its correct partner.
activities.explanation: Puri is in Odisha, artists make sand art, and a shankh is a conch shell.

activities.title: Traditional Dishes
activities.prompt: Which dishes are traditional in Odisha?
options: Dalma and pakhala
Sand art and chariots
Shells and fishing boats
Temple and sandy beach
activities.explanation: Dalma and pakhala are traditional dishes from Odisha.

activities.title: The Festival Chariots
activities.prompt: Thousands of people joyfully pull huge, colourful chariots during the festival.
activities.explanation: Thousands of people joyfully pull huge, colourful chariots during the festival.

activities.title: What People Pull
activities.prompt: What do thousands of people pull during the festival?
options: Small fishing boats
Beautiful sand pictures
Different sea shells
Huge colourful chariots
activities.explanation: Thousands of people joyfully pull huge, colourful chariots during the festival.

activities.prompt: A visitor sees Puri's popular temple and visits its sandy beach. Why?
options: Puri is coastal, with amazing sandy beaches and sand art.
Puri is coastal, but artists cover every sandy beach.
Puri's temple is popular, but Puri has no sandy beach.
Only sea shells can be found near Puri's temple.

why.Puri is coastal, but artists cover every: This mistake thinks artists cover beaches instead of creating art.
why.Puri's temple is popular, but Puri has n: This mistake thinks a popular temple means Puri has no beach.
why.Only sea shells can be found near Puri's: This mistake thinks shells replace all other sights.

activities.explanation: This is right because Puri is coastal and has amazing sandy beaches.

activities.prompt: Only sand art is special in Odisha. Why is this claim wrong?
options: Dalma and pakhala are also traditional Odisha dishes.
Sand art is also eaten as a traditional Odisha dish.
Sea shells are also traditional dishes in coastal Odisha.
Fishing boats are also called traditional Odisha dishes.

why.Sand art is also eaten as a traditional: This mistake treats sand art as food.
why.Sea shells are also traditional dishes i: This mistake treats sea shells as traditional meals.
why.Fishing boats are also called traditiona: This mistake treats fishing boats as traditional meals.

activities.explanation: This is right because dalma and pakhala are traditional Odisha dishes.

lessons.title: Living with Challenges

activities.prompt: How can people prepare for and stay safe during coastal storms?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Facing Challenges Together
activities.body: Coastal regions are places near the sea. People face several difficulties. Strong winds and cyclones often hit coastal regions of Odisha. Cyclones can harm people, animals and trees. They occur in coastal states from time to time. People study cyclones to find ways to protect lives and resources. Scientists, other people and the Government of Odisha work during cyclones. Early warnings, advance preparations and effective management help save people.
keyPoints: Coastal regions in Odisha face strong winds and cyclones.
Cyclones can harm people, animals and trees.
Warnings, preparations and management help protect lives.
activities.explanation: Communities study cyclones and work together to stay safe.

activities.prompt: A coastal family gets an early cyclone warning. How can people be protected?
steps: Odisha's coastal regions face strong winds and cyclones, so protection matters.
Early warnings help the government save people because they give time to act.
Scientists and other people work to protect lives and resources because cyclones can cause harm.
Therefore, early warnings, advance preparations, and effective management can help during cyclones.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Cyclones often hit the coastal regions of Odisha.
activities.explanation: Strong winds and cyclones often hit the coastal regions of Odisha.

activities.title: Why People Study Cyclones
activities.prompt: People study cyclones to find ways to protect lives and ______.
activities.hint: What do people protect besides lives?
activities.explanation: Studying cyclones helps people protect lives and resources.

activities.title: The Help of Early Warnings
activities.prompt: What do early warnings help the government do?
options: Save people during cyclones
Receive awards for saving people
Find ways to protect resources
Study cyclones from time to time
activities.explanation: Early warnings help the government save people during cyclones.

activities.title: From Danger to Response
activities.prompt: Put these events in order from the danger to the response.
items: Strong winds and cyclones hit coastal regions of Odisha
Cyclones can harm people, animals and trees
People find ways to protect lives and resources
activities.explanation: The danger comes first, and the protective response follows it.

activities.prompt: Only early warnings help during cyclones.
activities.explanation: Advance preparations and effective management also help during cyclones.

activities.title: Awards for Saving Lives
activities.prompt: For what has the Government of Odisha received awards?
options: Saving people during cyclones
Studying coastal regions
Protecting trees from winds
Managing coastal states
activities.explanation: The Government of Odisha received awards for saving people during cyclones.

activities.prompt: An early warning reaches Odisha's coastal towns before a cyclone. What should the government do next?
options: Use the warning to help save people before the cyclone.
Wait until the cyclone passes before telling anyone what to do.
Stop all strong winds before people have enough time to prepare.
Give an award before deciding how to protect people.

why.Wait until the cyclone passes before tel: This mistake waits until the danger has passed.
why.Stop all strong winds before people have: This mistake believes warnings can stop strong winds completely.
why.Give an award before deciding how to pro: This mistake puts awards before protecting people.

activities.explanation: This is right because early warnings help the government save people.

activities.prompt: Scientists study cyclones to protect lives and resources. Which work should they do next?
options: Plan ways to protect lives and resources when cyclones arrive.
Wait until after cyclones have caused harm before making plans.
Study only calm weather and ignore information about cyclones.
Stop studying once coastal regions receive cyclone awards.

why.Wait until after cyclones have caused ha: This mistake waits until people and resources are already harmed.
why.Study only calm weather and ignore infor: This mistake ignores important information about cyclones.
why.Stop studying once coastal regions recei: This mistake thinks awards remove the need to study cyclones.

activities.explanation: This is right because their work should protect lives and resources.

lessons.title: In the Mountains, with Nayan

activities.prompt: What would you like to discover about life in the mountains?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Mountain Life
activities.body: Mountains are rocky landforms that rise high above the ground. They are usually cold, and many Himalayan mountains are covered in snow. Steep slopes and surrounding valleys often shape mountain land. Sikkim lies in the Himalayan mountains. Warm thukpa, soft sel roti and traditional clothes are special features. Yaks are used for travel. Loosong and Namsoong marks the start of the Sikkimese New Year.
keyPoints: Mountains rise high above the ground.
Sikkim lies in the Himalayan mountains.
The Sikkimese New Year begins with an important festival.
activities.explanation: This lesson connects mountains with special features of Sikkim.

activities.prompt: Nayan visits Sikkim near New Year. What can he expect and use?
steps: Sikkim lies in the Himalayan mountains, and many are covered in snow.
Mountains are usually cold, so Nayan should wear warm clothes.
It marks the Sikkimese New Year, so Nayan may see the festival.
A yak can help him travel because yaks are commonly used there.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where does Sikkim lie?
options: Himalayan mountains
steep slopes
surrounding valleys
cold places
activities.explanation: Sikkim lies in the Himalayan mountains.

activities.prompt: Mountains often have steep ______ and surrounding valleys.
activities.hint: Find the description of a mountain's shape.
activities.explanation: Mountains often have steep slopes and surrounding valleys.

activities.prompt: Many Himalayan mountains are covered in snow.
activities.explanation: Many Himalayan mountains are covered in snow.

activities.prompt: How did the air feel in Gangtok?
options: clean and refreshing
hot and dusty
warm and oily
cold and smoky
activities.explanation: The weather was cool, and the air felt clean and refreshing.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with its description.
activities.explanation: Thukpa is warm and sel roti is sweet and soft. Yaks are used for travel.

activities.prompt: Which set lists trees found in Sikkim?
options: Oak, pine, walnut, thukpa
Oak, pine, walnut, yak
Oak, pine, walnut, bakhu
Oak, pine, walnut, chestnut
activities.explanation: These four trees—oak, pine, walnut and chestnut—are found in Sikkim.

activities.prompt: Mountains are usually cold. Nayan is packing for Sikkim. Which item is most useful?
options: A warm jacket for the cold weather.
A light shirt for the hot weather.
A sleeveless top for the cool weather.
A summer cap for the snowy weather.

This wrongly thinks mountain weather will be hot.
A sleeveless top does not give enough warmth in cold weather.
Snowy weather needs warmth, but a summer cap does not provide it.

activities.explanation: Mountains are usually cold, so a warm jacket is useful.

activities.prompt: Yaks are commonly used for travel in Sikkim. Nayan must cross the mountains. What should he use?
options: A yak to help carry him there.
Thukpa to help carry him there.
An oak tree to help carry him there.
A steep slope to help carry him there.

Thukpa is warm food, but it cannot carry him.
Oak trees grow in Sikkim, but they do not carry people.
Steep slopes are part of mountains, but they do not carry people.

activities.explanation: Yaks are commonly used for travel in Sikkim's mountains.

activities.prompt: Gangtok's weather was cool. Nayan wants a warm meal in Sikkim. Which food should he choose?
options: Warm thukpa from Sikkimese food.
Warm sel roti from Sikkimese food.
Cool thukpa from Sikkimese food.
Sweet sel roti from Sikkimese food.

Sel roti is sweet and soft, but it is not called warm.
Sweet does not mean warm, so this does not meet his warm-meal need.

activities.explanation: Thukpa is warm and is part of Sikkimese food.

activities.prompt: Bakhu, dumdyam and Gunyo cholo are Sikkimese clothes. Nayan says every Himalayan person wears them. What is wrong?
options: These clothes are for Sikkim, not every Himalayan person.
These clothes are for every valley, not only mountains.
These clothes are for Gangtok, not all Himalayan people.
These clothes are for all people in every country.

why.These clothes are for every valley, not: The fact does not say that everyone in Himalayan valleys wears them.
why.These clothes are for Gangtok, not all H: The fact names Sikkim, not Gangtok, as the place.
why.These clothes are for all people in ever: It gives Sikkimese clothes, not clothes for people everywhere.

activities.explanation: The fact names the people of Sikkim, not all Himalayan people.

activities.prompt: Many Himalayan mountains are covered in snow. Nayan says every mountain has snow. Why is his claim too strong?
options: Many have snow, but we cannot say every one does.
Many have snow, so every one must have snow.
One snowy mountain means all mountains have snow.
Snowy valleys prove every mountain has snow.

why.Many have snow, so every one must have s: This wrongly treats many as if it means every mountain.
why.One snowy mountain means all mountains h: One snowy mountain cannot prove that all mountains are snowy.
why.Snowy valleys prove every mountain has s: The fact is about mountains and does not use valleys to prove it.

activities.explanation: The fact says many Himalayan mountains have snow, not every one.

activities.context: After the holidays, children at school talked excitedly about the holidays they had spent. Colourful pictures and other items from their visits filled the desks. The teacher invited the children to share their holiday experiences. Chandni told the class about visiting a beach in Odisha. Ritika spoke about Rajasthan's desert, Gurpreet shared stories about visiting his grandparents in Amritsar, and Nayan described the majestic mountains of Sikkim.
activities.prompt: After Chandni shares about the beach in Odisha, which action best continues the teacher's invitation and the chapter's main idea?
options: Ask another child to share how a different natural setup shapes how people live.
Ask Chandni to describe the same beach visit again as the only example.
Tell the class that every place has the same natural setup.
End the sharing because one natural setup is enough.

why.Ask Chandni to describe the same beach v: Repeating one story would not show different places.
why.Tell the class that every place has the: The chapter introduces several different natural setups.
why.End the sharing because one natural setu: One child's story does not cover the whole chapter.

activities.explanation: This continues sharing and connects natural setups with life.

activities.context: After the holidays, children at school talked excitedly about the holidays they had spent. Colourful pictures and other items from their visits filled the desks. The teacher invited the children to share their holiday experiences. Chandni told the class about visiting a beach in Odisha. Ritika spoke about Rajasthan's desert, Gurpreet shared stories about visiting his grandparents in Amritsar, and Nayan described the majestic mountains of Sikkim.
activities.prompt: Nayan wants to apply the lesson's idea to his visit to the mountains of Sikkim. Which statement fits best?
options: The mountain surroundings can influence how people live in that place.
The mountains alone explain every choice made by people everywhere.
The natural setup matters only for how the mountains look, not for how people live.
A place's natural setup affects life only when it is a mountain.

why.The mountains alone explain every choice: This makes an unnecessarily broad claim.
why.The natural setup matters only for how t: The lesson says natural setup helps shape how people live.
why.A place's natural setup affects life onl: The lesson includes plains, deserts, coastal regions and mountains.

activities.explanation: This connects the natural setup with how people live.

activities.prompt: Explain why the natural setup of a place helps shape how people live.
activities.answer: A place's natural setup forms part of the surroundings in which people live. The lesson introduces plains, deserts, coastal regions and mountains. Different natural settings can influence how people live, and nature and culture are closely connected.
points: Natural setup is connected with how people live.
The chapter introduces several different natural setups.
Different settings can influence people's lives.
Nature and culture are closely connected.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: In the plains of Amritsar, Gurpreet sees large fields where many people work in farming. The soil is rich and fertile. The people of Amritsar like makki di roti and sarson da saag. Makki di roti is made with corn flour, while sarson da saag uses mustard leaves. Later, Gurpreet visits the Golden Temple, also called Sri Harmandir Sahib. A serene water tank surrounds its gold-plated structure. At langar sewa, volunteers cook, serve meals and wash dishes.
activities.prompt: Gurpreet wants to explain how the two popular foods are made. Which explanation matches the case?
options: Makki di roti uses corn flour, and sarson da saag uses mustard leaves.
Makki di roti uses mustard leaves, and sarson da saag uses corn flour.
Both dishes use corn flour.
Both dishes use mustard leaves.

It gives both dishes the ingredient used only for makki di roti in the case.
It gives both dishes the ingredient used only for sarson da saag in the case.

activities.explanation: Corn flour is used for makki di roti, while mustard leaves are used for sarson da saag.

activities.context: In the plains of Amritsar, Gurpreet sees large fields where many people work in farming. The soil is rich and fertile. The people of Amritsar like makki di roti and sarson da saag. Makki di roti is made with corn flour, while sarson da saag uses mustard leaves. Later, Gurpreet visits the Golden Temple, also called Sri Harmandir Sahib. A serene water tank surrounds its gold-plated structure. At langar sewa, volunteers cook, serve meals and wash dishes.
activities.prompt: Gurpreet sees many people in the plains of Amritsar working in farming and asks why. Which evidence from the case best explains this?
options: The plains have large fields with rich, fertile soil.
The Golden Temple is surrounded by a serene water tank.
The Golden Temple has a gold-plated structure.
The people of Amritsar like makki di roti and sarson da saag.

why.The Golden Temple is surrounded by a ser: The water tank surrounds the Golden Temple, not the farming fields.
why.The Golden Temple has a gold-plated stru: The gold-plated structure belongs to the Golden Temple and does not explain farming.
why.The people of Amritsar like makki di rot: Liking these foods does not directly explain why many people work in farming.

activities.explanation: Large fields and rich, fertile soil directly explain why many people work in farming there.

activities.prompt: Explain why many people in the plains of Amritsar work in farming.
activities.answer: Large fields in the plains of Amritsar provide space for farming. The soil there is rich and fertile, so it can support farming work. These two features help explain why many people in the region work in farming.
points: Mentions the large fields in the plains of Amritsar.
Explains that the soil is rich and fertile.
Connects these features to the work done by many people.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: How do cactus, khejri and babool survive in a desert?
activities.answer: Cactus, khejri and babool can grow in deserts, where rainfall is very little. Desert plants are able to survive with very little water. In particular, a cactus stores water in its stem, which helps it live during dry conditions.
points: Deserts have very little rainfall.
Cactus, khejri and babool grow in deserts.
Desert plants survive with very little water.
Cactus stores water in its stem.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: During Chandni’s visit to Puri, a coastal city in Odisha, she walked on the amazing sandy beaches. Artists were creating beautiful sand art, and Chandni looked for different kinds of sea shells. During a boat ride, she saw fishermen riding in boats in the sea and spotted turtles and other wonderful creatures. She also learned that many people in coastal regions depend on fishing for their living.
activities.prompt: If the fishermen in Chandni’s case stopped going out to fish, what might happen next in coastal regions?
options: People who depend on fishing might need another way to earn their living.
Artists might create more sand pictures to replace the lost fishing work.
More turtles might come ashore because fishing has stopped.
More sea shells might be found on the beaches because fishing has stopped.

why.Artists might create more sand pictures: Artists already create sand art, but the passage does not link their work to fishing.
why.More turtles might come ashore because f: The passage does not say that fishing affects how many turtles come ashore.
why.More sea shells might be found on the be: The passage does not say that fishermen collect or remove sea shells.

activities.explanation: This follows because many coastal people depend on fishing for their living.

activities.prompt: How does fishing support the lives of people in coastal regions, and why might stopping fishing cause a problem?
activities.answer: Many people in coastal regions depend on fishing for their living. If fishing stopped, those people might lose the work that supports them. They would need another way to earn a living, although the passage does not name another way.
points: Explains that many people depend on fishing.
Uses “for their living” to show how fishing supports them.
Explains that stopping fishing could create a livelihood problem.
Does not invent a replacement source of income.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: People in coastal regions of Odisha often face strong winds and cyclones. Cyclones can harm people, animals and trees, and they occur in coastal states from time to time. People study cyclones to find ways to protect lives and resources, while scientists and other people work to protect them during cyclones. After an early warning reaches the Government of Odisha, it can make advance preparations and use effective management. The Government has received awards for saving people during cyclones.
activities.prompt: An early warning has reached the Government of Odisha. What should it do next to protect lives and resources?
options: Make advance preparations and use effective management
Wait until after the cyclone before making preparations
Study cyclones only after the danger has passed
Stop preparations because the early warning means everyone is safe

why.Wait until after the cyclone before maki: Waiting until after the cyclone misses the chance to prepare in advance.
why.Study cyclones only after the danger has: Studying only after the danger has passed does not help people find protection ways.
why.Stop preparations because the early warn: An early warning helps the Government act; it does not guarantee everyone is safe.

activities.explanation: Correct: advance preparations and effective management help during cyclones.

activities.context: People in coastal regions of Odisha often face strong winds and cyclones. Cyclones can harm people, animals and trees, and they occur in coastal states from time to time. People study cyclones to find ways to protect lives and resources, while scientists and other people work to protect them during cyclones. After an early warning reaches the Government of Odisha, it can make advance preparations and use effective management. The Government has received awards for saving people during cyclones.
activities.prompt: If the Government of Odisha did not receive early warnings, what change would most directly follow?
options: The Government would have less help saving people during cyclones.
Strong winds would no longer affect coastal regions.
Cyclones would stop occurring in coastal states.
Scientists and other people could no longer study cyclones.

why.Strong winds would no longer affect coas: Receiving fewer warnings does not change the strong winds that hit coastal regions.
why.Cyclones would stop occurring in coastal: A lack of warnings does not stop cyclones from occurring.
why.Scientists and other people could no lon: Warnings are not the only reason people study cyclones.

activities.explanation: Correct: early warnings help the Government save people during cyclones.

activities.prompt: Explain why studying cyclones is important for protecting lives and resources.
activities.answer: Studying cyclones helps people find ways to protect lives and resources. Scientists and other people can use what they learn to work during cyclones. Early warnings, advance preparations, and effective management all help the Government of Odisha save people and protect resources when strong winds and cyclones hit coastal regions.
points: Cyclones are studied to find protection methods.
Scientists and other people help during cyclones.
Early warnings support Government action.
Preparations and management protect lives and resources.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Nayan picks a warm soup and a soft, sweet bread. Which matching of the dishes is correct?
options: Thukpa provides warmth, while sel roti has the sweet, soft qualities.
Sel roti provides warmth, while thukpa has the sweet, soft qualities.
Both dishes provide warmth and have sweet, soft qualities.
Neither dish is warm, sweet or soft.

why.Sel roti provides warmth, while thukpa h: The qualities of the two dishes have been swapped.
why.Both dishes provide warmth and have swee: Only thukpa is described as warm; sel roti is described as sweet and soft.
Both dishes are described as warm, sweet and soft.

activities.context: Nayan is visiting Sikkim. The weather in Gangtok is cool, and the air feels clean and refreshing. Mountains rise high above the ground, often with steep slopes and surrounding valleys. Many Himalayan mountains are covered in snow. activities.prompt: After seeing snow-covered Himalayan mountains in Sikkim, Nayan visits mountains in another part of the country. What can he reasonably expect?

He can expect oak, pine, walnut and chestnut trees in every mountain area.

why.He must see the same Himalayan snow beca: Many, not all, Himalayan mountains are covered in snow.
why.He can expect warm mountains because onl: Mountains are usually cold, regardless of the example from Sikkim.
why.He can expect oak, pine, walnut and ches: Those trees are stated to be found in Sikkim, not in every mountain area.

activities.explanation: This matches the description and usual climate of mountains.

activities.prompt: How does Loosong and Namsoong connect with the beginning of the Sikkimese New Year?

points: Loosong and Namsoong is an important festival.
The festival marks the start of the Sikkimese New Year.
It is connected with the beginning of the new year for the people of Sikkim.

chapters.title: Our Sky
chapters.summary: In this chapter: our changing sky; the sun’s journey; the shadows; shadow experiments and sundials.

lessons.title: Our Changing Sky

activities.prompt: What makes our sky look different from morning to night?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Sky That Changes
activities.body: The sky looks different at different times of the day. Its colour changes during the morning, afternoon and night. The Sun’s colour also seems to change. The Moon’s size and shape seem to change over time. Birds, animals, trees and humans have different activities during the day. You can observe the sky and share your observations with classmates.
keyPoints: The sky changes colour during the day.
The Sun and Moon seem to change.
Living things have different daily activities.
activities.explanation: Start by noticing changes in the sky and in daily life.

activities.prompt: You observe the sky at two times. Why might it look different?
steps: Observe the sky in the morning and afternoon.
Compare the colour because it changes during the day.
Record each time because the sky changes by time.
Conclude that different times can make the sky look different.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which colour appears in the example morning sky?
options: orange
blue
green
grey
activities.explanation: The example morning observation shows an orange sky.

activities.prompt: The sky keeps the same colour all day.
activities.explanation: The sky looks different at different times, and its colour changes.

activities.prompt: During the morning, afternoon and night, the colour of the sky ______.
activities.hint: Think about the colours you see at each time.
activities.explanation: The sky’s colour changes during the morning, afternoon and night.

activities.prompt: Which statement about animals and plants is correct?
options: Their behaviour may change.
Their behaviour never changes.
Their behaviour stays the same.
Their behaviour changes yearly.
activities.explanation: Animal and plant behaviour may change at different times of the day.

activities.prompt: Match each clue with the correct detail.
activities.explanation: These pairs use the sky example, daily activities and sky sharing.

activities.prompt: Put these times in the order you should observe the sky.
activities.explanation: The lesson asks you to observe the sky in the morning, afternoon and at night.

activities.prompt: Sharing your sky observations lets you compare them with classmates.
activities.explanation: You can share your sky observations with classmates and compare them.

activities.prompt: Which change can seem to happen to the Moon over time?
options: Its size and shape
Its size and speed
Its colour and sound
Its name and age
activities.explanation: The Moon’s size and shape seem to change over time.

activities.prompt: The Sun’s colour seems to change. Which observation best shows this?
options: You notice a different Sun colour at another time.
You notice a different sky colour at another time.
You notice a different Moon shape at another time.
You notice birds doing different things at another time.

why.You notice a different sky colour at ano: Wrong: a sky change does not show a Sun colour change.
why.You notice a different Moon shape at ano: Wrong: a Moon shape change does not show a Sun colour change.
why.You notice birds doing different things: Wrong: bird activity does not show a Sun colour change.

activities.explanation: Right: the Sun’s colour is the feature observed changing.

activities.prompt: Birds’ activities vary during the day. Which plan is the fairest test?
options: Watch birds during morning and again in afternoon.
Watch birds only once during the morning.
Ask friends what birds usually eat each day.
Observe tree leaves after lunch each day.

why.Watch birds only once during the morning: Wrong: one morning watch cannot compare different times.
why.Ask friends what birds usually eat each: Wrong: what birds eat does not test changes in daily activity.
why.Observe tree leaves after lunch each day: Wrong: tree leaves are not the behaviour being compared.

activities.explanation: Right: watching at two times makes the behaviour comparison fair.

lessons.title: The Sun’s Journey

activities.prompt: Why does the Sun seem to move across the sky?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Following the Sun
activities.body: The Sun is the brightest and most visible object in the sky. It gives us light and heat. In the morning, the Sun appears to rise. It seems to move upwards and comes overhead. Later, it appears to move downwards towards the other side of the sky. Eventually, it disappears from view. We all enjoy watching this visible journey.
keyPoints: The Sun gives us light and heat.
The Sun appears to rise in the morning.
The Sun’s visible journey ends when it disappears from view.
activities.explanation: The Sun’s visible journey moves from a morning rise to disappearing from view.

activities.prompt: A child watches the Sun from when it appears until it disappears. What journey does the child see?
steps: In the morning, the Sun appears to rise, so the journey begins.
It seems to move upwards and comes overhead, showing the middle part.
It appears to move downwards towards the other side, so the journey continues.
Finally, it disappears from view, so the child sees a full visible journey.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Gifts from the Sun
activities.prompt: What does the Sun give us?
options: Light and heat
Light and rain
Air and heat
Wind and clouds
activities.explanation: The lesson says that the Sun gives us light and heat.

activities.title: Above Us
activities.prompt: The Sun comes ______ during its visible journey.
activities.hint: This means it is above you.
activities.explanation: The Sun comes overhead as it seems to move across the sky.

activities.title: Complete the Sentences
activities.prompt: Match each beginning with its ending.
pairs: The visible journey of the Sun
activities.explanation: Each pair completes a fact about the Sun and its visible journey.

activities.title: After the Sunrise
activities.prompt: What does the Sun seem to do after it appears to rise?
options: Move upwards
Move downwards
Stay in one place
Disappear at once
activities.explanation: After appearing to rise, the Sun seems to move upwards.

activities.title: The Sun’s Journey
activities.prompt: Put these stages of the Sun’s visible journey in order.
items: The Sun seems to move upwards
The Sun appears to move downwards
activities.explanation: The Sun moves towards the other side before eventually disappearing from view.

activities.title: The Whole Journey
activities.prompt: Which sentence matches the Sun’s visible journey?
options: It rises, moves downwards, then comes overhead.
It stays overhead, then moves upwards.
It disappears, then rises and stays still.
It rises, comes overhead, then moves downwards.
activities.explanation: The Sun rises, comes overhead, then moves downwards before disappearing from view.

activities.prompt: The Sun appears to rise in the morning. What happens next?
options: The Sun will seem to move upwards and come overhead.
The Sun will move towards the other side at once.
The Sun will disappear before it ever comes overhead.
The Sun will stay in the same place all day.

why.The Sun will move towards the other side: This wrongly treats the other side as the immediate next step.
why.The Sun will disappear before it ever co: This wrongly makes disappearance happen before the Sun comes overhead.
why.The Sun will stay in the same place all: This wrongly imagines that the Sun never changes position.

activities.explanation: This is right because upward movement and overhead come next.

activities.prompt: The Sun seems to move upwards. Why does this show part of a journey?
options: Its visible position changes higher in the sky.
Its brightness changes instead of its position.
It gives us light and heat while moving.
It is more visible than other sky objects.

why.Its brightness changes instead of its po: This wrongly thinks brightness changes prove the journey.
This wrongly thinks light and heat explain the position change.
why.It is more visible than other sky object: This wrongly uses being visible to explain the position change.

activities.explanation: This is right because a changing visible position shows movement.

activities.prompt: The Sun appears in the morning and later disappears. A child wants to watch its full visible journey. Which plan is fairest?
options: Watch from its morning appearance until it disappears.
Watch only after the Sun has completely disappeared.
Watch only one moment before the Sun appears.
Watch only while the Sun is directly overhead.

why.Watch only after the Sun has completely: This starts too late to see the journey begin.
why.Watch only one moment before the Sun app: This misses the journey because the Sun is not yet visible.
why.Watch only while the Sun is directly ove: This sees only the middle and misses the beginning and end.

activities.explanation: This is right because it covers the whole visible journey.

activities.prompt: Someone says, 'The Sun has no journey because it stays in one place.' Which observation shows this claim is wrong?
options: The Sun appears to rise and then move upwards.
The Sun is the brightest object in the sky.
The Sun also gives us light and heat.
The Sun is the most visible object in the sky.

why.The Sun is the brightest object in the s: This confuses brightness with a change in position.
This confuses light and heat with a change in position.
why.The Sun is the most visible object in th: This confuses being visible with a change in position.

activities.explanation: This is right because it shows that the Sun's visible position changes.

activities.prompt: The Sun is moving towards the other side of the sky. What does the journey show next?
options: The Sun will eventually disappear from view.
The Sun will seem to move upwards.
The Sun will come overhead at that same moment.
The Sun will give us light and heat.

This wrongly returns to the earlier upward stage.
why.The Sun will come overhead at that same: This wrongly puts overhead after the other side of the sky.
This wrongly treats light and heat as the next visible step.

activities.explanation: This is right because disappearance follows movement towards the other side.

activities.prompt: The Sun seems to move upwards and comes overhead. A child says its journey stops there. What observation corrects this mistake?
options: It appears to move downwards towards the other side.
It seems to move upwards and then stops.
It comes overhead and never moves again.
It disappears as soon as it appears.

This repeats the mistake that upward movement ends the journey.
This wrongly thinks overhead is the final stage.
This wrongly makes disappearance happen at the very beginning.

activities.explanation: This is right because it shows the downward part that the child missed.

lessons.sceneCaption: The Sun begins its morning journey above the horizon at Triund Base Camp.

lessons.title: The Shadows

activities.prompt: Why does your shadow change shape and length throughout the day?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How Your Shadow Changes
activities.body: Your shadow moves with you. When you run, it seems to run too. Different poses change the shape of your shadow. Morning shadows are long. Noon shadows are short. Evening shadows are long again. Evening shadows point in the opposite direction from morning shadows. The lesson asks how your shadow changes. It wonders why these changes happen. It asks whether all objects change and whether shadows form only in sunlight.
keyPoints: Your shadow moves and changes shape with you.
Morning and evening shadows are long, but noon shadows are short.
Evening shadows point opposite to morning shadows.
activities.explanation: Look for movement, new shapes, changing lengths and opposite directions.

activities.title: Make a shadow

tasks.say: Make the shadow as big as you can.
tasks.then: Closest to the lamp, the object blocks the most light.

activities.takeaway: Light travels in straight lines, so an object blocks a patch of it; nearer the lamp, it blocks more.
activities.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, so an object blocks a patch of it; nearer the lamp, it blocks more.

activities.prompt: Your shadow looks different in the morning, noon, and evening. Why?
steps: Morning shadows are long, so your morning shadow looks long.
Noon shadows are short, so your shadow looks shorter at noon.
Evening shadows are long again, so your shadow becomes long.
Evening shadows point opposite to morning ones, so yours does too.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What happens when you run?
options: It seems to run.
It stays very still.
It turns much shorter.
It points both ways.
activities.explanation: When you run, your shadow seems to run with you.

activities.prompt: At ______, your shadow is short.
activities.hint: Choose the time with short shadows.
activities.explanation: Noon shadows are short.

activities.prompt: Match each clue with the correct shadow fact.
pairs: The shadow seems to run too
activities.explanation: Each pair shows movement, shape or shadow length in the lesson.

activities.prompt: How do evening shadows point compared with morning shadows?
options: In the opposite direction
In the same direction
They do not point
activities.explanation: Evening shadows point in the opposite direction to morning shadows.

activities.prompt: Put these times in the correct order.
activities.explanation: The order is morning, noon, then evening. The shadow lengths are long, short, long.

activities.prompt: Which question does the chapter ask?
options: Do shadows form only in sunlight?
Do shadows change your colour every day?
Do shadows make you run faster than your friends?
Do shadows stay still whenever you move?
activities.explanation: The chapter asks whether shadows form only in sunlight.

activities.prompt: You want to learn how your shadow changes. What should you do?
options: Change your pose and watch the shadow's shape.
Stand very still and look only once.
Run around and watch only where it points.
Close your eyes and guess its new shape.

One look cannot show how the shadow's shape changes.
why.Run around and watch only where it point: Watching direction alone misses the change caused by a pose.
Guessing cannot show what your shadow really does.

activities.explanation: Different poses change the shape, so watching shows the change.

activities.prompt: At noon, how does your shadow compare with your morning shadow?
options: It is shorter than the morning shadow.
It is longer than the morning shadow.
It has the same length as morning.
It points the same way as morning.

This mistake reverses the long morning and short noon facts.
This mistake treats long and short shadows as equal.
This mistake confuses shadow length with pointing direction.

activities.explanation: Morning shadows are long, but noon shadows are short.

activities.prompt: In the evening, how does your shadow compare with your morning shadow?
options: It is long and points the opposite way.
It is short and points the same way.
It is long and points the same way.
It is short and points the opposite way.

This mistake makes the evening shadow short and keeps the same direction.
This mistake gets the long length right but mixes up the direction.
This mistake gets the opposite direction right but makes the shadow short.

activities.explanation: Evening shadows are long and point opposite to morning shadows.

activities.prompt: The class asks about objects, your shadow, sunlight, and causes. Which plan is best?
options: Watch your shadow and others, changing one thing at a time.
Watch one shadow once and guess about every object.
Change many things together and make no comparisons.
Guess the causes without changing or watching anything.

why.Watch one shadow once and guess about ev: One look cannot show how shadows change for many objects.
why.Change many things together and make no: Changing many things together hides the cause of each change.
why.Guess the causes without changing or wat: Guessing gives no observations to explain shadow changes.

activities.explanation: Changing one thing at a time makes each shadow change easier to understand.

lessons.sceneCaption: Low morning sunlight creates long shadows along a busy roadside.

lessons.title: Shadow Experiments and Sundials

activities.prompt: How can shadows help us tell the time?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Shadows and Time
activities.body: Explore how light makes shadows in a dark room. Use a torch and stick. Point torchlight at the stick, then move it back and forth. Watch the shadow change. An object closer to the light makes a bigger shadow. Changing the light's direction changes the shadow's direction. The Sun seems to move east to overhead, then west. Shadows show time, and Samrat Yantra is a sundial that tells time accurately.
keyPoints: A torch and stick help you explore shadows.
The Sun's movement changes the shadow's direction.
Shadows can show the time.
activities.explanation: Light, moving objects and the Sun all help us learn about shadows.

activities.title: Make a shadow

tasks.say: Make the shadow as big as you can.
tasks.then: Closest to the lamp, the object blocks the most light.

activities.takeaway: Light travels in straight lines, so an object blocks a patch of it; nearer the lamp, it blocks more.
activities.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, so an object blocks a patch of it; nearer the lamp, it blocks more.

activities.prompt: A child watches a shadow during the day and wants to know the time.
steps: The Sun appears to move from East to overhead till noon, then toward West in the afternoon.
Because the Sun moves, the shadow changes direction.
These changing shadows can help the child find the time.
For accurate time, the child can use Samrat Yantra because it is a sundial that tells time accurately.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Explore Shadows
activities.prompt: What can you use to explore shadows in a dark room?
options: the Sun and a shadow
a torch and a stick
the east and the west
a sundial and noon
activities.explanation: A torch and stick help you explore shadows in a dark room.

activities.title: Point the Torchlight
activities.prompt: Point the torchlight at the ______.
activities.hint: It is the object you move during the experiment.
activities.explanation: Point the torchlight at the stick to begin the shadow experiment.

activities.title: Actions and Results
activities.prompt: Match each action with its result.
pairs: Move the stick back and forth
activities.explanation: Each action makes a clear change to the light or shadow.

activities.title: Why Shadows Turn
activities.prompt: Why does a shadow change direction during the day?
options: because the stick changes colour
because the shadow becomes bigger
because the Sun moves
because the torch moves
activities.explanation: The shadow changes direction because the Sun moves.

activities.title: The Sun's Journey
activities.prompt: Put the Sun's apparent positions in order.
activities.explanation: The Sun appears to move from east to overhead, then towards west.

activities.title: Tell the Time
activities.prompt: Which sundial can tell time accurately?
options: a torch
a stick
Samrat Yantra
a shadow
activities.explanation: Samrat Yantra is a sundial that can tell time accurately.

activities.prompt: A torch shines on a stick. The stick is moved close to the torch. What happens to its shadow?
options: It becomes bigger because the stick is closer to the light.
It becomes smaller because the stick is closer to the light.
It stays the same because the stick is closer to the light.
It becomes bigger because the stick is farther from the light.

why.It becomes smaller because the stick is: This confuses closeness with the bigger shadow made by a close object.
why.It stays the same because the stick is c: This wrongly believes that closeness does not change the shadow.
why.It becomes bigger because the stick is f: This confuses being farther away with being close to the light.

activities.explanation: This is right because an object close to the light makes a bigger shadow.

activities.prompt: The torchlight shines on a stick. The direction of the light is changed. What happens to the shadow?
options: The shadow changes direction because the light changed.
The shadow changes size because the light changed.
The shadow stays still because the light changed.
The shadow moves nearer because the light changed.

why.The shadow changes size because the ligh: This confuses a change in light direction with a change in shadow size.
why.The shadow stays still because the light: This wrongly believes that the shadow cannot change when the light changes.
why.The shadow moves nearer because the ligh: This confuses the shadow's direction with its distance from the light.

activities.explanation: This is right because changing the light direction changes the shadow direction.

activities.prompt: The Sun moves from East to overhead, then toward West. Why does a stick's shadow change direction?
options: Because the Sun moves during the day.
Because the stick moves during the day.
Because the torch moves during the day.
Because the shadow moves during the day.

This puts the cause on the stick, but the Sun is moving.
This puts the cause on the torch, but the Sun is moving.
This puts the cause on the shadow, but the Sun is moving.

activities.explanation: This is right because the shadow changes direction when the Sun moves.

lessons.sceneAlt: An equatorial sundial uses the shadow of sunlight to indicate the time.
lessons.sceneCaption: This equatorial sundial tells time by indicating it with the shadow cast by sunlight.

sceneCredit.text: Equatorial Sundial by Aliva Sahoo, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
sceneCredit.creator: Aliva Sahoo

lessons.title: Shadow Play and the Night Sky

activities.prompt: How do shadows and the Moon change what we see in the sky?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Looking at the Night Sky
activities.body: Shadow puppetry is performing with puppets that make shadows. It has been practised in India for a long time. After sunset, the sky dazzles with thousands of twinkling stars. You can observe different star patterns. The Moon appears to be the biggest object at night. Its shape looks different on different nights. A complete circle is Poornima or full Moon. An invisible Moon is Amavasya or new Moon.
keyPoints: Shadow puppetry is an old performing art in India.
Thousands of stars twinkle after sunset.
Poornima is the full Moon; Amavasya is the new Moon.
activities.explanation: Explore shadows, stars, and changing Moon shapes.

activities.title: Watch the Moon change shape

tasks.say: Make the full Moon, called Purnima.
tasks.then: At the full Moon the lit half faces us: a complete bright circle, nearly opposite the Sun.

tasks.say: Make the new Moon, called Amavasya, when no Moon is seen.
tasks.then: At the new Moon the lit half faces away from us, so we cannot see the Moon at all.

tasks.say: Stop at the first quarter: about half lit and growing.
tasks.then: One week after the new Moon we see a half circle, and the bright part is still growing: Shukla Paksha.

tasks.say: Find the last quarter: half lit and shrinking.
tasks.then: One week after the full Moon we see a half circle again, and the bright part is shrinking: Krishna Paksha.

activities.takeaway: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon goes round the Earth we see more or less of that lit half, so it grows from new Moon to full Moon and shrinks back to new Moon.
activities.explanation: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon goes round the Earth we see more or less of that lit half, so it grows from new Moon to full Moon and shrinks back to new Moon.

activities.prompt: Why can the Moon look different on different nights?
steps: A complete circle is Poornima, so it is one possible Moon shape.
An unseen new Moon is Amavasya, so the Moon can be invisible.
Because these shapes differ, the Moon's visible shape can change.
Thus, the Moon may look complete, cut down the middle, or unseen.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What does the sky do after sunset?
options: It hides all the stars.
It dazzles with twinkling stars.
It fills with bright daylight.
It shows only the Moon.
activities.explanation: After sunset, thousands of stars begin to twinkle.

activities.prompt: The complete circle is called ______ or the full Moon.
activities.hint: Use the Indian name for the full Moon.
activities.explanation: Poornima means the full Moon. This is the complete-circle shape.

activities.prompt: Match each Moon description with its name or meaning.
activities.explanation: A complete circle is the full Moon. An invisible Moon is Amavasya. A cut-down Moon looks like half.

activities.prompt: What can you observe in the night sky?
options: Patterns of toy trains
Patterns of busy markets
Patterns of twinkling stars
Patterns of paper boats
activities.explanation: You can observe different patterns of stars in the night sky.

activities.prompt: The Moon looks cut down the ______ on some nights.
activities.hint: Think of the line across a shape.
activities.explanation: On some nights, the Moon looks cut down the middle.

activities.prompt: Which statement about the Moon is correct?
options: It appears to be the biggest object at night.
It looks like a full circle on every night.
It can always be seen in the night sky.
It keeps the same shape on every night.
activities.explanation: The Moon appears to be the biggest object in the night sky.

activities.prompt: After sunset, a child wants to compare star patterns on two nights. What should the child do?
options: Look after sunset and record the patterns each time.
Watch the Moon only and ignore the stars.
Use one night's stars for the whole comparison.
Count shadow puppets instead of looking at stars.

why.Watch the Moon only and ignore the stars: This studies the Moon instead of comparing star patterns.
why.Use one night's stars for the whole comp: One night cannot show changes between nights.
why.Count shadow puppets instead of looking: This counts shadows instead of observing stars.

activities.explanation: This gives two fair observations after sunset.

activities.prompt: The Moon looks cut down the middle on one night. It looks complete another night. What can the child conclude?
options: The Moon's visible shape can change.
The Moon must always look complete.
The Moon must always be cut down the middle.
The Moon must stay visible in one shape.

why.The Moon must always be cut down the mid: This assumes the Moon is always cut down the middle.
This assumes one visible shape lasts every night.

activities.explanation: Poornima and the cut-middle shape show that the visible shape can change.

activities.prompt: The Moon cannot be seen on one night. What should the child expect on another night?
options: The Moon may be visible again.
The Moon must stay invisible every night.
The Moon must always be a complete circle.
The Moon must become a twinkling star.

why.The Moon must stay invisible every night: This mistakes one invisible night for every night.
why.The Moon must always be a complete circl: This assumes the Moon is always complete.
This confuses the Moon with a star.

activities.explanation: Amavasya is invisible, but the Moon can be seen on other nights.

activities.prompt: A child sees the Moon as a complete circle. What later sight shows a changed shape?
options: The Moon looks cut down the middle.
The Moon looks like the same complete circle.
The Moon cannot be seen at all.
The Moon looks like a twinkling star.

why.The Moon looks like the same complete ci: This shows the same shape, not a changed one.
An unseen Moon does not show a changed shape.
This confuses the Moon with a star.

activities.explanation: A cut-middle Moon is different from the complete circle.

lessons.title: Moon Festivals and Chandrayaan

activities.prompt: How do the Moon’s changing shapes connect our festivals and space exploration?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Moon in Our Lives
activities.body: The earliest calendars came from counting days with the Moon’s shape. Many festivals follow the Moon’s appearance. Diwali is celebrated when no Moon is in the sky. Eid is celebrated after a New Moon. The Moon is visible on that first night. The full round Moon is visible too. Chandrayaan’s Vikram Lander landed on the Moon on 23 August 2023. It collected data about the Moon’s surface.
keyPoints: Early calendars counted days using the Moon’s shape.
Many festivals follow the Moon’s appearance.
Vikram Lander landed on 23 August 2023 and collected surface data.
activities.explanation: The Moon connects early calendars, festivals, and Chandrayaan’s Moon mission.

activities.title: Watch the Moon change shape

tasks.say: Make the full Moon, called Purnima.
tasks.then: At the full Moon the lit half faces us: a complete bright circle, nearly opposite the Sun.

tasks.say: Make the new Moon, called Amavasya, when no Moon is seen.
tasks.then: At the new Moon the lit half faces away from us, so we cannot see the Moon at all.

tasks.say: Stop at the first quarter: about half lit and growing.
tasks.then: One week after the new Moon we see a half circle, and the bright part is still growing: Shukla Paksha.

tasks.say: Find the last quarter: half lit and shrinking.
tasks.then: One week after the full Moon we see a half circle again, and the bright part is shrinking: Krishna Paksha.

activities.takeaway: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon goes round the Earth we see more or less of that lit half, so it grows from new Moon to full Moon and shrinks back to new Moon.
activities.explanation: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon goes round the Earth we see more or less of that lit half, so it grows from new Moon to full Moon and shrinks back to new Moon.

activities.prompt: A family looks up on a festival night. They see no Moon. Which festival can they be celebrating?
steps: Diwali is celebrated when no Moon is visible, so it matches this night.
Eid needs a visible Moon, so it does not match this night.
Therefore, the family can be celebrating Diwali because the sky has no Moon.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What did the earliest calendars count?
options: Days with the Moon’s shape
Nights with heavy rain
Shapes of clouds
Names of trees
activities.explanation: The earliest calendars came from counting days with the Moon’s shape.

activities.prompt: Match each Moon clue to its description.
pairs: First night after a New Moon
activities.explanation: Diwali has no Moon in the sky. Eid follows a New Moon. The full round Moon is visible.

activities.prompt: The Vikram Lander collected data about the Moon’s ______.
activities.hint: Choose the short word from the lesson.
activities.explanation: The lander collected data about the Moon’s surface.

activities.prompt: Which clue shows that Eid is celebrated when the Moon is visible?
options: Diwali has no Moon in the sky.
Eid follows the first night after a New Moon.
Chandrayaan collected Moon surface data.
Early calendars counted cloud names.
activities.explanation: Eid is celebrated on the first night after a New Moon, when the Moon is visible.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in the order they happened.
items: Vikram Lander landed on the Moon
The data described the Moon’s surface
activities.explanation: The lander landed first, then collected data about the Moon’s surface.

activities.prompt: Which answer uses both festival and mission clues correctly?
options: Moon’s appearance guides festivals; the lander collected Earth surface data.
Diwali has a full Moon; the lander collected Moon surface data.
Moon’s appearance guides festivals; the lander collected Moon surface data.
Diwali has a full Moon; the lander collected Earth surface data.
activities.explanation: Many festivals follow the Moon’s appearance. Vikram Lander collected data about the Moon’s surface.

activities.prompt: A family looks up at festival time. They see no Moon. Which festival fits?
options: Diwali, because no Moon is visible.
Eid, because no Moon is visible.
Diwali, because a full Moon is visible.
Eid, because a full Moon is visible.

This wrongly links Eid with a sky that has no Moon.
This wrongly links Diwali with a visible full Moon.
This wrongly links Eid with a visible full Moon.

activities.explanation: This is right because Diwali is celebrated without a Moon.

activities.prompt: An early group wants to count days. What should it watch?
options: The Moon's shape.
The Moon's surface data.
The date when the lander landed.
The first night after a New Moon.

This mixes early counting with data collected by the lander.
One landing date cannot help count many passing days.
This mixes early counting with the night of Eid.

activities.explanation: This is right because early calendars counted days using the Moon's shape.

activities.prompt: A full round Moon appears. A child says Diwali is today. What correction is best?
options: Diwali needs no Moon in the sky.
Eid needs no Moon in the sky.
Diwali needs the first New Moon night.
Eid must follow every full Moon.

This wrongly says Eid needs no visible Moon.
This wrongly links Diwali with the first night after a New Moon.
This wrongly says Eid follows every full Moon.

activities.explanation: This is right because Diwali is celebrated when no Moon is visible.
